title: Understanding traffic law enforcement perceptions of autonomous vehicles: Insights from Chinese cities with operational robotaxi fleets through hypothesis testing and machine learning
authors: Xu, Ningzhe; Zhao, Dan; Yu, Yang; Liu, Jun
venue: Transportation Research Part A: Policy and Practice
abstract: Autonomous vehicles (AVs) are expected to improve road safety by reducing human error, which accounts for over 90% of traffic incidents. However, AVs also present new challenges for traffic law enforcement, particularly in their interactions with officers and their ability to navigate emergency situations, such as safely passing law enforcement officers (LEOs). This study examines these challenges through a survey of 1522 traffic LEOs in Chinese cities with operational AV fleets. The survey focused on two critical perceptions: LEOs’ confidence in AVs’ ability to follow traffic commands and trust in AVs’ ability to safely pass LEOs. Results indicate that over 90% of LEOs lacked confidence in AVs’ ability to follow commands, and nearly 70% did not trust AVs to safely pass LEOs. Officers with direct experience managing AV-related incidents or riding in a robotaxi reported slightly higher confidence and trust levels, but overall perceptions were mixed. Chi-square tests and machine learning analyses further indicated that factors such as AV-related knowledge, procedural training, and attitudes toward robotaxis were significantly associated with these perceptions. These findings underscore the need for targeted training programs, increased exposure to AV technologies, and public engagement strategies to enhance law enforcement trust in AVs and their safe integration into traffic systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Modelling the performance of emerging last-mile modes in 90 European pedestrian zones
authors: Garus, Ada; Mourtzouchou, Andromachi; Mattas, Konstantinos; Ciuffo, Biagio
venue: Journal of Cleaner Production
abstract: This article compares the operational performance and sustainability of drones, autonomous delivery robots (ADRs), and electric cargo e-bikes through a simulation framework developed for pedestrian zones in 90 European cities. For each city, 200 parcels were assigned to evaluate mode-specific routing, energy use, cost, and service performance. Multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) was used to incorporate stakeholder perspectives. E-bikes combine the lowest energy demand with the low unit cost. ADRs offer the quietest, most space-efficient ground operation, halving drone energy use while matching bike cost, though their pedestrian speed lengthens service time. Drones deliver the shortest point-to-point travel time, 6–11 % quicker than bikes, but at higher externalities. Stakeholder-weighted MCDA scores average 0.83 for bikes, 0.61 for ADRs and 0.18 for drones, placing each mode first in one core attribute: overall sustainability (bike), low-impact night delivery (ADR) and urgent response (drone). The findings suggest policy mixes that fund cargo-bike infrastructure for routine flows, license ADR fleets for quiet off-peak distribution, and reserve drones for time-critical or topographically constrained drops. Such differentiated deployment can support decarbonisation, protect pedestrian comfort and maintain service quality in Europe's historic urban cores. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Causality-constrained hierarchical LLM agents for online rule adaptation in building HVAC control
authors: Xin, Weilin; Liang, Wei; Chong, Adrian
venue: Applied Energy
abstract: Adaptive multi-zone HVAC control often requires identifying a building-specific predictive model or training a policy through environment interaction. These requirements increase the effort needed to deploy adaptive controllers across buildings with different HVAC configurations. To address this challenge, we propose a causality-constrained hierarchical large language model (LLM) agent framework for online cooling-setpoint rule adaptation. The framework operates in two stages. Offline onboarding standardizes building management system (BMS) points and establishes a human-confirmed causal graph. During online rule adaptation, hierarchical agents propose hourly updates to rule-based controllers (RBCs), while the RBCs generate 15-min setpoints. Structural and causal checks, together with zone cooling allowances, determine whether each proposed update is incorporated into the RBC. We evaluate the framework in three BOPTEST cases with one, two, and five zones against basic and enhanced RBCs, hierarchical model predictive control, proximal policy optimization (PPO), and multi-agent PPO. The framework achieved the highest mean reward and the lowest mean energy use among the compared controllers in all three cases. Energy use was 2.2–43.2% lower than that of the baselines, accompanied by small accumulated PMV deviations of 0.0192–0.4542 PMV⋅h. The causal experiments showed that the complete causal layer reduced accumulated PMV deviation and safety interventions in every case, primarily by constraining and stabilizing rule adaptation. Further ablations quantified the effects of memory, cross-zone coordination, and LLM thinking on rule adaptation, control performance, and LLM inference overhead. Overall, the framework combines competitive energy and comfort performance with explicit, reviewable online rule adaptation, supporting its potential for adaptive multi-zone HVAC control across the evaluated HVAC configurations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: BudgetSRE: Budget-Aware Multi-Agent Incident Response for Backend Operations
authors: Yang, Qingfan; Feng, Guoze; Wang, Yihang; Chen, Jingyi; Luo, Zhiwei
venue: 2026 3rd International Conference on Image Processing, Multimedia Technology and Machine Learning, IPMML 2026
abstract: Modern cloud incident response increasingly relies on large language model (LLM) powered agents, yet operational deployments face a critical and often overlooked constraint: cost. Unconstrained agents can consume thousands of tokens and dozens of tool calls per incident, incurring non-trivial monetary and latency overhead while occasionally issuing unsafe remediation actions. We present BudgetSRE, a multi-agent framework that treats budget - tokens, tool calls, and action depth - as a first-class design parameter alongside response quality and safety. BudgetSRE comprises a lightweight Scout Agent for cheap triage, a Specialist Agent invoked only when diagnostic uncertainty is high, an Action Planner that orders remediations by risk-to-benefit ratio, and a Budget Controller that dynamically reallocates quotas across agents. We formulate budget allocation as a constrained optimization problem and derive a greedy Pareto-style policy. Experiments on the AIOpsLab benchmark show that BudgetSRE achieves a success rate within 4-6 percentage points of an unconstrained oracle at medium budget, outperforms single-agent ReAct by up to 17.9 points at low budget, and reduces unsafe-action incidence by up to 53% compared with naive multi-agent baselines. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Greedy Priority Inheritance With Backtracking for Multi-Agent Pathfinding Problem
authors: Tang, Mingkai; Li, Yuanhang; Gan, Lu; Zhang, Chengxi; Sun, Yuxiang; Wu, Jin
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Some real-world transportation systems require moving robots from their start points to goal points without collision, which can be formalized as the multi-agent pathfinding (MAPF) problem. The Priority Inheritance with Backtracking (PIBT) algorithm is an efficient approach for MAPF with low-degree polynomial time complexity and proven completeness. PIBT employs a dynamic prioritization scheme to determine the order of sequential agent planning. However, this scheme may lead to low solution quality, which is measured by the sum of time steps each agent takes to reach its goal for the first time. In this work, we propose two greedy variants of the PIBT algorithm that improve solution quality while preserving completeness: Backflow-based Greedy PIBT (GPIBT-B) and Reduction-based Greedy PIBT (GPIBT-R). GPIBT-B introduces a backflow mechanism that allows a determined agent to adjust its plan during the planning of another agent, achieving higher solution quality while maintaining the same low time complexity as PIBT. GPIBT-R formulates the planning problem as a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP), enabling the use of efficient MILP solvers to find high-quality solutions. Experimental results show that GPIBT-B substantially improves solution quality with minimal additional computation time, while GPIBT-R achieves even better solution quality at the cost of increased computational time. Note to Practitioners—This paper addresses the challenge of inefficient multi-robot coordination in logistics and automation systems. While solvers like PIBT can quickly generate feasible paths, their solutions often suffer from low quality, leading to diminished system throughput and longer task completion times. To address this, we propose two greedy variants that significantly enhance solution quality. GPIBT-B uses a lightweight backflow mechanism, allowing robots to dynamically adjust their moves to avoid blocking each other. This achieves markedly faster goal attainment with minimal computational overhead. GPIBT-R employs an MILP model for higher-quality, globally optimized single-step plans, while more planning time is required. Experiments show GPIBT-B delivers superior solutions with negligible speed loss, making it ideal for real-time systems. GPIBT-R offers the highest quality for less time-sensitive applications. It should be noted that the solution quality of GPIBT-B, while significantly improved, may still be further optimized, and the computational efficiency of GPIBT-R remains an area for future enhancement. These algorithms can be directly applied to improve efficiency in warehouse logistics, automated sorting systems, and multi-robot assembly lines. Both algorithms assume a centralized coordination scheme where a server collects global information and distributes commands to robots. GPIBT-B is well-suited for real-time deployment due to its low overhead, while GPIBT-R is recommended for applications where path quality is prioritized over computation time. © 2004-2012 IEEE.

title: Learning-Assisted Formation Control of Networked Wheeled Robots with Barrier Safety Penalty
authors: Xiang, Yu-Zhu; Chen, Xizhe; Guo, Jian; Xiang, Zhengrong
venue: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
abstract: This paper investigates the formation control problem of IoT-enabled networked wheeled robots subject to environmental disturbances, safety constraints, and model uncertainties. To ensure safe operation in dynamic and complex environments, a barrier penalty-based safety mechanism is first constructed for each robot to achieve collision avoidance while maintaining the desired formation configuration. On this basis, a distributed model predictive control framework is developed to generate coordinated control actions using locally exchanged information. Furthermore, an identifier-actor-critic reinforcement learning architecture is integrated with the barrier penalty mechanism, enabling the robots to compensate for unknown dynamics and external disturbances without requiring accurate system models. Simulation results on networked wheeled robots verify the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed approach for intelligent multi-robot systems in IoT-based applications. © 2014 IEEE.

title: Robust Decentralized Control and Dynamic Modeling of Cooperative Quadrotor Formations for Slung Rigid-Plate Transportation Under 3D Impact Loads
authors: Saraswat, Shelesh Krishna; Zneid, Basem Abu; Mohammad, Hessan; Sollapur, Shrishail B.; Mohapatra, Tapas Kumar; Anand, T.; Kaur, Gaganjot; Bisht, Yashwant Singh
venue: Journal of Vibration Engineering and Technologies
abstract: Purpose: Cooperative multi-UAV slung-load transport is critically vulnerable to sudden external disturbances and impulsive excitations. This paper investigates the coupled dynamic modeling and robust decentralized control of a collaborative quadcopter formation transporting a rigid load plate via slung cables, with an explicit focus on three-dimensional central and eccentric inelastic impact scenarios. Methods: A modular Newton–Euler multi-body formulation is established by decoupling the interconnected system into distinct carrier agents and a suspended rigid-plate load agent, thereby enhancing dynamic scalability. Fully inelastic impact dynamics are formulated using spatial momentum conservation laws to characterize the transient 3D shock forces and moments. To ensure formation stabilization and trajectory tracking without central communication bottlenecks, feedback linearization is employed to linearize the coupled nonlinear multi-agent system, followed by the synthesis of a decentralized Linear Quadratic Regulator with integral action (LQR-I) for each carrier quadcopter. Results: Extensive numerical simulations demonstrate superior disturbance rejection and robust trajectory tracking across nominal and severe impact regimes. The proposed decentralized LQR-I controller achieves an overall position root-mean-square error (RMSE) as low as 0.023 m under nominal conditions, bounds the maximum transient vertical deviation to 0.8055 m under the most severe eccentric shock, and guarantees a rapid post-impact recovery time of approximately 8.1 s. Furthermore, continuous cable tension is preserved throughout all maneuvers (>12" " N with peak transient values reaching 51.8 N ), completely preventing cable-slack hazards, while quadcopter thrust commands remain strictly within the physical saturation bound of 25 N. Conclusion: The proposed decentralized LQR-I scheme coupled with feedback linearization provides an effective, computationally scalable, and practically viable control framework for multi-UAV slung-load logistics subjected to severe impulsive impact loads. © Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.

title: Agentic Lightweight Consensus for Resilient Monitoring and Control of Modern Data Centers in Smart Cities
authors: Furno, Domenico; Loia, Vincenzo
venue: Smart Cities
abstract: Modern data centers underpin smart-city services, yet their control loops must reconcile noisy, missing, or deliberately deceptive telemetry before acting autonomously. We present a two-path agentic architecture in which a deterministic fast path fuses sensor reports through a reliability-based fuzzy-preference OWA operator (FPR–OWA) and a persistent consensus-reaching process (CRP), while an optional reactive or LLM supervisor can only propose typed actions that a deterministic verifier must admit. Across 1890 indexed simulation scenarios and seven attack families, no estimator dominates: averaging attains the lowest global error and sensor redundancy explains most of the accuracy variation, whereas FPR–OWA + CRP provides the strongest anomaly-diagnostic signal. We prove that logistic dominance preserves the reliability ordering and add a zone-dynamic temporal-consistency ablation. In the original safety campaign, no unsafe execution was observed in the verifier-gated episodes, and the unified process-local runtime later passed all 24 deterministic fault-injection cases; both are empirical, not formal, guarantees. An illustrative closed-loop pilot adds standard control metrics and reveals delayed recovery under common-mode sensor bias; a CPU benchmark keeps persistent-CRP median latency below (Formula presented.) ms at 100 sensors. The result is a reproducible, bounded blueprint for verified autonomy in datacenter infrastructure; hardware validation, production authentication, and energy measurement remain future work. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Navigating complexity in offshore emergency response: lessons from the OMSAR 2024 exercise using effective management theory
authors: Samuel, Carlos; Samsudin, Khairilmizal; Sansuddin, Nurulilyana; Musa, Nor Azlan; Fernandes, Ashwin Anson; James, Nathaneal; Kamarudin, Ainul Husna
venue: Transportation Research Interdisciplinary Perspectives
abstract: Evaluating Large-Scale Emergency Exercises (LSEEs) within complex multi-agency landscapes remains a critical challenge for maritime transport governance. This paper analyses the OMSAR 2024 exercise—a multi-hazard simulation involving a support vessel collision and a mass maritime rescue operation along a critical 175-kilometre offshore transport corridor in Malaysia. Integrating the Five-Element Model of Effective Emergency Management with structured real-time observations from 37 subject matter experts, this study evaluates the operationalization of the Arahan NADMA No. 1 directive under intense logistical stress. Systematic refinement of 152 primary observer logs yielded 51 consolidated findings, exposing a critical disparity between tactical seamanship and systemic transport coordination. Severe procedural bottlenecks were concentrated in Resources & Logistics (25%) and Command Structure (22%), highlighted by a 40-minute ’command vacuum’ during vessel fleet handovers between corporate and state authorities. The findings demonstrate that inter-agency friction between separate maritime protocols undermines the Unified Command required for deep-water transport crises. We offer strategic policy interventions: standardizing maritime command triggers, digitalizing information systems for a Common Operating Picture, and institutionalizing biennial joint Emergency Preparedness and Response (EP&R) transit certifications to safeguard interdisciplinary maritime transport networks. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Adaptive Digital Control Architecture for Multi-Agent Industrial Electroplating Lines: A Modular Microcontroller-Based Approach
authors: Andrijević, Nebojša; Lovreković, Zoran; Đokić, Vladimir; Perišić, Jasmina; Milovanović, Marina
venue: Electronics (Switzerland)
abstract: This paper presents a deterministic embedded control architecture for an industrial electroplating line. The validated system includes two autonomous trolleys, 18 station-aligned process positions, shared-track motion, and redundant grouped baths. The proposed controller addresses the limitations of rigid sequential automation by combining asynchronous finite-state trolley execution, runtime allocation of equivalent technological stations, dwell-time-preserving retrieval, distributed thermal supervision, and layered fail-safe protection within a single ATmega2560-based implementation. The core contribution is the integration of virtual process groups and temporal FIFO logic into a compact plant-side embedded controller. This enables adaptive bath selection and process-completion-based retrieval without reliance on a real-time operating system or a computationally heavy supervisory runtime. The architecture also incorporates predictive pre-start validation, runtime software arbitration, hardware-wired interlocks, binary-coded trolley positioning, and a distributed 1-Wire thermal measurement network. Validation was performed in a controller-centered hardware-in-the-loop representation of an 18-station zinc electroplating line. Over a 100-batch horizon, the proposed architecture reduced makespan from 1642 min to 1244 min, corresponding to a 24.2% throughput improvement. Average trolley idle time decreased from 18.4 min/batch to 4.1 min/batch. Grouped-bath utilization increased from 64% to 91%, while tracked bottleneck incidents decreased from 18 to 2. These results show that adaptive, resource-aware, and safety-layered electroplating control can be realized effectively on a compact embedded platform in an industry-representative HIL setting, while preserving dwell-time integrity and controller-level safety invariants. © 2026 by the authors.

title: PRISM: Pipeline for Root-cause Investigation via Specialized Multi-agents
authors: Yan, Weiran; Wu, Yichao; Liang, Penghao; Yuan, Mengwei; Liu, Jianan; Yang, Jing; Li, Xianyou
venue: 2026 International Conference on Generative Artificial Intelligence and Information Security, GAIIS 2026
abstract: Root Cause Analysis (RCA) in microservice architectures is a complex task requiring the correlation of multimodal telemetry data across distributed components. Existing single-agent LLM approaches often struggle with long-context reasoning and hallucination, lacking rigorous evidence verification. To address these limitations, we propose PRISM (Pipeline for Root-cause Investigation via Specialized Multi-agents), a hierarchical multi-agent framework designed to emulate the workflow of Site Reliability Engineers (SREs). PRISM decomposes the RCA process into three specialized roles: a Triage Agent that rapidly localizes suspect services using rule-based traffic analysis; an Investigator Agent that gathers objective, quantified evidence across temporal windows without making diagnoses; and an RCA Specialist Agent that synthesizes evidence to deduce the root cause. Additionally, we introduce an Evidence Search Agent that works in tandem with PRISM to iteratively refine tool configurations by collecting ground-truth evidence, ensuring high-fidelity evidence retrieval. We evaluate PRISM on a high-fidelity dataset collected from the Google Online Boutique system, covering 16 scenarios across four fault categories. Experimental results demonstrate that PRISM achieves 93.8% accuracy in service localization and 100% in fault type classification, validating the effectiveness of structured multi-agent collaboration in automated troubleshooting. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Energy Efficient and Conflict-Free Path Planning for Autonomous Mobile Robot Fleets via Obstacle Persistence Evaluation and Smart Zoning
authors: Triki, Ghaylen; Mohammadpour, Mohammad; Kelouwani, Sousso; Zeghmi, Lotfi
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: The integration of Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) into smart manufacturing systems offers promising gains in flexibility and efficiency. However, navigating dynamic and constrained industrial environments remains challenging. AMRs often need to brake or stop abruptly to avoid collisions caused by unexpected changes or unforeseen nearby obstacles, which leads to high energy consumption and reduced operational efficiency. Unlike traditional methods that solely focus on safety, using priority rules or speed limits to avoid multi-robot deadlocks, our approach also considers energy efficiency and enables smooth navigation without imposing hierarchy among a fleet of robots. A hybrid framework is introduced that enables energy-aware and conflict-free path planning, enhancing long-term autonomy in AMR fleets. First, the decentralized AMR fleet operates autonomously while continuously reporting potential collision locations, along with the corresponding Time-To-Collision (TTC) values for unforeseen obstacles. Then, the data collected from the fleet is consolidated by a map coordinator unit, which introduces a novel obstacle persistence evaluation method. This method leverages Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) modeling to distinguish between temporary and persistent obstacles. Next, to prevent multi-robot deadlocks, we propose a smart zoning framework based on energy and reachability analysis. Finally, an adaptive path planning algorithm is employed, using the updated multi-layered costmap to balance between path length and conflict cost, adapting to spatiotemporal variations in high-traffic locations. Through comparisons with several state-of-the-art algorithms, we demonstrate that the proposed method ensures safe navigation while achieving smoother trajectory execution and effective energy optimization in dynamic environments. © 2013 IEEE.

title: Understanding organisations’ responsibilities and readiness for occupational road safety: Implications for saving lives beyond 2025
authors: Wennberg, Hanna; Nævestad, Tor-Olav
venue: Safety Science
abstract: Most organisations generate travel and transport and thus influence traffic safety. Nevertheless, their roles and responsibilities for occupational road safety remain poorly understood. This study examines organisational readiness for occupational road safety with a particular focus on the relationship between organisations’ perceptions of traffic safety and the implementation of traffic safety measures. The study is based on a survey of organisational representatives in 109 companies in Sweden in 2025. The survey consists of two questionnaires capturing organisational commitment and reported measures to improve traffic safety in organisations’ roles as employers and transport buyers. An employer questionnaire focuses on traffic safety requirements for employees’ work-related travel and organisational vehicle fleets, while a transport procurement questionnaire captures the requirements on transport procurement. Organisational readiness for occupational road safety is analysed using Organisational Readiness for Implementing Change (ORIC), including perceived capacity to influence traffic safety, views on responsibility, and the integration of traffic safety into occupational health and safety (OHS) or sustainability practices. The results show that many organisations have policies for work-related travel and set traffic safety requirements for their vehicles, while such requirements in transport procurement remain limited. Regression analyses indicate that organisations with higher readiness are more likely to set traffic safety requirements, particularly regarding work-related travel. The findings highlight the need to strengthen organisations’ awareness of their roles and responsibilities, clarify expectations for organisations from authorities, and further integrate traffic safety into organisational management systems to reduce road traffic fatalities and injuries, in line with the global road safety agenda, often framed as “saving lives beyond 2025”. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Autonomous collision-avoiding for multi-UAVs in complex dynamic environments: An event-triggered PPO approach with LSTM-attention integration
authors: Liang, Chengqing; Liu, Lei; Cao, Jinde; Li, Xiaodi
venue: Neural Networks
abstract: The challenge of flocking collision avoidance lies in selecting the optimal strategy that balances decision-making intelligence and resource saving in a complex dynamic environment. Meanwhile, the design of the collision avoidance reward function for deep reinforcement learning (DRL) in this scenario may lack a quantitative basis. To overcome this challenge, this paper proposes an event-triggered proximal policy optimization (ETPPO) avoidance strategy by combining rewards from a dynamic model under ideal environments and DRL rewards. Firstly, this strategy incorporates the intermittent communication costs of event-triggered mechanisms (ETM) to achieve a balance between avoidance performance and communication resources. Secondly, a composite avoidance reward mechanism is designed, which combines the cost function based on dynamic model and obstacle avoidance reward based on DRL. The quality and rationality of reward function design in complex environments are improved. Then, to make full use of historical information and focus on task-related key status information, an LSTM-Attention (LA) fusion module combining long short-term memory (LSTM) and attention mechanisms is introduced, and the ETPPO-LA algorithm is constructed. The stability of the network and training efficiency of the algorithm are improved. Finally, the proposed algorithm is verified based on the Ros-Stage simulation platform, which shows the advantages in terms of accumulated rewards and avoidance success rate. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd

title: Joint modeling of collision type and driver injury severities in truck-involved crashes: A copula-based multivariate approach
authors: Song, Penglin; Sze, N.N.
venue: Transportation Research Part A: Policy and Practice
abstract: Despite the vital role of trucks in freight transport, crashes in which they are involved often result in severe consequences. It is therefore crucial to identify the factors that influence the risk of truck-related crashes and resulting injuries to formulate effective fleet management and transport policy strategies. However, previous studies have often overlooked two major issues: interdependent correlations in driver injury severity within the same crash, and the endogenous influence of collision type on driver injury severity. Overlooking these issues can result in biased parameter estimation. Therefore, this study develops a copula-based multivariate model to jointly examine the relationships among collision type and driver injury severities in truck-involved crashes. Based on crash data from North Carolina for the period 2016–2019, the proposed model simultaneously measures the associations between potential risk factors and three dependent variables: collision type, car driver injury severity, and truck driver injury severity. The results indicate remarkable differences in how various factors affect the injury severity of truck drivers versus car drivers. The model also successfully accounts for the endogenous effect of collision type on driver injury severity using a recursive structure, thereby improving the precision of parameter estimation. Furthermore, the findings show that the proposed copula-based model effectively captures the interdependent correlations with superior interpretability, compared to conventional models. Based on these findings, decision-makers in the trucking industry can develop more effective countermeasures to reduce the injury risk of all drivers in truck-involved crashes. This can, in turn, enhance the overall safety and operation performance of freight logistics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Controlled Benchmarking of Memory Topologies in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems: Quality, Efficiency, and Privacy Trade-Offs
authors: Kolbeev, Artem R.; Belous, Aleksandr A.; Petrovski, Andrei V.; Kotenko, Igor V.
venue: Proceedings - 2026 IEEE Ural-Siberian Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Radioelectronics and Information Technology, USBEREIT 2026
abstract: Large language model agents are increasingly deployed in interactive, long-horizon settings, yet their behavior remains bounded by finite context windows and non-persistent prompting. In practice, this manifests itself as repeated information seeking, gradual constraint drift, and unstable output across similar episodes. These effects are amplified in multi-agent systems, where memory serves not only as persistence but also as a coordination substrate enabling division of labor, reuse of intermediate results, and convergence of shared task state. At the same time, agent memory is privacy-critical: storing and retrieving user-related traces expands the attack surface and may enable unintended disclosure, poisoning, or inference-style attacks. This paper proposes a controlled benchmarking methodology for comparing memory topologies in multi-agent systems based on large language model agents under a fixed agent structure, identical model settings, and a unified memory interface. Four configurations-no memory, local per-agent memory, shared memory, and hybrid memory with a crystallization policy that promotes only validated and depersonalized facts and rules to shared storage-are evaluated on a reproducible offline episode suite. The benchmark reports task success and constraint compliance, efficiency, and tail latency, and memory-specific measures including retrieval noise and duplicated work. The proposed protocol is intended as an engineering tool for selecting memory designs in privacy-sensitive agent systems. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Decision intelligence for electric bus charging scheduling through LLM-driven reward shaping and reinforcement learning
authors: Zhan, Jiahao; Yang, Ying; Zhang, Zhe; Liu, Yang; Bie, Yiming; Pei, Mingyang; Qu, Xiaobo
venue: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies
abstract: The rapid expansion of electric bus fleets has made charging scheduling a critical decision-intelligence problem in urban fleet-energy logistics. Reinforcement learning (RL) is promising for this problem, but reward function design still relies on manual trial-and-error and transfers poorly across scenarios. This paper develops an artificial intelligence and operations research (AI-OR) decision intelligence framework that integrates large language model (LLM)-driven reward shaping with RL-based sequential decision-making. The framework represents reward functions as executable code and iteratively optimizes them through four modules: reward initializer, performance analysis, reward exploration, and rollback. An event-triggered two-stage charging reallocation mechanism enforces the action-level operational constraints through action masking, while the battery safety bound is controlled through readiness conditions, reward shaping, and the acceptance criterion. Experiments on a synthetic scenario and two real-world bus stations in Guangzhou compare three mainstream LLMs under different initialization conditions. Results show that LLM-driven reward iteration outperforms traditional methods across all scenarios, reducing costs by up to 32.6 % in nominal within-day charging cost and by up to 22.5 % after an approximate adjustment for the energy left on board. Ablation and sensitivity analyses validate the contribution of each module and the framework’s adaptability to multiple RL algorithms. Reward-evolution analysis further identifies design principles for improving charging efficiency, supporting valley-period energy shifting, and enhancing fleet-energy logistics resilience. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Hallucination-Aware Collaborative Task Scheduling in Multiplex Industrial Networks with LLM-Driven Agents
authors: Li, Pan; Zuo, Tian-Yu; Liu, Mingyi; Jiang, Yichuan; Di, Kai; Lin, Junxiong
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering
abstract: LLM agents in an industrial workflow exchange plans, observations, and intermediate results. A wrong output from one agent can enter another agent's context and spread through the workflow. We model this process as a feedback amplified cascade on a multiplex network that represents task dependencies, communication links, physical proximity, and shared LLM services. The model reveals a connectivity–vulnerability trade-off. Extra cross-layer links can improve collaboration while making hallucination outbreaks easier. We then formulate the Hallucination-Aware Collaborative Task Scheduling (HACTS) problem and prove its NP-hardness. Our Cross-Layer Hallucination-Aware Scheduling algorithm (CLHAS) places verifiers, selects agents, and routes messages according to cascade risk. Under fixed propagation scenarios, verifier placement has a provable approximation guarantee, while the complete scheduler is a practical polynomial-time heuristic. Simulations and controlled API-driven case studies show that CLHAS improves the safety–utility trade-off over networked schedulers. Ablations show that verification and risk-aware routing suppress error propagation, while assignment gains depend on the model back bone and task structure. A strong single-agent baseline further shows that collaborative scheduling is most useful when the workflow requires information exchange across agents. © 2014 IEEE.

title: Intelligent Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Swarm Control Under Electronic Warfare: A Cognitive–Intent Dual-Stream Reinforcement Learning Framework
authors: Chen, Yang; Niu, Jinglong
venue: Drones
abstract: Multi-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) platforms integrate radio-frequency (RF) sensing, datalinks, and onboard embedded compute; adversarial electronic warfare (EW) degrades these subsystems through jamming and forces decentralized control policies to act on fragmented observations—a setting aligned with intelligent electronic systems and autonomous robotics in contested spectrum. Cooperative swarms then face two compounding failure modes: loss of coherent situational awareness, and reward-driven passive survival that suppresses mission completion. Memory-based multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) partially addresses the first but tends to reinforce the second; dense intent shaping addresses the second but becomes unreliable when observations are incomplete. We propose CIDA (Cognitive–Intent Dual-Stream Architecture), a reinforcement learning framework that decouples belief reconstruction from tactical intent at the representation level while coupling them through a unified actor–critic update. The cognitive stream encodes a 64-step observation history with a pre-normalized Transformer to reconstruct threat belief; the intent stream supplies a hierarchical potential field (reconnaissance, threat-weighted engagement, and approach incentives). A steady-state training mechanism (dynamic reward scaling and adaptive gradient clipping) stabilizes Transformer-based on-policy learning under non-stationary multi-agent dynamics. In a complex terrain scenario with SAM, AAA, and jammer assets, CIDA reaches 96.15% task success versus 12.21% (memoryless PPO) and 25.28% (MAPPO+RNN), with ablations showing nonlinear coupling and emergent tactics such as jammer bypass and weak-sector traversal. Results are robust to a four-fold sweep of the intent-shaping weight (above 90% success). © 2026 by the authors.

title: RNN Learning-Based Prescribed-Time Safe and Robust Cooperative Group Formation Control for High-Speed Flight Vehicle Swarm under Dynamic Event-Triggered Communication
authors: Qiao, Yitao; Li, Shuang; Jiang, Bin
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics
abstract: Concurrent and complex aerial missions with multiple targets exceed the capabilities of a single cooperative formation of high-speed flight vehicles (HSFVs). To address this challenge, this article decomposes a fleet of HSFVs (subject to multiple compounding factors, including unknown aerodynamic disturbances, unmodeled or parametric uncertainties, actuator faults, and potential intervehicle collisions) into several subgroups and develops a recurrent neural network (RNN) online learning-based prescribed-time safe and robust cooperative group formation control protocol under dynamic event-triggered communication. A distributed prescribed-time event-triggered estimator (DP-TE-TE) is first developed to drive all HSFVs to acquire the convex hull information (i.e., input, velocity, and position) spanned by multiple virtual leader vehicles (VLVs) before grouping or the input, velocity, and position information of their respective single VLV within the group after grouping. Then, based on the constraint-following theory, the safety distance inequality between any potentially colliding pair of HSFVs, along with the first-order differential equation involving the formation position tracking error, is converted into collision motion constraints and prescribed-time trajectory tracking constraints, respectively. To enhance the flight control performance of the swarm, an RNN is constructed for each HSFV to learn the unknown nonlinear function induced by multiple compounding factors, thereby providing online compensation for the subsequent control design. Finally, by integrating the constraint-following errors derived from collision motion constraints and prescribed-time trajectory tracking constraints, the RNN compensation term, and the estimated information, the prescribed-time safe and robust cooperative group formation control scheme (P-TSRCGFCS) is proposed. In the simulation examples, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms is verified by dividing 12 HSFVs and three VLVs into three subgroups to perform the desired cooperative group formation task. © 2013 IEEE.

title: Multi-agent deep reinforcement learning for group intelligence in emergency evacuation: A decentralized simulation-to-reality platform with perception-aware policies
authors: Li, Jixiang; Wan, Baishu; Song, Zhigong
venue: Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) enables agents to learn and optimize their policies through interactions within a shared environment, addressing both cooperation and competition challenges. In this work, we develop a MADRL framework specifically engineered for dynamic and complex environments, aiming to bridge the gap between simulation and real-world deployment. The proposed framework adopts a multi-scenario and multi-stage policy gradient approach with a decentralized training and execution structure, allowing agents to seamlessly transfer their learned behaviors to real-world applications such as emergency evacuation. Simulation results further demonstrate that the framework identifies optimal evacuation routes, referred to as "escape arcs," from collision heatmaps. These arcs represent paths that minimize congestion and maximize safe evacuation. In deployment, the generated policies have demonstrated versatility, effectively handling complex situations and showing significant potential for applications in public safety and emergency response. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Post-Hoc Knowledge Grounding for Verifiable Multi-Agent Search and Rescue Decision Support
authors: Tan, Yayun; Kurfess, Franz; Delgado, Emmanuel; Young, Christopher; Bloom, Gary
venue: AAAI Spring Symposium - Technical Report
abstract: Multi-agent systems powered by large language models (LLMs) show promise for complex decision-support tasks, yet their outputs often contain hallucinations that undermine trust in safety-critical domains such as search and rescue (SAR). We present a post-hoc verification framework that grounds LLM agent outputs in a probabilistic knowledge graph derived from approximately 12,000 curated cases from the International Search and Rescue Incident Database (ISRID). Our approach extracts structured claims from agent outputs, performs probabilistic reasoning to detect statistical anomalies, and produces tiered decisions (accept, flag, reject) with explicit evidence chains. The framework operates downstream of a seven-agent SAR system, verifying terrain predictions (where the subject is likely found) and status predictions (the subject's likely condition). These claims directly inform search prioritization. Experiments demonstrate that coordinators following our system's recommendations achieve 71.0% accuracy, compared to 51.6% when accepting all LLM outputs, a 19.4 percentage point improvement. The system detects anomalies with 81.3% F1 score while maintaining practical coverage (46.3% of claims verified). Ablation studies confirm anomaly detection as the critical component, contributing +5.7 percentage points over grounding alone. Our framework provides a practical path toward trustworthy AI in emergency response. Copyright © 2026, Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (www.aaai.org). All rights reserved.

title: Simulating Collaborative Learning with Data-Driven LLM-Agents
authors: Yan, Yu; Liang, Changhao; Ogata, Hiroaki
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
abstract: Simulating collaborative learning is a critical yet challenging goal in educational technology. While recent Large Language Model (LLM) advancements show promise, existing approaches often rely on static error models and rigid dialogue control and are primarily designed as student-facing training tools. To address these limitations, we present an autonomous ‘zero-player’ multi-agent simulation platform, powered by GPT-4o, designed as a computational testbed for research. Our key contributions are a data-driven, probabilistic engine for modeling a realistic spectrum of student capabilities, and a fine-grained, consensus-driven dialogue protocol that fosters emergent, bottom-up collaboration. Qualitative evaluations demonstrate that our system generates sound, expert-aligned problem solutions and, critically, produces plausible collaborative dynamics, including peer-to-peer error identification and correction. Our work establishes a high-fidelity platform for studying the mechanisms of collaborative learning and lays the groundwork for future predictive tools to help educators optimize student grouping. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: Trustworthy LLM-Based Agents for Data-Centric AI
authors: Chen, Tianlong; Pei, Jian; Zhang, Minxing; Zhao, Liang
venue: Proceedings of the ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
abstract: Large language model (LLM) based agents are evolving from conversational chatbots into autonomous decision-makers that plan, reason, wield tools, and collaborate across high-stakes domains such as healthcare, finance, and scientific discovery. Yet this power brings a fundamental challenge: trustworthiness. How can we guarantee that an agent remains robust when real-world data shifts, degrades, or is deliberately poisoned? What defenses exist against memory injection, tool-based exploits, or cascade failures in multi-agent systems? Can we embed domain-specific causal validity, clinical safety, or fairness directly into agent reasoning? And how do we measure trust when it spans robustness, security, reliability, and alignment - each with its own irreconcilable trade-offs? This tutorial delivers a systematic, data-centric roadmap to build LLM agents that are not merely capable but provably trustworthy. We organize the landscape into four interconnected pillars: (i) generalizability under distribution shift, noise, and adversarial inputs; (ii) security architectures that defend against emerging threats - from indirect prompt injection to supply-chain vulnerabilities; (iii) domain-grounded trust in science, engineering, medicine, and commerce, where agents must respect theories, systems, clinical causality, and fairness constraints; and (iv) multi-dimensional evaluation benchmarks that expose trade-offs rather than collapsing them into a single score. By unifying advances in LLM agents, robust machine learning, and data-centric AI, we equip the audience with both foundational principles and actionable recipes to design, deploy, and ultimately trust the next generation of autonomous agent systems. © 2026 Owner/Author.

title: TriBand-BEV: Real-Time LiDAR-Only 3D Pedestrian Detection via Height-Aware BEV and High-Resolution Feature Fusion
authors: Khoshkdahan, Mohammad; Vinel, Alexey
venue: AAMAS 2026 - Proceedings of the 25th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems
abstract: Safe autonomous agents and mobile robots need fast real time 3D perception, especially for vulnerable road users (VRUs) such as pedestrians. We introduce a new bird’s eye view (BEV) encoding, which maps the full 3D LiDAR point cloud into a light-weight 2D BEV tensor with three height bands. We explicitly reformulate 3D detection as a 2D detection problem and then reconstruct 3D boxes from the BEV outputs. A single network detects cars, pedestrians, and cyclists in one pass. The backbone uses area attention at deep stages, a hierarchical bidirectional neck over P1 to P4 fuses context and detail, and the head predicts oriented boxes with distribution focal learning for side offsets and a rotated IoU loss. Training applies a small vertical re bin and a mild reflectance jitter in channel space to resist memorization. We use an interquartile range (IQR) filter to remove noisy and outlier LiDAR points during 3D reconstruction. On KITTI dataset, TriBand-BEV attains 58.7/52.6/47.2 pedestrian BEV AP(%) for easy, moderate, and hard at 49 FPS on a single consumer GPU, surpassing Complex-YOLO, with gains of +12.6%, +7.5%, and +3.1%. Qualitative scenes show stable detection under occlusion. The pipeline is compact and ready for real time robotic deployment. Our source code is publicly available on GitHub. 1 © 2026 International Foundation for Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems.

title: Resilient Scheduling for Urban Infrastructure Maintenance and Inspection Fleets: A Potential-Guided MARL Approach
authors: Zhang, Shuyang
venue: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Automation and Robotics in Construction
abstract: Efficient fleet scheduling in urban infrastructure maintenance and inspection services requires a delicate balance between task productivity and operational safety. However, traditional centralized algorithms often struggle with the stochastic nature of dynamic urban environments, leading to communication latency and collision risks. To bridge the gap between global platform planning and local reactive execution, this paper proposes a Potential-Guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (PG-MARL) framework designed for resilient edge computing. By integrating global BFS-based topological guidance with decentralized reinforcement learning, the method utilizes a lightweight state representation to significantly accelerate training convergence and enable agents to navigate complex, non-convex environments autonomously. Experimental results in a discretized semantic grid environment demonstrate that PG-MARL achieves near-zero collision rates with an operational efficiency trade-off compared to optimal planning baselines. This study provides a resilient and safety-aware solution suitable for practical deployment as an autonomous edge intelligence module for city-level operation management platforms. © 2026 International Association on Automation and Robotics in Construction. All Rights Reserved.

title: Lay2Graph-MAPD: A Modular Framework with Layout-Aware Graph Generation for Multi-agent Pickup and Delivery Problems
authors: Knierim, Justus; Ringel, Jonas; Amberg, Boris; Glock, Katharina
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
abstract: Autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) are increasingly used in intralogistics to automate material handling and reduce physical workload. Efficient operation of large robot fleets requires solving the Multi-Agent Pickup and Delivery (MAPD) problem, which combines collision-free multi-agent path planning with task assignment. Although numerous powerful algorithms exist, no framework provides an end-to-end experimentation pipeline to systematically investigate how industrial layouts, routing graph structures, and planning algorithms influence MAPD performance. To address this gap, we introduce Lay2Graph-MAPD, a modular open-source framework that enables reproducible end-to-end MAPD experimentation. Starting from layout images, the framework generates MAPD benchmarks, including routing graphs, integrates state-of-the-art collision-free path planning and task assignment algorithms through plug-and-play interfaces, and provides comprehensive analysis tools within a unified workflow. An experimental evaluation demonstrates the applicability, robustness, and scalability of the framework across various layout classes, routing graph structures, fleet sizes, and algorithmic configurations. It further demonstrates that Lay2Graph-MAPD enables systematic investigation of how these factors influence MAPD performance in AMR systems. The code is publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21410202. © The Author(s) 2027.

title: Constraint Learning in Multi-Agent Dynamic Games From Demonstrations of Local Nash Interactions
authors: Zhang, Zhouyu; Chiu, Chih-Yuan; Chou, Glen
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: We present an inverse dynamic game-based algorithm to learn parametric constraints from a given dataset of local Nash equilibrium interactions between multiple agents. Specifically, we introduce mixed-integer linear programs (MILP) encoding the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions of the interacting agents, which recover constraints consistent with the local Nash stationarity of the interaction demonstrations. We establish theoretical guarantees that our method learns inner approximations of the true safe and unsafe sets. We also use the interaction constraints recovered by our method to design motion plans that robustly satisfy the underlying constraints. Across simulations and hardware experiments, our methods accurately inferred constraints and designed safe interactive motion plans for various classes of constraints, both convex and non-convex, from interaction demonstrations of agents with nonlinear dynamics. © 2016 IEEE.

title: Ellipsoid uncertainty tether model for collision avoidance in a fleet of Remotely Operated Vehicles
authors: Viel, Christophe
venue: Robotics and Autonomous Systems
abstract: During collision avoidance, the tether of Remote Operated Vehicle (ROV) is subject to entanglement with obstacles or other ROVs’ tether. This specificity renders traditional multi-robot obstacle avoidance approaches inadequate for tethered multi-robot scenarios. This paper proposes a guaranteed ellipsoid model for representing the ROV's tether and its nearby obstacles, enabling an efficient, low-computation collision avoidance method for a fleet of ROVs. The model ensures that if the ellipsoid encompassing the tether remains entirely outside the ellipsoid encompassing an obstacle, there is no risk that the tether collides with it. The approach requires only the two attachment points of the tether and its length, without needing any information about the tether's shape, dynamics, or external disturbances such as underwater currents. A collision avoidance strategy is developed based on potential field methods combined with tether length management. When multiple ROVs are involved, personalities are added to ROV to obtain different behaviors, reducing the likelihood of deadlocks during avoidance maneuvers. Simulations demonstrate the method's effectiveness across various scenarios, and its limitations are also discussed. © 2025 The Author

title: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning and Digital Twin Driven Intelligent Teaching System for Low-Altitude Logistics Talent Cultivation
authors: Li, Haidong
venue: Proceedings of the 3rd International Conference on Educational Digitalization and Computer Science in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, EDCS 2026
abstract: Background: The rapid development of the low-altitude economy has created an urgent demand for talents mastering advanced skills such as dynamic airspace collaboration, multi-agent decision-making, and real-time path planning. Traditional training modes face severe challenges including high costs, high risks, and a lack of intelligent adaptive guidance. Objectives: This study aims to design, implement, and validate an intelligent teaching system driven by multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) and digital twin (DT). The core objective is to develop a computer system capable of simulating complex low-altitude logistics scenarios, providing personalized adversarial training, and delivering intelligent feedback, so as to address the efficiency and adaptability issues in skills training. Methods: A design science research paradigm in computing is adopted. First, a high-fidelity, interactive digital twin simulation environment is constructed based on the Unity3D engine and real GIS data. Second, the multi-UAV collaborative delivery task is formalized as a partially observable Markov game, and a MARL decision engine based on the MADDPG framework is designed and implemented with algorithm optimizations for credit assignment and exploration efficiency. Finally, an AI tutor module integrated with large language models (LLM) and domain knowledge graphs is developed for automated generation of diagnostic feedback. Results: Technical evaluations show that the optimized MADDPG algorithm achieves a 91.3% task success rate and the lowest number of collisions in test scenarios, significantly outperforming baseline algorithms. The digital twin system maintains a rendering frame rate of >60 FPS under complex scenarios. Feedback generated by the AI tutor receives a relevance score of over 82% in expert evaluations. Teaching experiments reveal that the experimental group (N=30) using the system shows a 15.6% improvement in operational efficiency and a 32.4% reduction in planning errors compared with the control group (p<0.01). Conclusions: The main contributions of this study lie in the technical integration, algorithm optimization, and empirical validation of a MARL-DT-LLM intelligent teaching system. The system provides a scalable, data-driven solution for complex skills training such as low-altitude logistics, verifying the potential of advanced computer technologies to reshape vocational education models. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: MIRA: Safety-Constrained Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Joint Prescriptive Maintenance and Production Rescheduling in Industrial IoT
authors: Babu, Md. Ashraful; AlArjani, Ali; Lahby, Mohamed
venue: Future Internet
abstract: Industrial IoT maintenance often stops at health prediction, leaving maintenance, rescheduling, safety, and communication to separate decision processes. This study presents MIRA, a safety-constrained graph-based multi-agent reinforcement learning architecture for joint prescriptive maintenance, production rescheduling, and event-triggered communication. Machine condition was estimated from CNC milling data using temporal convolutional models; because predictive uncertainty failed a predefined validation gate, the controller used deterministic health estimates. Evaluation covered five controllers, six simulated scenarios, and 1800 matched episodes. Relative to Graph-MAPPO, MIRA reduced operational cost by 9.38%, weighted tardiness by 28.10%, unexpected failures by 17.39%, message count by 84.98%, and transmitted data by 83.83%, while increasing on-time completion by 23.55%, without a detectable difference in corrected critical-message recall. Across the three independently trained seeds, failures, safety violations, and message count favored MIRA consistently, whereas cost and tardiness favored MIRA in two seeds. Disabling the execution shield increased safety violations from 0 to 3.56 per episode. Post-training variation in the projected-health safe-start threshold from 0.124 to 0.132 produced no safety violations and only small changes in aggregate operational outcomes. Cross-domain health transfer to PHM 2010 failed without adaptation. The results support simulator-level decision coordination, while broader replication, variable-size deployment, and factory validation remain necessary. © 2026 by the authors.
