title: The electric vehicle routing problem with travel time and energy consumption uncertainty
authors: Han, Bing; Yan, Yifan; Chi, Tianze; Park, Yongshin
venue: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review
abstract: With the development of green logistics and the promotion of new energy vehicle policies, electric vehicles (EVs) have been put into the logistics and distribution area and offered numerous benefits. However, EVs are more susceptible to unpredictable exogenous and endogenous factors than traditional fuel vehicles. One of the issues is the uncertain fluctuations in travel time and energy consumption, which not only affect the safety of the route but potentially yield extra operation costs. This paper emphasizes the electric vehicle routing problem with travel time and energy consumption uncertainty (EVRP-TTECU). The objective is to develop risk-resistant routing and recharging decisions with the lowest conservatively estimated costs for EV fleet operators. A two-stage adaptive robust optimization framework is proposed, where the degree of uncertainty of a route depends on the number of arcs the vehicle passes through, and the recharging amount at stations and the service start time at customers can be adjusted depending on the circumstance. The problem is resolved by a proposed bi-level search method, which is coupled with a set-based heuristic method to find robust routes and a bidirectional labeling algorithm to provide a conservative estimation of the routes’ cost. The algorithm is examined by comparing it with commercial solver and several heuristics based on benchmark instances. Additionally, sensitivity analysis is performed to show the tradeoff between the operation cost and robustness, and a real distribution case is solved to illustrate the practical feasibility. This study can also offer some references to specific EV delivery scenarios, such as supermarkets and cold-chain distribution. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd

title: Research on Multi-agent Collaborative Mechanism for Civil Aviation Enterprise Safety Management Based on Evolutionary Game Theory
authors: Peng, Xueyan; Zhang, Yuan; Ye, Hang
venue: Communications in Computer and Information Science
abstract: Civil aviation safety is essential for public security and social stability. As operations expand and complexity grows, safety management challenges increasingly stem from internal stakeholder conflicts rather than system deficiencies. Corporate decision-makers, safety departments, and business units differ in resource allocation, responsibility, and performance goals, leading to dynamic strategic interactions. This study develops a tripartite evolutionary game model to examine these interactions through equilibrium analysis and numerical simulations. Key findings show that while business units are stable safety actors, they cannot sustain system safety alone. Corporate decision-makers shape overall safety trajectories, and safety departments require institutional independence to avoid passive responses. Resource inputs exhibit threshold effects, and targeted incentives—particularly rewarding safety departments—prove more effective than broad rewards. These insights inform resource optimization, accountability design, and cross-departmental collaboration in safety management. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: Ai SecureDataGuard: A Big Data Security, Privacy-Preserving and Visualization System for LLM-Powered Smart Homes
authors: Zhou, Jun; Li, Hongying; Wang, Fan
venue: Proceedings - 2026 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Big Data Science and Engineering, ICBDSE 2026
abstract: Now large language models and that multi-agent frameworks are widely used, platforms like MOSS can let users talk to smart homes naturally and link up all kinds of household devices. But there's a slew of tough issues hindering these products from practical commercial application IoT data from every device, constant user privacy leaks, intentional prompt injection and safety guardrail evasion attacks, plus no tool to monitor all risks instantly.For the resolution of all aforementioned drawbacks, I built a complete big data security framework named SecureDataGuard. It packs malicious input screening, differential privacy, federated lightweight anomaly tracking and real-time data visual monitoring into one set of tools. I built the whole system on top of MOSS AI's multi-agent structure, and also adopted mature industrial AI security tools from Anquan Data Intelligence.First, I made a two-step intent recognition algorithm to block prompt injection and jailbreak attempts. Second, I put together a mixed privacy protection scheme, so we can use data normally without exposing raw user information. I also developed a slimmed-down Transformer model called LADT to catch abnormal device behaviors the second they happen. On top of that, I built a monitoring panel with StarRocks and ECharts, so administrators can track every risk across bird's-eye view of the whole system.A large set of empirical experiments was implemented with real-world smart home operation records to corroborate the system's performance.. Encouraging results are observed in our experiments. The system accurately recognizes user commands with an accuracy rate of 97.8%.Identifies anomalous activity within 18 ms and lowers privacy leakage probability by 92%. All 18 key security metrics on the dashboard update within milliseconds. This work delivers a practical, deployable technical solution to handle smart home data safety, privacy risks, Anomalous Event Detection and Visual Risk Control © 2026 IEEE.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Hospital Supply Chain Optimization: A Systematic Review
authors: Louah, Soulaiman; Sarir, Hicham; Tahiri, Mohamed
venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent Systems and Digital Applications, ISDA 2026 - Proceedings
abstract: This research paper provides a systematic review of the literature relating to the application of artificial intelligence (AI) in supply chains for hospitals (HSC). It is currently limited in the literature regarding the ways AI is being researched and utilized within supply chains in hospitals, even though this area is a critical influence on healthcare outcomes, minimizing costs, and ensuring patient safety. This complexity is compounded by the fact that hospitals experience uncertainty in their businesses and demand varies at different levels, while at the same time maintaining compliance with federal regulations and having the need to make real-time decisions. AI techniques such as: machine learning; deep learning; natural language processing; expert systems; fuzzy logic; multi agent systems; neural networks; support vector machines; optimization algorithms; robotics; and computer vision, have all shown promise in improving inventory control, purchasing, shipping and receiving, forecasting demands for products, and allocating personnel and physical resources to be used in managing hospital supplies. The results of the literature review provided a classification of a total of 41 peer-reviewed research articles, published from 2002 to February 2026 and currently indexed in the SCOPUS database, with respect to the two major dimensions of AI technique and HSC function or activity. The results will guide the reader in realizing the current research focus, the prevailing AI methods, the lack of research in certain areas, and ideas for future research in developing intelligent and resilient HSCs. © 2026 IEEE.

title: GE-HAPPO: Graph-Enhanced Heterogeneous-Agent PPO for Coverage Optimization in Communication-Constrained USV-UAV Teams
authors: Lu, Xinrong; Liu, Hanxiao; Qu, Dong; Song, Rui; Peng, Yan
venue: Lecture Notes in Electrical Engineering
abstract: Conventional multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) methods for heterogeneous unmanned surface vessel-unmanned aerial vehicle (USV – UAV) coordination often rely on fixed-size observation vectors, which fail to capture dynamic spatial relationships, communication constraints, and heterogeneous capabilities. This limits their ability to achieve efficient coverage and safe operation in complex maritime-aerial environments. To address this, this paper proposes a Graph-Enhanced Heterogeneous Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (GE-HAPPO) framework that integrates a graph attention network into the MARL pipeline. The model constructs agent-centric heterogeneous graphs encoding communication, coverage, and spatial relations, and employs edge-aware multi-head attention to extract structural embeddings for policy optimization under a decentralized execution, centralized training scheme. In a constrained multi-target coverage scenario, GE-HAPPO improves coverage efficiency by 29.8%, task completion rate by 267%, and reduces island collisions by 71.4% compared to the baseline framework, demonstrating its effectiveness in structurally complex, constraint-rich multi-agent coordination tasks (This work was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China under Grant 62303297, the Shanghai Sailing Program under Grant 23YF1413100, the Open Research Project of the State Key Laboratory of Industrial Control Technology, China, under Grant ICT2024B40, and Shanghai Technical Service Center of Science and Engineering Computing, Shanghai University.). © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.

title: Flocking Control for Cucker-Smale Model under Data Privacy-Preserving Constraints
authors: Shao, Jinliang; Shi, Lei; Zheng, Wei Xing; Sun, Zhiyong; Liu, Qingchen
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Flocking is an essential ability for agent clusters to complete tasks in real-world scenarios. However, the data exchanged among agents during flocking may disclose their private information. This paper aims to investigate the flocking control problem for the Cucker-Smale model under data privacy-preserving constraints. The core idea of the proposed scheme is to inject privacy-preserving factors into the states transmitted by each agent. In addition, a weight function that depends on the masked information is designed to generate the edge weights of the interaction topology, which characterize the influence degree between agents. For the privacy-preserving Cucker-Smale model, three essential features defined by Reynolds for achieving flocking are studied, i.e., velocity matching, non-collision, and aggregate motion. Algebraic conditions are established to ensure flocking without compromising the privacy of the initial states of agents, and the performance of the privacy-preserving scheme is analyzed against both malicious agents inside the network and eavesdroppers outside the network. Finally, numerical examples and a semi-physical experiment are provided to verify the theoretical results. Note to Practitioners - This paper is motivated by the need to coordinate multiple autonomous agents, such as uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) and mobile robots, when their state information has to be exchanged over wireless networks. In many practical missions, exchanged positions and velocities may reveal sensitive information that compromises agent's privacy. This paper provides a privacy-preserving flocking control method that enables agents to achieve coordinated group motion while reducing the risk of exposing private state information. The proposed method can be implemented by injecting specially designed privacy-preserving factors into the transmitted data, without changing the basic distributed interaction structure of the flocking controller. From an engineering perspective, the results provide useful design guidelines for balancing three practical requirements: velocity coordination, collision avoidance, and data privacy. The effectiveness of the method is illustrated through numerical simulations and a semi-physical Crazyflie-based UAV experiment. © 2004 IEEE.

title: Route Optimization for Autonomous Drone-based Blood Delivery Using a Hybrid Intelligent Algorithm
authors: Hou, Jun; Chen, Xin; Chen, Lina; Liu, Fan
venue: Lecture Notes in Electrical Engineering
abstract: The emergence of the Low-altitude Economy, driven by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), offers a transformative solution for time-critical logistics, particularly in healthcare. This paper addresses the complex route optimization problem for autonomous drone-based blood delivery, a critical challenge in ensuring rapid emergency medical response. We first formulate the problem as a comprehensive mathematical model, the Multi-Drone Blood Delivery Routing Problem (MD-BDRP), which incorporates realistic operational constraints such as non-linear, payload-dependent energy consumption, vehicle capacity limits, and service time windows. To solve this NP-hard problem, we design and implement a novel hybrid intelligent algorithm, HGA-VNS, which synergizes the global exploration capabilities of a Genetic Algorithm (GA) with the powerful local search of a Variable Neighborhood Search (VNS). Extensive computational experiments, based on a real-world case study in Nanjing, China, are conducted to validate the effectiveness of our approach. The results demonstrate that HGA-VNS significantly outperforms a baseline genetic algorithm in both solution quality and stability. Furthermore, our parametric analysis provides actionable insights into the critical trade-offs between key operational parameters, such as fleet size, total cost, and energy safety thresholds, offering a robust decision-support framework for the practical and economic deployment of autonomous drone delivery systems. © Beijing Paike Culture Commu. Co., Ltd. 2026.

title: Simulating Public Ecological Product Supply Systems: An Agent-Based Model Integrating Government, Enterprises, Public and ENGO
authors: Dong, Yuchen; You, Weijia
venue: Sustainability (Switzerland)
abstract: Public ecological products constitute the most fundamental public goods supporting human well-being. Enhancing the high-quality supply of public ecological products is critical for maintaining ecological safety, ensuring the ecological regulation function, and promoting the harmonious coexistence of humans and nature. To deeply investigate the supply process and behavioral mechanisms of public ecological products, this study constructs a simulation model based on Agent-Based Modeling (ABM) to simulate the behavior rules and dynamic processes of four main subjects involved in the supply of public ecological products: government, enterprises, the public, and environmental non-governmental organizations (ENGOs). After calibrating the model parameters with relevant data from the water production and supply industry in Beijing, the good fit of the model output results verifies the effectiveness of the model. This study reveals the operating mechanism of multi-subject collaborative supply of public ecological products, providing a basic model for investigating the mechanism and evolution process of ecological product supply under more complex conditions, and also providing a powerful tool for the ex-ante evaluation of the implementation effect of public ecological product supply policies. © 2025 by the authors.

title: FORMIGA: a fleet management framework for sustainable human–robot collaboration in field robotics
authors: Yalcinkaya, Beril; Couceiro, Micael S.; Soares, Salviano; Valente, António
venue: Frontiers in Robotics and AI
abstract: Robotic fleet management systems are increasingly vital for sustainable operations in agriculture, forestry, and other field domains where labor shortages, efficiency, and environmental concerns intersect. We present FORMIGA, a fleet management framework that integrates human operators and autonomous robots into a collaborative ecosystem. FORMIGA combines standardised communication through the Robot Operating System with a user-centered interface for monitoring and intervention, while also leveraging large language models to generate executable task code from natural language prompts. The framework was deployed and validated within the FEROX project, a European initiative addressing sustainable berry harvesting in remote environments. In simulation-based trials, FORMIGA demonstrated adaptive task allocation, reduced operator workload, and faster task completion compared to semi-autonomous control, enabling dynamic labor division between humans and robots. By enhancing productivity, supporting worker safety, and promoting resource-efficient operations, FORMIGA contributes to the economic, and environmental dimensions of sustainability, offering a transferable tool for advancing human–robot collaboration in field robotics. Copyright © 2026 Yalcinkaya, Couceiro, Soares and Valente.

title: Integrated Approach to Marine Engine Maintenance Optimization: Weibull Analysis, Markov Chains, and DEA Model
authors: Budimir, Damir; Medić, Dario; Ružić, Vlatka; Kulej, Mateja
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
abstract: This study addresses the growing need for predictive maintenance in the maritime industry by proposing an optimized strategy for ship engine maintenance. The aim is to reduce unplanned failures that cause significant financial losses and disrupt global logistics flows. The methodology integrates Weibull reliability analysis, Markov chains, and Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA). A dataset of 512 diesel engine components from container ships was analysed, where the Weibull distribution (β = 1.8; α = 18,500 h) accurately modelled failure patterns, and Markov chains captured transitions between operational states (normal, degraded, failure). DEA was used to evaluate the efficiency of different maintenance strategies. Results indicate that targeting interventions in the degraded state significantly reduces downtime and improves component reliability, particularly for high-pressure fuel pumps and turbochargers. Optimizing maintenance extended the Mean Time to Failure (MTTF) up to 22,000 h and reduced the proportion of failures in critical components from 64.3% to 40%. These findings support a transition from reactive to proactive maintenance models, contributing to enhanced fleet availability, safety, and cost-effectiveness. The approach provides a quantitative foundation for predictive maintenance planning, with potential application in fleet management systems and smart ship platforms. © 2025 by the authors.

title: A Decentralized Potential Field-Based Self-Organizing Control Framework for Trajectory, Formation, and Obstacle Avoidance of Fully Autonomous Swarm Robots
authors: Abdel-Nasser, Mohammed; El-Ferik, Sami; Rashad, Ramy; Saif, Abdul-Wahid A.
venue: Robotics
abstract: In this work, we propose a fully decentralized, self-organizing control framework for a swarm of autonomous ground mobile robots. The system integrates potential field-based mechanisms for simultaneous trajectory tracking, formation control, and obstacle avoidance, all based on local sensing and neighbor interactions without centralized coordination. Each robot autonomously computes attractive, repulsive, and formation forces to navigate toward target positions while maintaining inter-robot spacing and avoiding both static and dynamic obstacles. Inspired by biological swarm behavior, the controller emphasizes robustness, scalability, and flexibility. The proposed method has been successfully validated in the ARGoS simulator, which provides realistic physics, sensor modeling, and a robust environment that closely approximates real-world conditions. The system was tested with up to 15 robots and is designed to scale to larger swarms (e.g., 100 robots), demonstrating stable performance across a range of scenarios. Results obtained using ARGoS confirm the swarm’s ability to maintain formation, avoid collisions, and reach a predefined goal area within a configurable 1 m radius. This zone serves as a spatial convergence region suitable for multi-robot formation, even in the presence of unknown fixed obstacles and movable agents. The framework can seamlessly handle the addition or removal of swarm members without reconfiguration. © 2025 by the authors.

title: Integrated order splitting, allocation, and delivery problem with a synchronized truck and drone fleet
authors: Yang, Ruiguang; Li, Xiangyong
venue: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review
abstract: In this paper, we study the integrated order splitting, allocation, and delivery problem with a synchronized fleet of trucks and drones (OSADP-STD), a pervasive challenge in the online retail industry that presents significant operational complexities for retailers. By leveraging inventories spread across multiple geographi- cally distributed fulfillment centers, retailers use a fleet of trucks and drones to collaboratively fulfill customer orders, which may consist of one or multiple products. The successful execution of the OSADP-STD relies heavily on the strict coordination and synchronization of the fulfillment resources. We first present a mixed integer linear programming model for the OSADP-STD, which poses significant challenges in obtaining high- quality solutions within reasonable time. To tackle these challenges, we propose a heuristic based on adaptive large neighborhood search. We then validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach through extensive experiments. We finally present sensitivity analyses that demonstrate how the integrated fulfillment strategy can optimize order fulfillment performance, providing a more cost-effective solution and highlighting the key factors that influence a retailer's fulfillment operations. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd

title: Entity-Aware Spatiotemporal MAPPO: A Multi-UAV Cooperative Navigation Framework Based on Asymmetric Artificial Potential Fields
authors: Yang, Junzhe; Yao, Pingqing
venue: 2026 International Conference on Image, Signal Processing and Pattern Recognition, ISPP 2026
abstract: Multi-UAV cooperative navigation in highly dynamic environments presents critical challenges in modern autonomous robotics. Traditional Artificial Potential Fields (APF) often converge to local optima, whereas standard Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) methods struggle with long-term spatiotemporal reasoning, yielding high collision rates and erratic maneuvers. This paper proposes an Entity-Aware Spatiotemporal Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) framework. To process complex kinematic histories, we introduce a Spatiotemporal Attention Mechanism integrating inverse distance physical priors and temporal positional encoding, alongside a Safe Radius Masking technique to eliminate NaN gradient explosions. Furthermore, an Asymmetric APF reward shaping scheme applies distinct repulsive forces for obstacles versus teammates, optimizing safety and efficiency. Extensive tests demonstrate that our approach achieves superior success rates and faster convergence than baseline models. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Safety-boundary-aware time-varying formation control for multi-agent systems in unknown corridors
authors: Zhu, Dingqi; Lian, Zhi; Chen, Mou; Lin, Wen-Juan
venue: ISA Transactions
abstract: Safe traversal of multi-agent formations in constrained environments is essential for many cooperative robotic applications, yet existing methods often rely on accurate prior maps, which limit their applicability in unknown corridors. To overcome this challenge, this paper studies the safe traversal of multi-agent systems through unknown corridors using time-varying formations, where agents possess only coarse prior knowledge of the corridor and must rely on online perception to progressively refine environmental information. To ensure safety during traversal under such limited information, an online safety-boundary construction method is proposed to derive an inner safety envelope with an explicit margin that is theoretically guaranteed to lie within the true boundary. Unlike approaches that depend on local obstacle avoidance, we compute the time-varying formation parameters under the safety-boundary constraints to generate reference trajectories for all agents. Accurate tracking of the generated reference trajectories is achieved by designing a trajectory-tracking control law. Simulation results show that, while preserving the prescribed formation geometry with high accuracy, the proposed method efficiently utilizes the available corridor space, achieving an average corridor utilization rate of 96.2%[jls-end-space/]. © 2026 International Society of Automation. title: A Comprehensive Review of Reinforcement Learning Applications in Health Monitoring of Civil Infrastructures
authors: Ullegaddi, Ankit; Mohan, S.C.; Mahmoodian, Mojtaba; Chan, Ricky W. K.; Sidiq, Amir
venue: Structural Control and Health Monitoring
abstract: The concept of structural health monitoring (SHM) of civil infrastructure has evolved rapidly with the incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI). Although available literature mainly focuses on supervised and unsupervised learning to detect and classify damages, both are inherently limited in addressing sequential decision-making, optimization of long-term maintenance, adaptive sensing, and dynamic uncertainty handling. In comparison, reinforcement learning (RL) offers a policy-based framework that can learn optimal actions by interacting with changing structural and environmental circumstances. Although there is an increasing use of RL applications in SHM, there has not been a comprehensive and critical review of RL applications. This review paper critically evaluates RL approaches used in civil infrastructure SHM, which spans across sensor network optimization, energy management of internet of things (IoT)–based wireless sensor networks (WSNs), updating finite element models (FEMs), contact and noncontact damage detection, unmanned vehicle-based inspection, predictive maintenance planning, autonomous SHM and structural control, etc. The review traces the methodological development from tabular Q-learning to complex deep reinforcement learning (DRL), multiagent systems, hierarchical designs, and combined physics-informed systems. In each of these areas, RL shows a high potential in adaptive resource scheduling, enhanced damage localization, large-scale network maintenance planning, integration of digital twins, federated learning, edge intelligence, and smart infrastructure ecosystems. Nevertheless, a few inherent challenges that prevent large-scale applications, such as high-dimensional state-action spaces, complexity in reward engineering, sample inefficiency, lack of real-world validation, and lack of transferability to heterogeneous infrastructure types, are discussed. Most of the existing implementations are simulation-based or applied to lab-scale models and lack standardized validation procedures for field deployment. Future research should focus on physics-informed and risk-sensitive formulations of RL in safety-critical systems, as well as on scalable multiagent and hierarchical learning designs, transfer and federated learning to alleviate data scarcity and privacy limitations, uncertainty-aware safe exploration strategies, and enhanced interchangeability with IoT-enabled digital twin ecosystems. Through this review, academicians, researchers and industrial experts will get critical insights on RL-based SHM to transform into an intelligent, resilient, sustainable, and autonomous infrastructure monitoring. Copyright © 2026 Ankit Ullegaddi et al. Structural Control and Health Monitoring published by John Wiley & Sons Ltd.

title: ACF-MATD3 Formation Control for Multi-Agent Wheeled Mobile Robot Systems
authors: Hu, Zhanfeng; Gou, Junnian
venue: 2026 9th International Conference on Advanced Algorithms and Control Engineering, ICAACE 2026
abstract: Multi-agent wheeled mobile robot systems have been widely applied in tasks such as cooperative operations, environmental monitoring, and formation transportation. As such, formation control becomes an important topic to study for the area of unmanned systems. However, conventional formation control is based upon graph theory and consensus theory, requiring accurate modeling and complex mathematical analysis that restricts its flexibility in handling dynamic and high-dimensional settings. In this paper, the formation control problem is formulated as a multiagent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) problem, and an Action Consistency-Formation Multi-Agent Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (ACF-MATD3) algorithm is developed to address formation control in an obstacle-free environment. Based on a leader-follower scheme, the algorithm introduces the action consistency loss and the formation maintenance loss to improve the coordination between agents as well as the robustness of their formations. In the square formation task, compared to the original MATD3 algorithm, the proposed approach reduces the mean squared error (MSE) by approximately 28.9 % and the standard deviation by 81.6 %. In the formation transformation task, a multi-branch input fusion architecture achieves an overall 47.4 % reduction in collision rate with 4 2. 4 % drop in global MSE. Additionally, when combined with Adaptive B-Spline Network (ABSN), the collision rate drops to zero while the global MSE decreases by another 20.7 %. Simulation and real-world experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing deep reinforcement learning methods in terms of accuracy, stability, and robustness, indicating strong potential for practical engineering applications. © 2026 IEEE.

title: How safe are the United Kingdom's ports? A statistical analysis using accident data and AIS vessel movements
authors: Manole, Iulia; Majumdar, Arnab; Garcia Sinobas, Alberto
venue: Journal of Navigation
abstract: Maritime safety faces growing challenges due to an expanding global fleet, tighter schedules, and increasingly complex stakeholder interactions. This study integrates multiple data sources to determine a more accurate representation of major marine accident causative factors in the United Kingdom. Logistic regression and data modelling are applied to Automatic Identification System data (2011-2017) and reported accidents from the Marine Accident Investigation Branch (2013-2019). Results show that larger vessels, daytime transits, service ships, winter conditions, and confined high-density areas such as ports impact accident likelihood. Interviews validate the data and emphasize the influence of port geometry and channel complexity. Among major UK ports, London, Plymouth and Milford Haven exhibit the highest accident-to-traffic densities. While maritime regulations and safety management systems in ports and vessels are seen as adequate by industry professionals, human factors require the greatest attention to improve maritime safety. © The Author(s), 2025. Published by Cambridge University Press on behalf of The Royal Institute of Navigation.

title: Dynamic safety assessment of Autonomous Vehicle based on Multivariate Bayesian Inference (DyAVSA)
authors: Popov, Peter
venue: Journal of Reliable Intelligent Environments
abstract: This paper deals with the Bayesian safety assessment of autonomous vehicles (AV) using as a key safety measure the probability of catastrophic failure per mile of driving (pfm), assumed a random variable. The paper takes the view that pfm may (and typically will) vary due to changing road driving conditions. Accommodating this variation in a Bayesian inference on pfm requires one to use a multivariate probabilistic model whereby the changeable pfm is captured explicitly for the different driving conditions. The model that we use in this work is derived from our prior work and accounts for the uncertainties in both—the operational profile (i.e., the likelihood of the different driving conditions) and the pfms, conditional on the respective operating conditions. The concept of the “dynamic AV safety assessment (DyAVSA)” is presented in the work, too, whereby the Bayesian predictions used at run time rely on the operational data collected by a fleet of AVs. DyAVSA benefits both: (1) the AV vendors, for monitoring the safety changes of the entire AV fleet; (2) the owners/users of individual AVs, whose safety assessment is personalized and different from the assessment of the AV fleet. DyAVSA thus offers a major change in the AV safety management than is currently the case. It allows the AV users/owners to benefit from the aggregated safety relevant data collected from a fleet of AVs. Our findings show that the benefits from DyAVSA for the owners/operators of the individual AV instances may be significant: the safety predictions they can make by using the data collected by the entire fleet of AV instances and shared among them, may differ considerably from the predictions the AV instances would be able to make relying on own observations only. Sharing data would lead to a much more rapid reduction of uncertainty in the pfms than would be the case if the AV instances relied on their own observations only. The presented DyAVSA, based on a multivariate Bayesian safety assessment, can be applied to other complex intelligent systems such as robots, UAVs, etc. © The Author(s) 2025.

title: Dynamic Disassembly Planning of End-of-Life Products for Human–Robot Collaboration Enabled by Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Li, Weidong; Peng, Yiqun; Zhou, Yong; Pham, Duc Truong
venue: Springer Series in Advanced Manufacturing
abstract: DisassemblyDeep reinforcement learning is a critical stage in the remanufacturingRemanufacturingof end-of-lifeEnd of Life (EoL) (EoL) products. High labour costs and the limited capability of robots to perform intricate disassembly tasks have led to the growing adoption of human–robot collaboration (HRC) for disassembly operationsDisassembly operations. This chapter addresses a key challenge in HRC-based disassembly: the inherent uncertainty introduced by human behaviour. Such uncertainty arises when the time taken to complete a task and the sequence of tasks chosen by a human operator differ from the predefined disassembly plan, necessitating dynamic planning for subsequent tasks. To address this, Stackelberg equilibrium-enabled task assignment policies are proposed. Under these policies, the human leader selects tasks that maximise efficiency-related returns, based on the robot’s optimal response to the human’s choice. Acting as the follower, the robot selects tasks that maximise safety-related returns for each human decision. To determine the optimal policy values and ensure both safety and efficiency throughout the HRC-based disassembly process, an improved multi-agent proximal policy optimisation (i-MAPPOImproved Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimisation (i-MAPPO)) algorithm is developed. Finally, a case study involving the disassembly of an electric vehicle battery demonstrates that the proposed approach effectively adapts to human uncertainty with a high success rate, while maintaining short disassembly timesDisassembly Time (DT) and ensuring that the human–robot distance remains within the safety threshold throughout the process. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: PROCESSES AND CONTROL SYSTEMS: SYNTHESIS, MODELING, OPTIMIZATION
authors: Krasnikov, Igor
venue: PROCESSES AND CONTROL SYSTEMS: SYNTHESIS, MODELING, OPTIMIZATION
abstract: The collective monograph focuses on the study of modeling methods, analytical assessment and optimization of complex technical systems in industry and energy. The presented materials cover the tasks of heat transfer, operational reliability, mobile control, distributed energy and predictive monitoring, forming a holistic scientific and applied basis for the implementation of engineering solutions in real production conditions. The monograph is aimed at systematizing methods that ensure increased efficiency of technological facilities through mathematical analysis, digital measurements and adaptive control. The first section examines in detail the processes of secondary condensation in large-capacity ammonia synthesis units of the AM-1360 type. Special attention is paid to methods for experimental identification of thermophysical parameters that determine the operation of heat exchangers in unsteady modes. Refined mathematical models of heat transfer have been constructed and the influence of structural deviations on energy consumption parameters has been assessed. It is shown that the use of adaptive software control allows to adjust temperature profiles, reduce the load on refrigeration units and increase the resource of heat engineering equipment. The presented results can be taken into account during the modernization of technological lines of the chemical industry. The second section is devoted to the analysis of the operational reliability of transport systems based on large sets of statistical data. A methodology for detecting latent deviations and "repeated anomalies" that are not recorded by standard control means is proposed. An assessment of negative statistics and time trends is carried out, which allow to establish potential areas of infrastructure degradation. The feasibility of the transition from reactive maintenance to preventive management is substantiated, when decisions are based not on the fact of failure, but on early signs of its occurrence. This approach creates the basis for the implementation of predictive diagnostics systems in transport. The third section considers the issue of optimal regulation of azimuthal power plants of marine vessels. Based on parametric modeling, the influence of external disturbances and variable loads on the behavior of the ship complex was investigated. Adaptive controller structures were developed that ensure course stability, reduce energy consumption, and increase the accuracy of maneuvering operations. Criteria for selecting control laws for operating conditions where traditional PID methods lose their effectiveness were outlined. The results confirm the possibility of integrating new-type controllers into ship motion systems. The fourth section is devoted to the architecture of autonomous microgrid-class electric power systems. The principles of coordination between generation, storage, and consumption of electricity using multi-agent subsystems are considered. Mechanisms for maintaining stability in the event of loss of connection to the centralized network are substantiated, and the issue of load balancing in abnormal modes is also considered. The presented models demonstrate the possibility of forming a flexible energy infrastructure capable of providing guaranteed power supply to technological equipment without involving dispatch control. The fifth section presents approaches to predictive maintenance of metallurgical equipment using the example of the lining of induction crucible furnaces. The technology of 3D laser profiling is proposed for spatial reconstruction of the inner surface of the lining and determination of zones of marginal wear. Criteria for permissible deviation of geometry are established and a methodology for calculating the residual resource of the lining layer is developed. Practical results confirm that the transition to condition-based monitoring allows to reduce emergency downtime and economic losses associated with the destruction of working units. The summarized results of the monograph can be used during the design, adjustment and operation of automation systems, energy facilities and industrial units. The presented methods create the basis for the development of integrated control systems in which mathematical modeling is combined with digital monitoring and preventive intervention. The materials of the publication constitute a scientific contribution to the development of engineering practice, focused on increasing technological reliability and optimizing the life cycle of technical systems. © Author(s) 2025. All rights reserved.

title: Evaluation of multi-token MAC-cum-routing protocol in intelligent transportation system: Smart traffic management system
authors: Yoganathan, B.; Ramasamy Sankar Ram, C.
venue: Urban Mobility and Challenges of Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: Multitoken MAC-cum-Routing Protocols plays a vital role in Smart Traffic Management Systems (STMS) by reducing the congestion in Urban Areas. Generally Smart Traffic Management Systems are handled using the Wireless Sensor Networks with the help of Routing Protocols. Wireless Sensor Network consists of nodes which run on the battery power. The main challenges that are faced by the Wireless Sensor Networks are the lifetime of the node and the data integrity. By using Multitoken MAC-cum-Routing Protocols we can enhance the lifetime of the wireless sensor nodes and also we can achieve the data integrity. The Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming the Intelligent Transportation System (ITS) by enhancing efficiency, safety, and convenience. The important areas in which IoT plays a vital role are Fleet Management, Traffic Management, Public Transportation, Connected Cars, Smart Parking, Supply Chain and Logistics and Safety & Security. Hence the integration of IoT in transportation is leading to smarter, safer, and more efficient systems that benefit both operators and passengers. © 2025 by IGI Global Scientific Publishing.

title: Enhancing Critical Infrastructure Resilience: An Integrated Framework for Hazardous Material Management of Electric Vehicle Batteries
authors: Vukmirović, Dragan; Radojičić, Stefan; Stanojeveć, Nebojša; Dragović, Nebojša; Čomić, Tijana
venue: Advanced Sciences and Technologies for Security Applications
abstract: This paper addresses the “electrification paradox”: while electric vehicles (EVs) are vital for decarbonising transport, the rapidly growing wave of end-of-life (EoL) EV batteries creates a new, high-stakes hazardous waste stream that threatens the resilience of storage, transport and recycling infrastructures. We first synthesise the regulatory and scientific basis for treating EoL lithium-ion batteries as hazardous materials, highlighting the combined risks of toxic emissions, long-term environmental contamination, and acute thermal runaway events. Building on this risk profile, we propose an integrated technology framework that combines the Internet of Things (IoT), high-fidelity Digital Twins, and Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) to move from reactive, compliance-driven management to predictive, adaptive and resilient operations. Three detailed use cases—proactive thermal-runaway prevention in warehouses, dynamic rerouting of high-risk loads, and AI-assisted emergency response—illustrate how the framework senses, simulates, and responds to evolving hazards in real time. We then examine key implementation challenges, including cybersecurity, scalability, interoperability, explainability, human-in-the-loop governance and algorithmic fairness. Finally, we show how the same data backbone underpins a Digital Battery Passport that enables second-life markets, optimised recycling and alignment with emerging policy, positioning EoL batteries as traceable resources within a secure circular economy. We conclude by outlining future research directions in multi-agent control, quantum optimisation and end-to-end digital threads for critical materials. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: A Distributed Cooperative Control Framework for Dynamic Shape Formation and Obstacle Avoidance of Robot Swarms
authors: Hu, Yangtian
venue: 2026 8th International Conference on Information Science, Electrical and Automation Engineering, ISEAE 2026
abstract: To address the challenges of autonomous pattern generation, configuration maintenance, and collision-free motion for multi-agent robot swarms in complex obstacle environments, this paper proposes a distributed formation control framework that integrates image-based shape matching, distributed state consensus, and multi-command cooperative control. Based on a single-integrator dynamic model, the framework constructs neighbor perception topologies, uses dual consensus on position and orientation, and linearly fuses four control inputs - shape entering, regional exploration, inter-robot interaction, and obstacle avoidance - to achieve rapid convergence of robot swarms from initial states to user-defined target shapes. It further supports safe coordinated motion under static obstacle constraints. A full simulation platform was developed in MATLAB with a swarm of 30 robots and the letter "A"as the target formation. Results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves 100% coverage and entering rates within 13 seconds. The uniformity index stabilizes at approximately 1.5, and robot trajectories exhibit smooth obstacle circumnavigation without collisions or fragmentation. This validates the effectiveness, robustness, and environmental adaptability of the method, providing theoretical support and technical references for engineering applications such as unmanned aerial vehicle swarms and autonomous mobile robot formations. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Research on One-to-Many Pickup and Delivery Vehicle Routing Optimization Method Considering Three-Dimensional Loading
authors: Shen, Jiayi; Zhang, Yinggui
venue: Sustainability (Switzerland)
abstract: Simultaneous optimization of vehicle routing and cargo loading is essential for reducing operational costs and improving the environmental performance of logistics systems. To overcome the limitations of traditional sequential approaches to the one-to-many pickup and delivery vehicle routing problem with three-dimensional loading constraints (3L-PDVRP), this paper proposes a deeply coupled hybrid genetic algorithm (HGA). The algorithm adopts a grouping-based genetic encoding strategy to accommodate variable fleet sizes and incorporates a tree-search-based loading module. A dynamic three-dimensional loading feasibility verification mechanism is embedded directly into the evolutionary search so that routing decisions are continuously guided by fragility, stacking stability, support constraints, and other loading constraints. In addition, an adaptive hybrid insertion strategy is employed to balance global exploration and local exploitation during route construction and repair. Extensive computational experiments on extended benchmark instances derived from standard datasets show that the proposed method consistently outperforms a large neighborhood search (LNS)-based baseline from the literature, reducing the average total travel distance by 10.60% and increasing the average vehicle loading rate by 2.76%. These results indicate that the proposed HGA provides an effective approach to the synergistic optimization of routing and loading in one-to-many distribution settings, offering practical value for lowering transportation costs and supporting more sustainable logistics operations. This methodology provides decision support for logistics enterprises, reducing travel distances while ensuring three-dimensional loading feasibility, thereby enabling greener and safer transportation operations. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Safe Navigation and Formation Control for UAV Swarms Under Wind Disturbances
authors: Nikolakakis, Vasilis; Eqtami, Alina
venue: EEITE 2026 - 7th International Conference in Electronic Engineering and Information Technology
abstract: The deployment of autonomous multi-UAV swarms in complex, dynamic environments requires robust navigation strategies that ensure both formation integrity and collision avoidance. This paper presents a decentralized, reactive planning framework for multi-agent systems operating under continuous aerodynamic disturbances, such as wind gusts. Building upon existing CLF-CBF-QP-based control formulations, the proposed approach focuses on implementation-oriented aspects, emphasizing physical feasibility and real-time execution. Leveraging an optimization-based architecture, the framework utilizes Control Lyapunov Functions (CLFs) for trajectory generation and Robust Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) as a real-time safety filter against dynamic obstacles and inter-agent collisions. To account for unpredictable wind disturbances, a robustness margin is explicitly incorporated into the safety constraints, ensuring physically executable and safe avoidance maneuvers. The decentralized scheme is evaluated through simulation studies, demonstrating the swarm's ability to elastically reconfigure its formation to bypass dynamic threats while maintaining safety clearances. The results highlight the practical applicability of the framework for real-world robotic operations. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Fusing a Slimming Network and Large Language Models for Intelligent Decision Support in Industrial Safety and Preventive Monitoring
authors: Tian, Weijun; Yin, Jia; Wang, Wei; Guo, Zhonghua; Zhu, Liqiang; Li, Jianbo
venue: Electronics (Switzerland)
abstract: Intelligent personnel safety management is a critical component of smart manufacturing infrastructure. This paper presents an integrated framework combining a structurally optimized neural network (enhanced with spatial and channel feature fusion mechanisms for multi-scale detection) with an agent-based large language model (LLM) enhanced with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) capabilities for factory safety monitoring. The visual detection component employs the Similarity-Aware Channel Pruning (SACP) method for automated, performance-preserving compression by identifying and suppressing redundant channels based on similarity and norm regularization, while the agent-based LLM with RAG capabilities dynamically integrates real-time violation data with established safety management protocols to generate precise diagnostic reports and operational recommendations. The optimized network achieves real-time violation detection in parallel video streams, and the LLM-powered assistant facilitates intelligent decision-making through natural language querying. Extensive evaluations on multiple benchmark datasets and a real-world safety helmet detection dataset demonstrate the scheme’s superior performance in both accuracy and practical applicability for industrial deployment. © 2025 by the authors.

title: Formation flying and constellation missions using nanosatellites: A comprehensive review of mission architectures, technology enablers and future trends
authors: Rallabandi, Ramamurthy Hanumath Bhanu; Balakrishnan, Varunkumar
venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers, Part G: Journal of Aerospace Engineering
abstract: This comprehensive review analyzes 53 successful multi-nanosatellite missions between 2016 and 2024, all operational over 6 months from established databases, representing 775 satellites enumerated individually in Table 1, across commercial Earth-observation fleets (Planet Labs Flock/SuperDove, 10 batches; Spire Global Lemur-2, 12 batches), IoT constellations (Swarm Technologies SpaceBEE, 10 batches), and smaller scientific, technology-demonstration and educational clusters. Rapid advances in CubeSat technologies have significantly expanded the range of feasible multi-satellite mission architectures. Missions are classified into three architectures: Strictly Controlled Formation (n = 2, 4%), Constellation Formation (n = 35, 66%), and Swarm/Cluster Formation (n = 16, 30%). By primary application the corpus comprises Earth Observation (n = 28), IoT/Telecommunications (n = 12), Technology Demonstration (n = 6), Scientific Research (n = 5) and Geodesy & Education (n = 2). All shares reported in this review are mission-weighted unless a satellite-weighted basis is stated explicitly. Technological enablers critically assessed include GPS relative navigation achieving <1 m accuracy (CanX-4/5 heritage), NanoFEEP low-thrust propulsion for formation maintenance and 25-year deorbit compliance when incorporated into an appropriate end-of-life disposal strategy consistent with international debris mitigation guidelines, and swarm intelligence enabling autonomous task allocation. The end-to-end operational lifecycle from PSLV-C37 record-setting 88-satellite Flock-3p deployment through 200 Mbps SuperDove imaging pipelines to Hybrid Adaptive Reconfigurable Fault Tolerance (HARFT) radiation-resilient architectures is systematically mapped. Operational challenges spanning power constraints, collision avoidance, and scalability are systematically paired with validated mitigations across mission scales. A novel decision framework is proposed to guide architecture selection by matching science objectives to GNC complexity levels. Synthesizing operational insights from record-setting commercial constellations and precision scientific formations, this review establishes the complete formation flying design-to-operation methodology, projecting pathways toward hybrid autonomous networks, robotic servicing, and sustainable LEO infrastructure. © IMechE 2026

title: Multi-Agent Cooperative Pursuit Based on Permutation Invariance and Task Decomposition
authors: Yang, Kun; Chen, Kaixi; Deng, Fang; Chen, Chen
venue: Unmanned Systems
abstract: Multi-agent pursuit-evasion has significant applications in military, transportation, and industrial sectors. This task faces dual challenges of uncertain swarm scale and environmental uncertainty within unstructured dynamic environments. To address these, we propose a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework based on permutation invariance to balance pursuit efficiency and collision avoidance safety. First, in the evaluation stage, we introduce a hybrid feature aggregation mechanism based on the DeepSets structure and a predicted intercept point auxiliary task. By extracting permutation-invariant group features and introducing kinematic priors, this approach achieves zero-shot transfer and rapid convergence of the method across different swarm scales. Second, in the execution stage, we construct a residual gating architecture based on task decomposition. This architecture utilizes a frozen basic tracking stream to handle the global game and employs a conditioned residual stream with a dynamic gating mechanism to manage local obstacle avoidance, effectively resolving the multi-objective conflict problem under sparse rewards. Finally, extensive simulations and physical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method, after training on small-scale swarms, achieves robust zero-shot transfer to medium and large-scale swarms, completing efficient and stable pursuit tasks. Furthermore, the method was successfully transferred to a physical platform, completing tasks smoothly even in the presence of faulty agents, thereby validating its applicability in the real world. © 2028 World Scientific Publishing Company.

title: Digital Twin Approach for Ship Energy Management
authors: Bonvicini, A.; Cangelosi, D.; Ingargiola, R.; Marchese, A.; Previti, G.
venue: Progress in Marine Science and Technology
abstract: In response to the increasing demand for greener and more efficient maritime solutions, Fincantieri has placed digital transformation and sustainability at the core of its strategic objectives. To support this mission, CETENA has developed an advanced onboard energy management system, called ASSIST ENERGY, that leverages digital twin technology to optimize ship operations and enhance decision-making. The system integrates seamlessly with ship automation frameworks to collect and analyze operational data, offering comprehensive insights into the vessel’s energy performance. Central to this solution is a sophisticated simulator that reproduces the ship’s energy behavior through agent-based modeling. This approach allows for detailed representation and interaction of individual components, enabling accurate predictions of system behavior under varying operational scenarios. A key innovation of the platform is its use of machine learning algorithms to identify optimal operational strategies, reduce energy consumption, and improve overall vessel efficiency. These algorithms dynamically adjust parameters based on real-time and historical data, enabling a continuous feedback loop for performance optimization. The collected data are accessible through user-friendly web platform available both onboard and onshore via cloud integration. This platform empowers ship operators and fleet managers with actionable insights, fostering data-driven decision-making processes. CETENA’s research efforts extend beyond shipboard operations through its participation in the MISSION project, aimed at integrating ship systems with port operations. By promoting just-in-time arrivals, this initiative minimizes port waiting times, optimizes speed profiles, and enhances navigational safety, contributing to the overall sustainability of maritime logistics. This paper discusses examples of simulation methodologies and optimization strategies in CETENA ASSIST ENERGY. Furthermore, it highlights the role of digital twins and machine learning in achieving sustainable maritime operations. © 2025 IOS Press.

title: Safety-Aware Multi-Robot Scheduling Under Time-Critical Constraints: A Colored Traveling Salesman Problem Approach
authors: Duan, Yaxing; Li, Jun
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: The Colored Traveling Salesman Problem (CTSP) is a seminal generalization of the Multiple TSP, where colors represent the heterogeneity of salesmen and their city visits. This work presents a time-critical extension, termed the Time-Critical CTSP (T-CTSP). By emphasizing the timing of visits, T-CTSP explicitly captures spatio-temporal behaviors of agents, enabling the modeling of multi-agent path planning and scheduling in time-critical, safety-aware applications. A distance constraint is incorporated to ensure safe separation between salesmen and to prevent inter-agent conflicts. To solve large-scale instances, we propose a Beam Variable Neighborhood Search (BeamVNS) algorithm that integrates graph sparsification, greedy initialization, swap search, beam insertion, temporal coordination, and route-segment reconstruction. Graph sparsification reduces complexity by constructing a sparse city network, whereas a defined sequential insertion neighborhood has been theoretically proven to fully cover the solution space. Combined with a truncated tree search, this facilitates efficient beam-guided exploration. Extensive experiments validate the proposed formulation and demonstrate that BeamVNS outperforms baseline methods adapted for T-CTSP. Finally, T-CTSP and BeamVNS are applied to multi-robot 3D printing and rebar mesh welding, proving their effectiveness in optimizing complex robotic manufacturing processes. Note to Practitioners - This work is motivated by practical challenges in safety-aware multi-robot coordination. The proposed time-critical colored traveling salesman problem provides a unified mathematical formulation that simultaneously captures routing decisions, temporal coordination, and safety-distance constraints. The beam variable neighborhood search is developed to address the large-scale T-CTSP instances. Extensive experiments demonstrate that BeamVNS can provide high-quality and safety-aware operational plans for decision-makers. For practitioners, this framework can serve as a planning tool for multi-robot task scheduling and path planning in manufacturing and automation systems. Case studies in multi-robot 3D printing and rebar mesh welding further verify that the proposed approach effectively ensures collision avoidance among robots and significantly improves operational efficiency. © 2004 IEEE.

title: Reinforcement Learning Based AGV Path Planning
authors: Zhou, Yusun; Yin, Rui; Chen, Xianfu; Zhou, Zhuo; Wu, Celimuge; Tian, Yuping
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing, ICICC 2026
abstract: The multi-Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV) system is an important component of intelligent manufacturing, but currently faces the challenge of dynamic path planning. This paper proposes a multi-AGV path planning methodology based on a two-tier architecture that integrates Petri nets and Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO). Specifically, the Petri net employs place and token mechanisms to preemptively prevent AGV conflicts, thereby furnishing safety constraints for the path planning process. Within this framework, MAPPO undertakes the dynamic path planning task, adopting a Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution (CTDE) architecture. By modeling intersection nodes as individual agents, the approach decouples the complexity of the state space from the number of AGVs. Furthermore, a novel reward function is devised that incorporates inter-node travel time, balancing instantaneous congestion avoidance with goal-oriented guidance. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method yields higher task completion efficiency within the system, showing relatively better performance particularly in scenarios with higher AGV densities. These preliminary simulation results suggest its potential scalability and indicate possible value for future industrial applications. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Distributed Formation Control for Multi-Agents
authors: Yuan, Zhidong; Zhang, Xuxiu; Zhao, Xinyu
venue: Advances in Transdisciplinary Engineering
abstract: This study proposes a distributed formation control framework for multi-agent systems by integrating deep reinforcement learning (DRL) with interdisciplinary methodologies from control theory, robotics, and artificial intelligence. Aimed at addressing collaborative formation challenges in dynamic environments, the approach uses graph-theoretic modeling for formation-keeping and obstacle avoidance and dynamic Attention-based Advantage Actor-Critic (DA-A2C) algorithm to solve collaborative formation problems in dynamic environments like autonomous drone swarms and robotic fleets. To balance formation consistency and obstacle repulsion, this strategy optimizes neighbor perception dynamic weight allocation using the dynamic ω-zone mechanism. Experimental validations in simulated environments with static/moving obstacles show superior performance over SA2C, MATD3, and DDPG baselines, covering formation control and obstacle avoidance in complex situations and outperforming other algorithms in adaptability and robustness. This research can improve cross-domain applications in intelligent transportation, industrial automation, and emergency response systems. The method works in multi-robot formation systems, and future study will focus on 3D environment generalization and efficient communication protocols. © 2025 IOS Press.

title: SCALE-COMM: Shared, Contrastively-Aligned Latent Embeddings for MARL Communication
authors: Abouelyazid, Mahmoud; Hammad, Eman
venue: IEEE Intelligent Vehicles Symposium, Proceedings
abstract: Emergent communication enables partially observant Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) to coordinate effectively in decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) settings. However, existing approaches often struggle with unstable communication protocols, ungrounded message semantics, and interference between communication learning and policy optimization, leading to degraded coordination over time. We propose SCALE-COMM (Shared, Contrastively-Aligned Latent Embeddings for COMMunication), a self-supervised framework for learning compact, stable, and policy-relevant communication representations. SCALE-COMM decouples communication learning from policy optimization by training low-dimensional latent messages that capture task-relevant planning and traffic information, while enforcing consistency across agents and time. Across standard MARL benchmarks and a realistic warehouse coordination task, SCALE-COMM consistently outperforms existing communication frameworks in both representation quality and task performance. The learned communication space yields improved stability, sample efficiency, and throughput under policy fine-tuning, demonstrating the effectiveness of representation-driven communication for scalable multi-agent coordination. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Distributed Safe Navigation for Multi-Robot Systems With Fixed-Time Convergence and Deadlock Resolution
authors: Yin, Jia-Yuan; Yang, Guang-Hong; Wang, Huimin; Wang, Jun-Sheng
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: —This letter addresses the problem of distributed safe navigation for multi-robot systems (MRSs), proposing a comprehensive framework that unifies safety-critical control, real-time navigation, and deadlock resolution. To enable a fully distributed implementation of control barrier function (CBF)-based safety, this work employs a regularized primal decomposition to decouple inter-agent safety constraints. A novel distributed Fixed-Time Stable Gradient Flow (FxTS-GF) algorithm is then designed, which enables each robot to complete the optimal safety responsibility allocation and efficiently solve its local quadratic program (QP) for collision avoidance within each control cycle. Furthermore, the framework incorporates a distributed deadlock resolution mechanism that breaks undesired equilibria through coordination among neighboring robots. Theoretical guarantees are provided for the framework’s anytime-safety, optimality, and fixed-time stability. Finally, the effectiveness and practical applicability of the proposed method are validated through both simulations and hardware experiments on a team of mobile vehicles. © 2026 IEEE. All rights reserved,

title: Robust Multiagent Combinatorial Path Finding
authors: Kidushim, Yehonatan; Natan, Avraham; Stern, Roni; Kalech, Meir
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Consider a system of multiple physical agents tasked with collaboratively collecting a set of spatially distributed goals as quickly as possible while avoiding collisions with the environment and with each other. This type of problem, which involves Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) and task allocation, is called Multi-Agent Combinatorial Path Finding (MCPF). Prior work on MCPF assumed each agent has a final goal it must reach, there are no orientation constraints on the agents’ movements, and the agents will follow their planned actions as intended. These assumptions rarely hold in real physical robots, which limits the applicability of existing MCPF algorithms in practical applications. We propose the Robust CBSS framework, a robust planning approach that solves MCPF without the aforementioned simplifying assumptions, and provide two implementations: a baseline version (RCbssBase) and an efficient version (RCbss-Eff ). RCbssEff generalizes the Conflict-Based Steiner Search (CBSS) algorithm, building on ideas from the p-Robust CBS algorithm and algorithms for solving the Equality Generalized Traveling Salesman Problem. We prove that RCbssEff is complete and can be configured to return optimal solutions. Experimental results on benchmark MCPF problems show that RCbssEff balances planning time, solution cost, and collision reduction compared to baselines. © 2026, Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (www.aaai.org). All rights reserved.

title: Swarm Robotics Collaborative Architecture Based on Embodied Cognition: A Survey From Emergence to Intelligent Decision-Making
authors: Xu, Wan; Liu, Zheng; Yang, Chen-Xiao; Nie, Ao; Zhang, Hai-Tao
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Against a backdrop of rising automation demands and fundamental scientific challenges, this paper examines the driving factors and technological bottlenecks that constrain the iterative development of swarm-robot systems. To address these challenges, we introduce a group-embodied cognitive-synergy paradigm based on the progressive integration of emergence, planning, and cognition. The proposed architecture outlines a clear evolutionary pathway for distributed automation control: a bottom layer grounded in emergent mechanisms of swarm intelligence arising from local interactions, a middle layer of structured control centered on geometric constraints, and a top layer of collaborative decision-making driven by multi-agent reinforcement learning and game theory. Within this framework, representative technical methods are mapped to typical application scenarios such as search and rescue, flexible logistics, and precision formation control, and the resulting trade-offs among scalability, real-time performance, robustness, and verifiability are systematically summarized. Based on this integrated analysis, we argue that future development should focus on achieving a careful balance among the robustness of bottom-layer emergence mechanisms, the effectiveness of middle-layer structural constraints, and the adaptability of top-layer decision-making. This study aims to provide researchers with a systematic collaborative framework and insights into the future development of intelligent autonomous systems. Note to Practitioners - To ensure the reliability and efficiency of distributed robotic systems, addressing the problem of group integration is essential. Our study, 'Swarm Robotics Collaborative Architecture Based on Embodied Cognition: A Survey from Emergence to Intelligent Decision-Making,' examines the integrated pathway from bottom-layer emergent control to top-layer intelligent decision-making. The paper offers systematic architectural reference for practitioners by examining performance trade-offs in typical scenarios, including industrial logistics and search-and-rescue operations. By clarifying how to balance the robustness of underlying interaction mechanisms with the adaptability of high-level decision-making, this work aims to help industry professionals overcome key technical bottlenecks and deploy advanced swarm intelligence technologies in complex real-world engineering environments. © 2004-2012 IEEE.

title: Driver Behavior–Based Intelligent System for Traffic Accident Detection and Early Warning
authors: Ai, Duong Huu; Nguyen, van Loi; Luong, Khanh Ty
venue: International Journal of Robotics and Control Systems
abstract: This study presents an intelligent system for traffic accident detection and early warning based on driver behavior analysis. A driver behavior–based intelligent system for traffic accident detection and early warning operates by continuously monitoring the driver’s actions using cameras and vehicle sensors. It collects real-time data such as eye movements, head pose, steering patterns, and acceleration signals. Advanced deep learning models such as YOLO and recurrent neural networks analyze these features to detect fatigue, distraction, or abnormal driving behavior. The system then evaluates the risk level based on predefined thresholds and contextual traffic conditions. When the risk exceeds a safety limit, it generates early warnings to prevent potential accidents. It is widely applied in smart vehicles, fleet management systems, and advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS). It helps monitor driver fatigue, distraction, and risky behaviors in real time to improve road safety. In commercial transportation, it supports logistics companies by reducing accident rates and operational costs. Experimental results show improved detection accuracy, high precision–recall performance, and reduced false alarms under diverse driving conditions. Overall, the system contributes to fewer traffic accidents, enhanced driver awareness, and more reliable intelligent transportation systems. © 2025 The Authors.

title: Designing Agentic AI Experiences: UX Strategies for Collaborative, Human-Centered AI
authors: Yocco, Victor
venue: Designing Agentic AI Experiences: UX Strategies for Collaborative, Human-Centered AI
abstract: The era of the passive digital tool is ending. Software is becoming an active partner capable of autonomy, thanks to Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI). This evolution presents User Experience (UX) professionals with new challenges and demands a fundamental change in UX design. UX must evolve from designing screens to choreographing relationships. Designing Agentic AI Experiences provides a practical framework for building AI partners that users trust. This book bridges the gap between psychological theory and interface practice. It empowers UX designers and researchers to lead the integration of AI into products that respect human dignity and build trust between user and system. Readers of this book will learn to: * Design Trust: Use the Trust Battery model to measure and maintain user confidence over time * Define Personality: Craft Agent Personas and Relationship Archetypes that align with user expectations * Structure Delegation: Implement the Ladder of Autonomy to guide users from simple suggestions to fully automated actions * Ensure Safety: Deploy Circuit Breakers and feedback loops that prevent errors and keep the human in control * Scale Strategy: Establish an Agentic Center of Excellence to govern multi-agent ecosystems across the enterprise The technology is ready. The challenge is no longer building intelligence behind the interface but designing the partnership. This book shows you how. © 2027 Victor Yocco.

title: Obstacle avoidance adaptive coverage control using collective initial excitation
authors: Surendhar, S.; Roy, Sayan Basu; Bhasin, Shubhendu
venue: IFAC-PapersOnLine
abstract: This paper introduces the obstacle avoidance adaptive coverage control for the mobile sensor network (MSN). In addition to obstacle avoidance, parameter convergence of the unknown spatial sensory function is guaranteed under the mild excitation condition termed collective initial excitation (C-IE). The proportional-integral (PI) type adaptation enables the multi-agents to achieve convergence and consensus under a less stringent excitation condition than collective persistence of excitation (C-PE). The proposed coverage algorithm is evaluated through simulation. © 2025 Elsevier B.V.. All rights reserved.

title: Dynamic Resource Reservation using Deep Reinforcement Learning: Optimizing Resource Allocation for Platoon-Based C-V2X Networks
authors: Khan, Irshad; Haladappa, Manjula Sunkadakatte
venue: Engineering Letters
abstract: The rapid growth of wireless technologies for short-range communication highlights the critical need for efficient resource management in Cellular Vehicle-to-Everything (C-V2X) networks. Operating within the Fifth Generation (5G) technology framework, these networks improve system performance through direct device-to-device interaction and resource allocation among mobile users and proximate devices. However, effectively allocating resources in V2X networks remains a challenging issue with current methods. This study introduces Dynamic Resource Reservation with Deep Reinforcement Learning (DR2-DRL), a novel approach leveraging a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework to mitigate packet collisions in vehicular networks. DR2-DRL aids vehicles in making intelligent radio resource selections. An enhanced attention-based technique is applied to increase training efficiency, enabling vehicles to systematically focus on pertinent data from the observations and actions of nearby vehicles. With its ability to select resources independently without the need to provide global information, this approach is especially wellsuited for C-V2X. Comprehensive simulations reveal that DR2DRL performs better than alternative decentralized techniques, proving its reliability and scalability in constantly changing vehicular networks. DR2-DRL achieves a 5.26% improvement for a platoon size of 8, highlighting its ability to provide more up-to-date information in urban scenarios compared to Modified MADDPGwitTDec. © 2025, International Association of Engineers.
