title: ResQConnect: An AI-Powered Multi-Agentic Platform for Human-Centered and Resilient Disaster Response
authors: Aththanayake, Savinu; Mallikarachchi, Chemini; Wickramasinghe, Janeesha; Kugarajah, Sajeev; Meedeniya, Dulani; Pradhan, Biswajeet
venue: Sustainability (Switzerland)
abstract: Effective disaster management is critical for safeguarding lives, infrastructure and economies in an era of escalating natural hazards like floods and landslides. Despite advanced early-warning systems and coordination frameworks, a persistent “last-mile” challenge undermines response effectiveness: transforming fragmented and unstructured multimodal data into timely and accountable field actions. This paper introduces ResQConnect, a human-centered, AI-powered multimodal multi-agent platform that bridges this gap by directly linking incident intake to coordinated disaster response operations in hazard-prone regions. ResQConnect integrates three key components. It uses an agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) workflow in which specialized language-model agents extract metadata, refine queries, check contextual adequacy and generate actionable task plans using a curated, hazard-specific knowledge base. The contribution lies in structuring the RAG for correctness, safety and procedural grounding in high-risk settings. The platform introduces an Adaptive Event-Triggered (AET) multi-commodity routing algorithm that decides when to re-optimize routes, balancing responsiveness, computational cost and route stability under dynamic disaster conditions. Finally, ResQConnect deploys a compressed, domain-specific language model on mobile devices to provide policy-aligned guidance when cloud connectivity is limited or unavailable. Across realistic flood and landslide scenarios, ResQConnect improved overall task-quality scores from 61.4 to 82.9 (+21.5 points) over a standard RAG baseline, reduced solver calls by up to 85% compared to continuous re-optimization while remaining within 7–12% of optimal response time, and delivered fully offline mobile guidance with sub-500 ms response latency and 54 tokens/s throughput on commodity smartphones. Overall, ResQConnect demonstrates a practical and resilient approach to AI-augmented disaster response. From a sustainability perspective, the proposed system contributes to Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 11 by improving the speed and coordination of disaster response. It also supports SDG 13 by strengthening adaptation and readiness for climate-driven hazards. ResQConnect is validated using real-world flood and landslide disaster datasets, ensuring realistic incidents, constraints and operational conditions. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Smart Logistic System: A Multidisciplinary Integrated System for Driving Safety and Transportation Management
authors: Mogahed, Hussein Sh; Mohamed, Ahmed H.; Ali, Mohamed A.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: The logistics and transportation industry faces several critical challenges, including the absence of real-time vehicle data, inadequate safety measures, and inefficient resource management. This paper presents the Smart Logistic System (SLS), a unified intelligent transportation architecture that integrates embedded systems, Augmented Reality (AR), Machine Learning (ML), Internet of Things (IoT), and digital-twin technology within a single operational framework, rather than as independent subsystems. The system continuously monitors key vehicle parameters — location, speed, fuel consumption, and engine performance — to support proactive maintenance and minimize downtime. An edge-deployable driver-behavior-monitoring module employs computer vision and a lightweight MobileNetV3-Small classifier to detect drowsiness, distraction, and other hazardous behaviors in real time. Special-needs support includes seizure detection, GPS-based wandering alerts, and AR-guided vehicle-operation assistance. A route-optimization module formulates logistics planning as a constrained, multi-objective vehicle routing problem that jointly considers transportation cost, travel time, and estimated carbon emissions, while a digital-twin layer maintains a continuously synchronized virtual representation of fleet state to support fleet-manager decision-making. A mobile application delivers real-time data, alerts, and navigation to drivers; a desktop application allows managers to decode raw Controller Area Network (CAN) data; and a cloud platform provides secure storage, synchronization, and visualization. On a held-out benchmark, the driver-behavior-monitoring module achieves accuracy and inference-latency performance competitive with, and in several respects exceeding, recent state-of-the-art driver-monitoring methods; the route-optimization, predictive-maintenance, and digital-twin modules are validated through architectural and feasibility analysis rather than large-scale benchmarking. Taken together, these results indicate that SLS’s principal contribution is the integration of safety monitoring, logistics optimization, predictive maintenance, digital-twin synchronization, and accessibility features within a single operational architecture — a step toward more secure, efficient, and inclusive logistics and transportation systems. © 2000-2011 IEEE.

title: ARIA: An Agentic Release Intelligence Architecture for Autonomous End-to-End Mobile DevOps - From Build Prediction to Incident Resolution
authors: Gudimetla, Satyanarayana; Gangula, Suresh; Adinarayana, R.; Challa, Chandrakanth; Vunnam, Sudhakar; Buhyavarapu, Sudhamadhuri
venue: 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Systems, and Emerging Technologies, ICAISET 2026
abstract: Enterprise mobile delivery pipelines remain fragmented: build, CI, release, deployment, and incident response operate as disconnected stages, with post-deployment learning rarely propagating upstream. We present ARIA (Agentic Release Intelligence Architecture), a multi-agent architecture whose central contribution is the ARIA Feedback Protocol (AFP) - a confidence-gated, time-decayed mechanism providing two complementary benefit pathways: (i) per-incident observability acceleration that enriches diagnosis context for every incident, and (ii) multi-incident feedback accumulation that improves upstream test selection over time. ARIA coordinates five specialized agents through a shared provenance substrate and a graduated autonomy model whose governance components are mapped to NIST AI Risk Management Framework practices. A controlled simulation study parameterized from the public CI/CD histories of Signal Android, Firefox for Android (Fenix), and Wikipedia Android reports baseline, ablation, and sensitivity analyses over 30 stochastic replications. The per-incident mechanism yields a statistically significant MTTR reduction from 51.0 to 44.6 minutes (-12.6%, p<0.001, d=0.86) and governance improvement from 8.3 to 9.1 (+10.1%, p<0.001, d=1.30). The multi-incident mechanism (DDR +1.0%, RIR -5.8%) shows favorable trends; a post-hoc power analysis determines that ≈670 observations (≈22 applications) are needed for 80% statistical power, providing a concrete sample-size target for future production studies. An offline replay against 30 held-out CI failure events yields 83.3% prediction accuracy (vs. 60.0% baseline), supporting simulation fidelity. © 2026 IEEE.

title: 10th International Conference on Microelectronics, Electromagnetics and Telecommunication, ICMEET 2025
venue: Lecture Notes in Electrical Engineering
abstract: The proceedings contain 50 papers. The special focus in this conference is on Microelectronics, Electromagnetics and Telecommunication. The topics include: A Secure Optimized Bi-GRU-Based Attacker Detection Model Using Grey Wolf Optimizer; SRM-Based PV Water Pumping System Optimized Using the Mayfly Algorithm Under Partial Shading Conditions; remote Management of Solar Energy Harvesting Systems Using Bluetooth Connectivity; Architecture for AI-Augmented Smart Classrooms Through IoT Sensor Networks and Adaptive Learning Systems; anIoT-Based Adaptive Voltage Stabilizer with Buck-Boost Topology for Industrial/Residential Grid Support; ioT-Based Adaptive Conservation Control for Real-Time Water Quality and Distribution Monitoring; neural Network-Based Control Framework for Real-Time Ambient Temperature and Humidity Stabilization; autonomous Solar-Powered System for Hygrothermal and Water Level Monitoring in Real Time for Mobile Applications; smart IoT Driven Frequency Spectrum Based Agricultural Field Protection System Against Wild Animals; haptic-Feedback Navigation Cane for the Visually Impaired Using Embedded Safety Systems for Urban Mobility; robotic Process Automation in Healthcare: Advancing Operational Efficiency with Ethical Safeguards; supply Chain Disruptions: Machine Learning Techniques for the Global Value Chains and Economics Resilience; AI-Driven Trade Liberalization Analysis and Its Effects on Small and Medium Enterprises in Developing Countries; Machine Learning Based Insights into the Pedagogical Shifts in the STEM Education: From Rote Learning to Critical Thinking; preface; Preliminary Automated AI Based Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy Using Fundus Images; Automating De Novo Protein Design via LLM-Based Multi-agent Systems; automated Assessment in Network Security Education by Means of Unit Testing; artificial Consciousness: Integrating Human Intuition and Emotional Intelligence into Machine Cognition; techTheraphy: A Mental Health Support System.

title: Human-Guided AI Agent Framework Utilizing Conversational Guardrails in Clinical Settings
authors: Reza, Jamil Ur; Mamatjan, Yasin
venue: Signals and Communication Technology
abstract: Clinical decision support systems increasingly utilize AI to enhance diagnostic accuracy and workflow efficiency, but their “black‑box” nature and lack of structured clinician interaction often impede trust and real‑world adoption. In critical medical domains, ensuring transparent reasoning and human oversight is critical to both safety and clinician acceptance. We present a human-guided multi-agent artificial intelligence (AI) framework designed for clinical settings, which uses conversational guardrails to ensure safe, transparent decision support. Our system, built on CrewAI, ingests patient data and routes it through an ensemble predictor (XGBoost + Logistic Regression, Area Under Curve = 0.9123) before applying SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to produce patient-specific attributions. A dedicated assessment agent, constrained by domain-specific guardrails, synthesizes model outputs into draft interpretations and then pauses for structured human feedback (agreement/disagreement, comments, key points). This human-in-the-loop both validates and enriches the AI’s clinical reasoning. Finally, an automated report generator compiles physiological data, prediction probabilities, SHAP contributions, guardrail-filtered assessments, and clinician annotations into a cohesive, personalized patient report. Our framework demonstrates how conversational guardrails can bridge AI efficiency with clinician expertise, enhancing trust, interpretability, and the personalization of heart-disease risk assessments. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: Quality-Aware Potential-Based Reward Shaping for Fixed-Wing UAV Formation Navigation
authors: Jiang, Tiantian; Zhou, Xinglin; Li, Ang; Zhou, Dexiang; Zhang, Zhiyu; Ma, Ming
venue: Proceedings - 2026 IEEE 27th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Applications, CCSSTA 2026
abstract: Reward design is a key bottleneck in multi-agent reinforcement learning for fixed-wing UAV formation navigation, where a policy must coordinate assigned slot arrival, formation preservation, and collision avoidance under bounded vehicle motion. Common additive rewards mix progress, geometry, and safety terms, whereas directly gating task reward by formation quality can weaken the completion signal before the formation is fully corrected. This paper proposes quality-aware potential-based reward shaping (QA-PBRS), which separates base completion credit, completion-time formation-quality bonus, potential-based approach guidance, and explicit safety penalties. A heading-aligned formation-quality measure evaluates geometry consistently across target orientations. In four-UAV CTDE MASAC experiments, QA-PBRS achieved the highest final success rate (95.3%) and the lowest obstacle-collision rate (2.9%) among the tested reward variants. Although the quality-gated baseline yielded the lowest final formation error, QA-PBRS provided a stronger balance between reliable arrival and obstacle-collision safety. These results indicate that separating task completion from shaping and safety terms can make reward design more interpretable and robust for fixed-wing formation navigation. © 2026 IEEE.

title: An Integrated on-Board Weighing and Data Transmission System for Commercial Trucks Using Blockchain and IoT
authors: Singh, Pancham; Singh, Aditya Pratap; Pahuja, Neeti; Jain, Surbhi; Ayushi; Singh, Ankita
venue: 2026 International Conference on Green Technologies and Sustainable Solutions, GTSS 2026
abstract: Overloading of agricultural commercial trucks, especially in the case of sugarcane transportation, is a major problem that has been compromising road safety, the lifespan of infrastructure, fuel consumption, and compliance with regulations. Usually, weighing processes at stationary weighbridges are slow, operators are exposed to errors and the location is vulnerable to illegal operations. In this article, we developed a combined on, board dynamic weighing and secure data communication system for commercial trucks based on IoT sensors, GPS, and blockchain technology. The load cells fixed to the vehicle suspension continuously follow the changes in the load during the trip, signal conditioning and amplification make possible accurate weight estimation in real, time. The results of the measurement accuracy tests in different road conditions vary within 1-2%, thus the intermediate weighbridge stops are rendered obsolete. By using encrypted communication protocols, the system sends the weight and location data to the recipients and stores it on a tamper, proof blockchain ledger, thus ensuring data integrity, auditability, and transparency for the regulatory authorities. Besides, GPS integration allows route optimization and real, time fleet monitoring which, in turn, brings about less idle time, better logistics efficiency, and reduced fuel consumption. The proposed system architecture is capable of automated compliance reporting, reducing the corruption risk and gaining the trust of the involved stakeholders within the agricultural supply chain. Thanks to its modular and scalable design, the system could be adapted to other commercial vehicle fleets and agricultural commodities, thus being a cost, effective and efficient solution. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Real-Time Multi-Drone Replanning for Disruption Management in Urban Aerial Logistics Networks
authors: Zhang, Dongyuan; Sui, Zezhi; Zhang, Bangyan; Mao, Yinian; Quan, Quan
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Urban aerial logistics networks are vital for efficient last-mile deliveries yet remain vulnerable to disruption events. These events trigger cascading conflicts across multiple drones, risking system-wide scheduling breakdowns. Rapidly generating coordinated trajectories for large-scale fleets, adaptable from small and simple maps to large and complex ones, is essential. This letter presents a real-time replanning framework that resolves cascading conflicts and reduces system-wide delays without relying on predefined traffic zones. The upper level rapidly explores promising priority orders with anytime refinement; the lower level leverages spatiotemporal occupancy to generate conflict-free trajectories, enabling robust collision avoidance. Evaluations across diverse urban scenarios show conflict-free plans for 100 drones with 5 disruptions in 0.3\,\mathrms and a 43.02% reduction in total delay compared to baselines. This work enhances urban drone delivery resilience by efficiently handling unexpected disruptions while preserving delivery schedules. © 2016 IEEE.

title: A IoT-Enabled Autonomous Systems for Smart Waste Management: A Systematic Review and Research Outlook
authors: Mahajan, Pradnya B.; Vaze, Vinod Moreshwar; Takale, Dattatray G.
venue: Information Systems Engineering and Management
abstract: The waste Management systems of urban areas are increasing in need of intelligent, scalable and sustainable solutions. The merger of Artificial Intelligence and the Internet of Things (AIoT) has been gaining more momentum in the prior decade in particular 2018–2025 in practical implementations of autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), smart bins with sensory capabilities, and edge cloud computing to end-to-end waste management. This systematic review, using PRISMA guidelines, synthesizes peer-reviewed literature from IEEE, Elsevier, Springer, Wiley, and MDPI to identify and screen studies and analyses perception (vision-based waste detection & multimodal sensing), cognition (on-device/edge inference, route planning, learning-based decision-making) & action (ROS-enabled autonomy, manipulation, fleet coordination). We connect key enablers (e.g., YOLOv4/Lightweight MobileNets) CNN/transformer detectors, SLAM and LiDAR/ultrasonic fusion, LoRa/NB-IoT/MQTT communications, and edge cloud orchestration to reported results in terms of classification accuracy, collection latency, travel distance reduction, and energy utilization. Recent prototypes and pilots suggest a range of steady advances made on proof-of-concept vision prototypes such as resource-aware edge inference, privacy-aware learning, and resource-aware telemetry at a city scale. However, there are still open gaps on robust operation in unstructured environments, interoperability among heterogeneous municipal platforms, energy sustainability (battery-solar hybrids, mission planning), and human-robot interaction (safety, acceptance, governance). We put forward a research agenda focusing on federated and continuous learning for AIoT; standardized data/ontology schemas; green autonomy (energy-aware planning and renewable integration); and ethics by design frameworks for public-space robotics. Through consolidation of developments and unresolved problems of 2018–2025, this review makes sense on a coherent taxonomy, comparative lessons and a forward roadmap to come up with scientifically rigorous, deployable and citizen friendly AIoT waste systems in smart cities. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: P3GASUS: Pre-Planned Path Execution Graphs for Multi-Agent Systems at Ultra-Large Scale
authors: Duhan, Tanishq; He, Chengyang; Sartoretti, Guillaume
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Executing pre-planned paths in multi-agent systems is challenging, as a lack of synchronization can lead to collisions or live-/deadlocks, while enforcing strict synchronization may cause a widespread team delay in reaching goals. An Action Dependency Graph (ADG) solves this problem by identifying and synchronizing only the necessary robots during execution by post-processing all agents' paths into a static directed graph with actions as nodes and edges representing the execution precedence order between actions. However, ADG's creation phase currently requires an exhaustive search of the action space that inflates both computation and communication (O(R 2~ T 2 ), where R is the number of robots and T is the maximum path length). This makes ADG the bottleneck for current state-of-the-art MAPF planners, which can solve for up to 10000 agents, and lifelong MAPF, which needs constant replanning during execution. Moreover, this biquadratic scaling also limits the extension of ADG to continuous space scenarios, where high-frequency updates typically effectively result in long path lengths. Addressing these limitations, in this work, we propose three improved execution graphs to cater to different needs and scenarios: SAGE, which adds edges based on the sequence in which robots visit a position; MAGE, which takes the execution graph of SAGE as input and prunes its redundant edges, reducing communication burden during execution; and FORTED which combines both approaches with a reduced complexity of O(RT), making it the overall best in discrete scenarios, trading-off scalability to continuous space scenarios. All three methods achieve speedups of 300-8000 folds over ADG, with MAGE and FORTED reducing communication overhead by more than 14 times. By integrating these methods with a framework for robust distributed path execution for both discrete and continuous scenarios, we introduce P3GASUS, an end-to-end method for pre-planned path execution in multi-agent systems. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of P3GASUS in discrete and continuous multi-agent scenarios using hybrid (real and virtual) teams with up to 3000 robots. © 2016 IEEE.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning-Based Drone Trajectory Design for Fire Rescue
authors: Sun, Nan; Han, Zidong; Li, Xiaoyang
venue: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Wireless Communication Systems
abstract: As a critical application of the low-altitude economy, fire rescue requires drones to collect the dynamic wildfire information observed by distributed ground users and to deliver it to command centers for timely decisions. To this end, the trajectories of drones need to be designed with respect to the value of information (VoI), the age of information (AoI), as well as the safety and energy constraints over time-varying air-to-ground links. Conventional studies focused on perimeter tracking or connectivity, leaving user-centric VoI-AoI service under explicit fire condition unexplored. To bridge this gap, a physics-enriched simulation environment with a robot-operating-system-compatible interface is developed in this paper. A cooperative strategy based on multi-agent proximal policy optimization with parameter sharing is further proposed. Simulations are conducted to illustrate the performance gain of the proposed strategy compared with other baselines. © 2026, VDE Verlag GmbH. All rights reserved.

title: AI-Based Whole-Body Vibration Monitoring Framework for Driver Fatigue, Comfort, and Road Safety
authors: Wanto, Rio Darma; Sekti, Binastya Anggara; Sardana, Gusti Muhamad
venue: Automatic Systems for Monitoring Drivers' Vibrations
abstract: Whole-body vibration (WBV) is a critical factor affecting driver comfort, fatigue, occupational health, and road safety. This chapter presents an AI-based monitoring framework that integrates vibration sensors, signal processing, machine learning, risk classification, and mitigation responses to assess driver exposure in real time. The framework transforms raw vibration data from seats, steering wheels, floors, wearables, smartphones, and vehicle systems into meaningful indicators for fatigue detection, comfort assessment, and safety evaluation. It also emphasizes sensor placement, data quality, AI reliability, standards compliance, and human-centered intervention. By supporting alerts, rest-break recommendations, smart seat adjustment, adaptive damping, and fleet-level decision-making, the proposed approach promotes proactive monitoring to reduce fatigue, improve comfort, protect occupational health, and enhance safer transportation systems in modern mobility environments. © 2027 by IGI Global Scientific Publishing. All rights reserved.

title: Hybrid Distributed and Decentralised Reinforcement Learning for Formation Control of Multi-Robots With Obstacle Avoidance
authors: Peng, Yaoqian; Zhang, Xinglong; Xie, Haibin; Xu, Xin
venue: CAAI Transactions on Intelligence Technology
abstract: Recently, learning-based control for multi-robot systems (MRS) with obstacle avoidance has received increasing attention. The goals of formation control and obstacle avoidance could be intrinsically tied. As a result, developing a safe and near-optimal control policy with the actor-critic structure is challenging. Therefore, a hybrid distributed and decentralised asynchronous actor-critic reinforcement learning (Di-De-RL) technique is proposed to address this problem. First, we decompose the integrated formation control and collision avoidance problem into two successive ones. To solve them, we design a distributed reinforcement learning (Di-RL) algorithm that employs a neural network-based actor-critic structure for formation control, and a decentralised RL (De-RL) algorithm that incorporates a potential-field (PF)-based actor-critic structure for collision avoidance. In Di-RL, the actor-critic pairs are trained in a distributed manner to achieve near-optimal consensus formation control. With the trained policy of Di-RL fixed, the PF actor-critic pairs in De-RL are trained in a decentralised manner for safe collision avoidance. Such an asynchronous training design of the hybrid Di-RL and De-RL enables weight convergence and control safety in the learning process. The simulated and real-world experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and enhanced performance of the approach in formation control with both static and dynamic obstacle avoidance, highlighting its advantages in resolving the conflict between the safety objective and optimal control. © 2025 The Author(s). CAAI Transactions on Intelligence Technology published by John Wiley & Sons Ltd on behalf of The Institution of Engineering and Technology and Chongqing University of Technology.

title: Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning with Reward Shaping for Fixed-Wing Multi-UAV Trajectory Tracking and Collision Avoidance
authors: Nguyen, Phuoc-Bao-Duy; Tan, Luy Nguyen
venue: Conference Proceedings - ICCE 2026: 2026 IEEE 11th International Conference on Communications and Electronics
abstract: Trajectory tracking for fixed-wing unmanned aerials (UAVs) in obstacle-cluttered environments remains a formidable challenge due to their inherent non-holonomic kinematic constraints. This problem is further exacerbated in dense multiUAV scenarios, where the system must navigate complex spatial geometries to simultaneously execute static obstacle avoidance and dynamic inter-agent collision avoidance. To address these tightly coupled objectives, this paper proposes a novel hierarchical hybrid control framework that seamlessly integrates deep reinforcement learning with the L1 navigation algorithm. A key contribution of this work is the development of a continuous adaptive reward shaping mechanism. Within this hierarchical architecture, the soft actor-critic agent functions as a high-level planner generating virtual path offsets, while the L1 controller ensures smooth, kinematically feasible low-level execution. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed method ensures high-fidelity trajectory tracking, allowing UAVs to execute smooth evasive maneuvers and rapidly return to the reference path, thus guaranteeing safety and efficiency in highly demanding multi-agent intersections and curved scenarios. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Design of a SMART Valve Testbed for Nuclear Thermal Dispatch
authors: Bairagi, Anutam; Chen, Minghui; Ifeanyi, Ark; Creasman, Sarah; Coble, Jamie; Agarwal, Vivek
venue: Energies
abstract: By the year 2050, the United States aims to achieve net-zero carbon emissions. To achieve this target, the licensing of the Light Water Reactor (LWR) fleet has been extended for 20 more years. To stay economically competitive with other power sources such as renewable and fossil-fuel power plants, the U.S. Department of Energy has introduced a plan to modernize the existing LWR fleet and diversify the revenue stream. One of the plans is to dispatch thermal energy to endothermic industrial processes. SMART valves will play an important role in this initiative by efficiently balancing the load by regulating valves in a coordinated manner while monitoring the thermal-hydraulic systems to enhance safety and maintain the integrity of the power plant. This research aims to develop a facility to test the coordinated control algorithm and produce various test results for training the monitoring system. The constructed facility is capable of simulating various operational and accidental scenarios by coordinating all the valves (positions) and pump (flowrate). The facility is developed with an Internet of Things (IoT)-based custom system and a python-based valve position control and coordination mechanism. It has achieved stable sensor outputs, pump control, and coordinated valve regulation in all three valves with minimum obstruction in the system. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Collision-Aware Density-Driven Control of Multi-Agent Systems via Control Barrier Functions
authors: Seo, Sungjun; Lee, Kooktae
venue: IFAC-PapersOnLine
abstract: This paper tackles the problem of safe and efficient area coverage using a multi-agent system operating in environments with obstacles. Applications such as environmental monitoring and search and rescue require robot swarms to cover large domains under resource constraints, making both coverage efficiency and safety essential. To address the efficiency aspect, we adopt the Density-Driven Control (D2C) framework, which uses optimal transport theory to steer agents according to a reference distribution that encodes spatial coverage priorities. To ensure safety, we incorporate Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) into the framework. While CBFs are commonly used for collision avoidance, we extend their applicability by introducing obstacle-specific formulations for both circular and rectangular shapes. In particular, we analytically derive a unit normal vector based on the agent's position relative to the nearest face of a rectangular obstacle, improving safety enforcement in environments with non-smooth boundaries. Additionally, a velocity-dependent term is incorporated into the CBF to enhance collision avoidance. Simulation results validate the proposed method by demonstrating smoother navigation near obstacles and more efficient area coverage than the existing method, while still ensuring collision-free operation. © 2025 The Authors.

title: Constraining an Unconstrained Multi-agent Policy with offline data
authors: Guan, Cong; Jiang, Tao; Li, Yi-Chen; Zhang, Zongzhang; Yuan, Lei; Yu, Yang
venue: Neural Networks
abstract: Real-world multi-agent decision-making systems often have to satisfy some constraints, such as harmfulness, economics, etc., spurring the emergence of Constrained Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (CMARL). Existing studies of CMARL mainly focus on training a constrained policy in an online manner, that is, not only maximizing cumulative rewards but also not violating constraints. However, in practice, online learning may be infeasible due to safety restrictions or a lack of high-fidelity simulators. Moreover, as the learned policy runs, new constraints, that are not taken into account during training, may occur. To deal with the above two issues, we propose a method called Constraining an UnconsTrained Multi-Agent Policy with offline data, dubbed CUTMAP, following the popular centralized training with decentralized execution paradigm. Specifically, we have formulated a scalable optimization objective within the framework of multi-agent maximum entropy reinforcement learning for CMARL. This approach is designed to estimate a decomposable Q-function by leveraging an unconstrained “prior policy” 1 ote> in conjunction with cost signals extracted from offline data. When a new constraint comes, CUTMAP can reuse the prior policy without re-training it. To tackle the distribution shift challenge in offline learning, we also incorporate a conservative loss term when updating the Q-function. Therefore, the unconstrained prior policy can be trained to satisfy cost constraints through CUTMAP without the need for expensive interactions with the real environment, facilitating the practical application of MARL algorithms. Empirical results in several cooperative multi-agent benchmarks, including StarCraft games, particle games, food search games, and robot control, demonstrate the superior performance of our method. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd

title: Decentralized formation with collision avoidance of multi-agent conformable fractional nonlinear robot systems
authors: Ángeles-Ramírez, O.A.; González-Figueroa, S.; Fernández-Anaya, G.; Martínez-Hernández, E.G.; González-Sierra, J.; Ramírez-Neria, M.
venue: Asian Journal of Control
abstract: The formation control problem for a multi-agent robot system is addressed from the general conformable fractional multi-variable framework viewpoint, considering interagent collision avoidance based on the combination of local attractive and repulsive potential functions for general well-defined formation graphs for the case of point or omnidirectional robots by using the classical Lyapunov's stability analysis. The theoretical development of a control law from the viewpoint of the multivariable conformable fractional-order calculus is given. In addition, a comparison of the convergence performance to the desired pattern with collision avoidance between the integer-order and the general conformable fractional-order case is provided. Finally, an illustrative numerical example is given to exhibit the performance of the proposed strategy. © 2025 Chinese Automatic Control Society and John Wiley & Sons Australia, Ltd.

title: A Deep Reinforcement-Learning-Based Route Optimization Model for Multi-Compartment Cold Chain Distribution
authors: Hu, Jingming; Wang, Chong
venue: Mathematics
abstract: Cold chain logistics is crucial in ensuring food quality and safety in modern supply chains. The required temperature control systems increase operational costs and environmental impacts compared to conventional logistics. To reduce these costs while maintaining service quality in real-world distribution scenarios, efficient route planning is essential, particularly when products with different temperature requirements need to be delivered together using multi-compartment refrigerated vehicles. This substantially increases the complexity of the routing process. We propose a novel deep reinforcement learning approach that incorporates a vehicle state encoder for capturing fleet characteristics and a dynamic vehicle state update mechanism for enabling real-time vehicle state updates during route planning. Extensive experiments on a real-world road network show that our proposed method significantly outperforms four representative methods. Compared to a recent ant colony optimization algorithm, it achieves up to a 6.32% reduction in costs while being up to 1637 times faster in computation. © 2025 by the authors.

title: Mobile robot navigation using deep reinforcement learning: Algorithms, challenges, and future directions
authors: Ramananda Sagar, Bagu; Kumar Abbili, Kiran; Konjeti, Rama Krishna
venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers, Part C: Journal of Mechanical Engineering Science
abstract: Autonomous navigation of mobile robots in unstructured, dynamic environments is a critical challenge in robotics. Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has emerged as a promising approach for enabling robots to learn complex navigation policies through continuous interaction with their surroundings. This review paper presents a value-based algorithms, policy-based algorithms, hybrid DRL algorithms, hierarchical DRL algorithms, and multi-agent DRL (MADRL), with a focus on their applicability to real-world robotic navigation tasks. Despite significant advancements, several challenges remain such as sample inefficiency, safety constraints, and limited generalization to unseen environments. This review further highlights open research issues and future directions, including sim-to-real transfer, multi-agent collaboration, and hybrid approaches that integrate DRL with classical navigation methods. © IMechE 2026

title: Secure Data Aggregation for Oilfield Transport and Inspection Vehicles Using Onion-Routed Federated Learning
authors: Ganesh, Ramya; Rana, Shruti; Patel, Prushti; Trivedi, Chinmay; Kavar, Jemi; Bavarva, Robin; Pathak, Lakshin; Patel, Devamm
venue: 2026 IEEE Texas Power and Energy Conference, TPEC 2026
abstract: The safety and communication abilities of vehicular ad-hoc networks (VANETs) are highly dynamic and thus vulnerable to distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks, which exploit the network's dynamic topology. This paper proposes an onion-routed federated learning framework for privacy-preserving, real-time DDoS detection in VANETs deployed in the oil and gas industry. In such industrial environments, fleets of vehicles transport hazardous materials and equipment across remote and high-risk sites, where secure and reliable communication is vital for operational safety. A TinyML-based model is trained locally on each vehicle's network traffic, and the model updates are securely encrypted and anonymized using onion routing before aggregation, ensuring that raw data never leaves the node. A 5G-enabled communication layer guarantees low-latency and dependable update transfer among vehicles, roadside units, and the central aggregator. Intensive testing on the LR-HR DDoS 2024 data indicates that the suggested framework can attain a global model precision of 0.9988 and a global loss of 0.043, which guarantees a high level of accuracy and efficiency in detecting the low-rate and high-rate DDoS attacks. The findings demonstrate that the framework can achieve the privacy and security, and real-time performance balance in highly dynamic oil and gas VANET environments. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Early Fault Prediction in Industrial Equipment using MA-LSTM-CNN
authors: Dinesh.t; Manogar.k; Prabu.m; Chandrasekaran.k
venue: Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking, ICPCSN 2026
abstract: Prediction of the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of the component or equipment is gaining more attention in the manufacturing industries as it helps to avoid the catastrophic equipment failure. In this paper, a new Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction method is designed and implemented using Multi attention Convolution Neural Network in high-risk industrial environments as it is resilient to multiple faults and different operating conditions. Convolution Neural Network processes the complex sensor data and extracts the uncertain characteristics of the equipment as crucial degradation features using different filters functions to data trajectories containing data distribution discrepancies. Those degradation features are projected to long short-term memory to captures short term variation and long-term overall degradation. Those short-term variation and long-term overall degradation feature of the equipment are projected to pooling layer containing attention mechanism to assign weights to the crucial degradation features. Weighted feature of different time steps is applied to fully connected layer to determine early sign of degradation, its risk level, Finally Fault progression and remaining useful life of the equipment is predicted using SoftMax function. Experimental analysis is performed using NASA C-MAPSS dataset composed of 21 sensor measurement including temperature, pressure, and speed etc. on different operational settings of the fleet of the turbofan engine. On performance analysis, model provides prediction accuracy of 98% compared to conventional models. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Role-Structured Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Airship-Guided UAV Pursuit Tracking
authors: Yang, Kejie; Zhou, Yuting; Zhu, Ming; Zhang, Yifei
venue: 2026 International Conference on Robot Perception and Intelligent Control, RPIC 2026
abstract: This paper investigates heterogeneous aerial pursuit tracking with one high-endurance airship, multiple UAV pursuers, and evasive targets. The task is formulated as a partially observed mixed cooperative-adversarial game under centralized training and decentralized execution. A role-difference-potential multi-agent reinforcement learning framework is proposed, in which each agent maintains an individual actor and critics are shared at the role level with identity conditioning. To improve cooperative credit assignment, pursuer optimization combines potential-based shaping with counterfactual one-step difference rewards. The potential function integrates coverage guidance, approach pressure, capture-neighborhood entry, encirclement quality, and safety regularization; actions are parameterized by bounded speed and yaw rate for kinematic consistency. Simulation results show stable coordinated closure and reliable capture, indicating that role-structured entropy-regularized learning with difference-potential rewards is a practical baseline for heterogeneous pursuit tasks. © 2026 IEEE.

title: LiDAR-Based Modified Virtual Force Field Navigation for Decentralized Multi-Robot Systems in ROS Simulation
authors: Lone, Mohd Aaqib; Kovács, Szilveszter
venue: International Journal of Robotics and Control Systems
abstract: Autonomous navigation in dynamic environments remains a fundamental chal-lenge in mobile robotics, particularly when robots must avoid moving obstacles using onboard sensor data. This study presents a Modified Virtual Force Field (MVFF) algorithm for decentralized multi-robot navigation using 2D LiDAR sensing within the Robot Operating System (ROS). The research contribution is a reactive navigation framework that computes per-beam inverse-square repulsive forces directly from raw Cartesian LiDAR measurements without occupancy-grid construction, extending standard VFF by replacing grid-cell certainty aggregation with direct per-beam force computation at the native Li-DAR scan frequency, and incorporating explicit inter-robot repulsive forces for decentralized multi-agent coordination. Robot pose estimation uses Adaptive Monte Carlo Localization (AMCL) against a pre-built map, while all obstacle avoidance decisions are computed from live LiDAR beams independently, eliminating map-update latency from the reactive control loop. The algorithm was implemented as a standalone ROS node and evaluated in Gazebo simulation using three differential-drive robots across multiple scenarios: corridor traversal, single dynamic obstacle avoidance, multiple dynamic obstacles, and shared workspace navigation, each repeated five times. Compared with a standard VFF reactive controller and a hybrid fuzzy-VFF system, MVFF reduced navigation time by 24% (50.3 s vs. 38.2 s), collision count by 46.9% (3.2 vs. 1.7), and behavior-switching latency by 25% (400 ms vs. 300 ms). Minimum obstacle approach distance decreased by 40% (2.5 m vs. 1.5 m), reflecting more precise force-field regulation. Path smoothness improved by 50% and navigation state classification accuracy increased by 21.3% (0.75 vs. 0.91). These results demonstrate that MVFF provides an efficient and responsive navigation strategy for decentralized multi-robot systems in simulation. Future work will address real-world validation, embedded processor profiling, and benchmarking against TEB and DWA planners. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Adaptive Target Trapping with Multirobot Systems via Distributed Probabilistic Inference
authors: Huang, Mengdie; Xiao, Dengyu; Sun, Yu; Pu, Huayan; Luo, Jun
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics
abstract: In the field of multiagent systems, the multirobot coordinated encirclement task in a dense environment is extremely challenging. However, existing methods often rely on pre-defined task assignments, limiting the system's ability for self-organized encirclement, which undermines robustness, especially against agile targets in dense environments. To address this issue, a novel distributed probabilistic inference model for cooperative trapping is proposed, based on adaptive cooperative trapping factors. The model can propagate Gaussian messages in parallel using the incremental collaborative Gaussian belief propagation (ICGBP) algorithm, achieving self-organized encirclement, thereby enhancing capture efficiency and ensuring effective collision avoidance. Specifically, we derive the relationships between Gaussian messages under various constraints and provide theoretical proof to guarantee the asymptotic convergence of the algorithm. Moreover, we extensively investigate the relationships between several parameters of task configuration and trapping success rates, determining the optimal range of the adaptive shrinking radius. Finally, both simulations and real-world experiments with highly maneuverable and human-controlled targets are performed, validating the effectiveness and robustness of ICGBP for multirobot adaptive target trapping under high-randomness unknown evasion strategies. © 2025 IEEE.

title: A Privacy-Preserving On-Device Multi-Agent Architecture for AI PC (POMA) Workflow Automation
authors: Begum, Sultana; Rosenzweig, Michael
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on AI and Data Analytics, ICAD 2026
abstract: AI agents that automate desktop workflows can reduce time spent on repetitive knowledge work, but enterprise deployment raises acute privacy and trust challenges. Computer-use agents (CUAs) observe sensitive on-screen content and execute high-impact actions in open-world environments, making them vulnerable to prompt injection and unsafe tool use. Meanwhile, recent model evolution has significantly improved the capabilities of small language and compact multimodal models, enabling specialized low-latency inference that can run fully on-device. This paper presents AIPC-POMA, a privacy-preserving on-device multi-agent architecture for personal and enterprise AI PC workflow automation. AIPC POMA composes a set of carefully crafted, task-specialized small agents including an SLM for drafting, a compact VLM+OCR stack for document and screen understanding, and a sandboxed CUA for GUI interaction coordinated by a local Orchestrator and enforced by a Policy Verifier. POMA is designed around two principles: privacy by minimized data flow and trust by controlled action execution, achieved through least-privilege action primitives, risk-aware gating, and auditable execution traces. We describe a hardware aware implementation optimized for heterogeneous AI acceleration on AI PCs such as Panther Lake-class system, and we introduce an evaluation task suite and adversarial safety battery targeting indirect prompt injection and real-world agent threats. We define metrics spanning utility, latency, privacy leakage, and action safety, demonstrating that POMA enables practical low-cost automation while reducing exposure to untrusted inputs. © 2026 IEEE.

title: AI-Enabled Multi-Agent Path Planning for Intelligent Transportation Systems: A Field-Geometry Coupling and Topological Decision-Making Integrated Framework
authors: Deng, Ziheng
venue: Proceedings of SPIE - The International Society for Optical Engineering
abstract: In this paper, an interdisciplinary framework combining differential manifold perception modeling, field-geometry coupling optimization, and algebraic topology decision theory is proposed to meet the need for multi-agent cooperative decision-making in dynamic intelligent transportation scenarios. A four-dimensional spatio-temporal manifold model is constructed based on LiDAR temporal point cloud, and the essential decoupling of dynamic and static obstacles is realized through tangential space motion vector field and manifold curvature features. The dynamic coupling equation of virtual boundary field gradient and Bessel control point is innovatively established, and the energy functional optimization theory based on variational principle is developed to solve the cooperative problem of safety constraint and geometric smoothness in trajectory planning. The chain complex algebraic structure of traffic participant intent transfer is constructed, the topological nature of human-machine decision conflict is analyzed by homology group dimension, and the accessibility metric axioms are defined to realize dynamic scenario adaptation. Theoretically, it forms a trinity methodology system of "differential geometry, field theory, and algebraic topology", which provides a new mathematical basis for multi-modal perception, collaborative decision making, and intention compatibility in complex traffic environments. Its interdisciplinary characteristics can be extended to the theoretical research of intelligent urban transportation, swarm robot navigation, and other fields. © 2025 SPIE.

title: A multiagent architecture for Industrial Internet of Things safety applications
authors: Barbosa, Gibson; Sadok, Djamel F.H.; Kelner, Judith; Ribeiro, Luis
venue: Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) is a key technological pillar of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, also known as Industry 4.0. In this context, an area of considerable interest is human safety technology. Solutions rely on multiple sensors connected to a central monitoring system and supported with software to autonomously or semi-autonomously identify safety hazards. To this end, Computer vision systems are leveraged. However, streaming continuous video from numerous sensors can strain network resources, risking timely hazard response in large industrial setups. This work proposes a reference IIoT architecture based on Multi-Agent Systems to manage safety risks. It allows for scalable sensor integration and dynamically assesses sensor input based on risk levels. To prevent network overload, the architecture uses sensor-level intelligence at the edge layer to assess situational risks and decide whether to forward video signals to a centralized local cloud agent. The central cloud agent, using strategies like ensemble learning, selectively requests additional data from distributed edge agents based on the diagnosed risk. This approach was tested in monitoring safety during aircraft assembly, showing that edge processing reduces network load by limiting unnecessary data transmission without compromising accuracy. This architecture effectively distributes processing to the edge, maintaining detection accuracy while minimizing network traffic compared to continuous centralized video transmission. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd

title: Toward Goal-Oriented Communication in Multi-Agent Systems: An Overview
authors: Charalambous, Themistoklis; Pappas, Nikolaos; Nomikos, Nikolaos; Wichman, Risto
venue: IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society
abstract: As multi-agent systems (MAS) become increasingly prevalent in autonomous systems, distributed control, and edge intelligence, efficient communication under resource constraints has emerged as a critical challenge. Traditional communication paradigms often emphasize message fidelity or bandwidth optimization, overlooking the task relevance of the exchanged information. In contrast, goal-oriented communication prioritizes the importance of information with respect to the agents' shared objectives. This review provides a comprehensive survey of goal-oriented communication in MAS, bridging perspectives from information theory, communication theory, and machine learning. We examine foundational concepts alongside learning-based approaches and emergent protocols. Special attention is given to coordination under communication constraints, as well as applications in domains such as swarm robotics, federated learning, and edge computing. The paper concludes with a discussion of open challenges and future research directions at the intersection of communication theory, machine learning, and multi-agent decision making. © 2020 IEEE.

title: A Technical Introduction to Hyperautomation Technologies and Tools
authors: Sasikala, S.; Venkatesh, C.; Kingsly Jabakumar, A.; Yazhini, S.
venue: Studies in Systems, Decision and Control
abstract: This chapter presents a reference architecture for hyperautomation in multi robot systems that must work under real timing and safety limits. The problem is clear. Many fleets run well in a single cell then fail when spread across lines shifts or sites because integrations are brittle, models drift and exception handling lives in tribal knowledge rather than code. It defines a five-layer stack from perception and actuation up to enterprise and governance, with security and audit wrapped across all layers. Each interface uses explicit data contracts for events, commands and metrics so services evolve safely while keeping at least once delivery and idempotent handlers. Timing is treated as a budget per hop not a hope, with fast safety loops at the edge and slower process decisions in orchestration. The chapter specifies multi robot task allocation policies, a guarded task state machine, runtime assurance patterns for learned policies and a twin in the loop flow for testing changes before rollout. Process mining and event logs feed back into workflows and metrics so improvement is continuous and traceable. A smart warehouse case study shows how the architecture performs in a goods to person setting with mobile robots. The study compares baseline dispatch with the proposed coordination stack using throughput, latency, reallocation time, safety incidents and SLA breaches. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: Joint Task Allocation and Charging Scheduling for UAVs: Managing Corridor Congestion and Non-Linear Hovering Penalties
authors: Zhang, Miaohan; Pan, Nan; Zhang, Sheng; Zhang, Yangyang; Liang, Weijie
venue: 2026 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia: Industry and Transportation Integrated Smart Energy System, I and CPS Asia 2026
abstract: The rapid development of low-altitude corridors and complex industrial collaborative inspections imposes stringent requirements on the automated online scheduling of the UAV fleet. Existing path planning studies based on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) often lack practical physical constraints, neglecting the severe nonlinear hovering energy consumption induced by microscopic collision avoidance in 3D corridors and queuing at terminal base stations. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a Joint UAV Task Allocation and Charging Scheduling Model (JUTACS) formulated for 3D constrained corridors. Developed within a Semi-Markov Decision Process (SMDP) framework, the proposed JUTACS systematically characterizes heterogeneous inspection tasks, the dynamic congestion of charging base stations, and the asynchronous spatio-temporal transitions of the UAV fleet. Furthermore, a Dual-Layer Kinematics-Driven Neural Combinatorial Optimization Solving Framework (CAMT-RH) is introduced. In this hierarchical architecture, the upper layer employs a Congestion-Aware Mask Transformer (CAMT-PPO) as the global scheduling hub, while the lower layer embeds a Priority-based Spatio-Temporal Reservation (P-STR) mechanism as a physical feasibility evaluator, thereby achieving the collaborative optimization of inspection task allocation and path planning. Comparative evaluations against greedy dispatching, MAPPO, rolling-horizon MILP, ALNS, and neural scheduling baselines demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves the best reward, task completion, hovering control, and online inference efficiency. In addition, ablation studies, congestion sensitivity analyses, and zero-shot generalization experiments reveal how the congestion-aware encoder, dynamic feasibility mask, P-STR feedback, and nonlinear hovering penalty jointly improve robustness under varying UAV fleet sizes and chargingstation bottlenecks. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Low-Latency Edge-Enabled Digital Twin System for Multi-Robot Collision Avoidance and Remote Control
authors: Mtowe, Daniel Poul; Long, Lika; Kim, Dong Min
venue: Sensors
abstract: This paper proposes a low-latency and scalable architecture for Edge-Enabled Digital Twin networked control systems (E-DTNCS) aimed at multi-robot collision avoidance and remote control in dynamic and latency-sensitive environments. Traditional approaches, which rely on centralized cloud processing or direct sensor-to-controller communication, are inherently limited by excessive network latency, bandwidth bottlenecks, and a lack of predictive decision-making, thus constraining their effectiveness in real-time multi-agent systems. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel framework that seamlessly integrates edge computing with digital twin (DT) technology. By performing localized preprocessing at the edge, the system extracts semantically rich features from raw sensor data streams, reducing the transmission overhead of the original data. This shift from raw data to feature-based communication significantly alleviates network congestion and enhances system responsiveness. The DT layer leverages these extracted features to maintain high-fidelity synchronization with physical robots and to execute predictive models for proactive collision avoidance. To empirically validate the framework, a real-world testbed was developed, and extensive experiments were conducted with multiple mobile robots. The results revealed a substantial reduction in collision rates when DT was deployed, and further improvements were observed with E-DTNCS integration due to significantly reduced latency. These findings confirm the system’s enhanced responsiveness and its effectiveness in handling real-time control tasks. The proposed framework demonstrates the potential of combining edge intelligence with DT-driven control in advancing the reliability, scalability, and real-time performance of multi-robot systems for industrial automation and mission-critical cyber-physical applications. © 2025 by the authors.

title: OR-AGENT framework – Architecting electrified heavy-duty drayage applications
authors: Sujan, Vivek A.; Sun, Ruixiao; Snyder, Isabelle
venue: Applied Energy
abstract: The widespread adoption of zero-emission vehicles in heavy-duty (HD) commercial freight transportation faces considerable technoeconomic challenges. For heavy-duty trucks, ensuring high uptime, cost parity with diesel, and safety standards is especially critical as these vehicles operate over long distances with heavy loads, where any downtime or off-nominal behaviors significantly impacts logistics, productivity, and the total cost of ownership. Unlike traditional diesel refueling, BEV charging infrastructure must be co-optimized with vehicle deployment, operational demands, and grid capacity to ensure cost-effective and reliable freight operations. However, the lack of a standardized ownership and service model has led to a fragmented approach—where commercial vehicle operators may invest in, own, and maintain both vehicle/batteries and charging/energy infrastructure. This disconnect may exclude energy service providers from the equation, forcing fleet operators to explore ‘behind-the-fence’ energy solutions that increase capital investment, operational downtime, overhead costs, and, in some cases, net carbon emissions. To address these issues, this study introduces OR-AGENT (Optimal Regional Architecture Generation for Efficient National Transport), a comprehensive modeling framework that integrates powertrain architectures, charging infrastructures, and energy backbone systems into a cohesive strategy. In this paper, OR-AGENT is applied to develop an interconnected systems architecture for energy efficiency and resiliency enhancement of heavy-duty drayage vehicles at the Port of Savannah, GA. This framework showcases an interconnected systems approach to electrifying heavy-duty drayage vehicles at the Port of Savannah, GA. The study assessed BEVs with 400–1200 kWh battery capacities, accounting for seasonal variations in weather and freight routing. A diverse charging mix (150 kW–1250 kW) was evaluated alongside grid capacity constraints, cost, and carbon intensity analysis, leading to the development of a strategic microgrid/Distributed Energy Resources (DER) deployment architecture to ensure a reliable and sustainable transition. However, the findings also highlight the need for alternative zero-emission solutions for remaining trips, such as larger batteries, electrified roadways, hydrogen powertrains, or net-zero emission fuels. The findings are incorporated into a Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) model to identify optimal architectures for an interconnected electrified ecosystem. © 2025

title: Airy: Reading Robot Intent through Height and Sky
authors: Chen, Baoyang; Xu, Xian; Qu, Huamin
venue: Proceedings - SIGGRAPH Asia 2025 Art Papers, SA 2025
abstract: As industrial robots move into shared human spaces, their opaque decision making threatens safety, trust, and public oversight. This artwork, Airy, asks whether complex multi agent AI can become intuitively understandable by staging a competition between two reinforcement trained robot arms that snap a bedsheet skyward. Building on three design principles-competition as a clear metric ("who lifts higher?"), embodied familiarity (audiences recognize fabric snapping), and sensor to sense mapping (robot cooperation or rivalry shown through forest and weather projections)-the installation gives viewers a visceral way to read machine intent. Observations from five international exhibitions indicate that audiences consistently read the robots' strategies, conflict, and cooperation in real time, with emotional reactions that mirror the system's internal state. The project shows how sensory metaphors can turn a black box into a public interface. © 2025 Copyright is held by the owner/author(s). Publication rights licensed to ACM.

title: Harnessing cutting-edge technologies for sustainable future shipping: An overview of innovations, drivers, barriers, and opportunities
authors: Alamoush, Anas S.; Ölçer, Aykut I.
venue: Maritime Technology and Research
abstract: Sustainable shipping technologies are advancing considerably, but results are fragmented. This study, thus, reviews the literature and organizes the results into cohesive clusters based on their defining characteristics, drivers, barriers, and opportunities. The first cluster, automation technologies, includes autonomous navigation, remote machinery operation, automated maintenance, and cargo handling systems. These technologies streamline operations, reduce human error, and improve safety, thereby driving efficiency and sustainability in maritime transport. The second cluster, digital technologies, covers tools such as the Internet of Things (IoT), big data analytics, blockchain, digital twinning, and augmented and virtual reality. These innovations enable real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, and the optimization of vessel performance, leading to cost savings, reduced emissions, and improved decision-making capabilities. The third cluster, Carbon emission reduction technologies, focuses on decarbonization strategies including alternative fuels, battery-electric and hybrid propulsion, renewable energy capture, and technologies for reducing emissions via hull and propeller efficiencies, waste heat recovery, and exhaust treatment. These solutions play a vital role in meeting the industry's decarbonization targets. Finally, the fourth cluster, advanced emerging technologies, includes advanced sensors, robotics, advanced materials, human-computer interaction, human augmentation, and artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms. These cutting-edge innovations support automation and enhance ship operations, and pave the way for future advancements in sustainable shipping. This study has broad implications for industry stakeholders, including shipowners, operators, technology vendors, and policymakers. For instance, shipowners can leverage automation and digital technologies to optimize fleet management, reduce operational costs, and improve energy efficiency, enhancing sustainability. Policymakers and shore regulators can learn about future technologies and their barriers and opportunities and, thus, prepare for future actions. Overall, this study provides valuable insights for both practitioners and academics, offering a comprehensive overview of the latest developments and best practices in sustainable shipping. © 2025, Kasetsart University Faculty of International Maritime Studies. All rights reserved.

title: A Human-in-the-Loop and Explainable AI Framework for Decision Support in Battery Lifecycle Management Using Digital Battery Passports
authors: Welage, T.D.; De S. Jayasekara, K.D.; Gunawardena, U.A.D.P.; Samarathunga, L.S.W.
venue: International Conference on Human Centric Artificial Intelligence, ICHCAI 2026 - 1st International Conference
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are central to electrified transport and renewable energy systems, yet evaluating their sustainability under real operating conditions remains challenging. Conventional life cycle assessment (LCA) approaches rely on static assumptions, generic datasets, and nominal performance values, limiting their ability to support timely and contextaware decision-making across battery use, second-life deployment, remanufacturing, and end-of-life management. These limitations are particularly critical in industrial settings where human actors must make safety-, sustainability-, and valuesensitive decisions under uncertainty. This paper proposes a human-centric Artificial Intelligence (AI) framework for dynamic LCA based on a Digital Battery Passport (DBP) architecture that integrates real-time operational data into environmental assessment and decision support. The system treats the passport as a continuously evolving digital entity that ingests telemetry from the Battery Management System (BMS), interfaces with enterprise systems, and updates environmental indicators through a Digital Twin (DT) environment. AI-enabled analytics interpret degradation behavior, estimate State of Health (SoH), detect anomalies, and generate explainable recommendations for human stakeholders such as fleet operators, sustainability managers, remanufacturing engineers, and recyclers. A dynamic functional unit based on cumulative delivered energy is introduced to replace static capacity-based metrics, enabling a more realistic representation of battery performance over time. The framework supports continuous recalculation of carbon footprint and related environmental indicators, while preserving human oversight through transparent indicators, role-based access, and auditable event logging. Use cases are demonstrated for firstlife operation, second-life classification, and end-of-life pathway selection. The results show that integrating DBP, DT infrastructure, and explainable AI establishes a scalable foundation for human-centered environmental intelligence in the circular battery economy. The challenges include trust, interpretability, data governance, interoperability, SME adoption barriers, and uncertainty in battery health estimation. The proposed approach positions dynamic LCA not only as an automation tool, but as a human-in-the-loop AI system for critical sustainability decisionmaking. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Challenges and Opportunities in Secure Real-Time Digital Twin Systems for AR/VR-Enabled Smart Factories
authors: Min, Ziran; Shetty, Ram; Shekhar, Shashank; Chhokra, Ajay Dev; Kritzler, Mareike; Cui, Tao; Gupta, Ashish; Ahlgrim, Tobias; Reed, Jeffrey H.; Gokhale, Aniruddha
venue: MITOTI 2025 - Proceedings of the International Workshop on Middleware for IT/OT Integration, Part of Middleware Conference 2025
abstract: Modern high-efficiency factories face challenges in workforce training, real-time remote assistance, and safe, efficient coordination of automated guided vehicles (AGVs). However, realizing such tightly coupled human-machine collaboration introduces a number of challenges in real-time coordination, localization, network determinism, cybersecurity and cross-domain data consistency across cyber-physical layers. This paper discusses the challenges and opportunities in developing an integrated real-time digital twin control architecture that unifies augmented reality-enabled and virtual reality-enabled operator support with safety-aware orchestration of AGV fleets. Achieving centimeter-level localization and stable AR/VR overlays requires a deterministic timing architecture that combines precise clock alignment via the Precision Time Protocol (PTP) and IEEE 802.1AS with resilient data fusion across programmable logic controllers (PLCs), real-time locating systems (RTLS), and AGV telemetry. In addition, such highly networked digital twin ecosystems require end-to-end cybersecurity mechanisms that ensure confidentiality, integrity, and availability from edge devices to cloud services. Secure time synchronization, authenticated data exchange, and runtime anomaly detection become crucial to prevent cascading effects from cyber intrusions to physical operations. On the opportunity side, the convergence of edge computing, time-sensitive networking, and semantic digital twin opens new possibilities for resilient, trustworthy industrial automation system. Emerging research directions include adaptive virtual fencing, dynamic path replanning, security-aware scheduling, and AR/VR feedback loops that continuously align the physical and virtual worlds. Finally, we outline a vision for human-centric, secure, and real-time digital twin ecosystems that jointly optimize AR/VR experience quality, motion-to-photon latency, and industrial safety, thereby paving the way for resilient and data-driven factories of the future. © 2025 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: Automated Shuttle Experiments in Helmond
authors: Hofman, Patrick; Graindorge, Matthieu
venue: Lecture Notes in Mobility
abstract: The City of Helmond aims to offer new mobility services to users by operating on public roads a fleet of remotely supervised automated public transport vehicles from/ to mobility hubs/stations to Helmond’s neighbourhoods and (economic) hotspots. The first step has been to set up two pilots with automated shuttles in 2021 and 2022 (in FABULOS and LivingLAPT EU projects). These two pilots showed that some improvements of the automated shuttle service are necessary to offer a quality of service (speed, comfort, perception of (social) safety) at least equivalent to the current conventional public transport. To go beyond these projects and to achieve Helmond’s ambition, Helmond participates in specific projects (like Move2CCAM – on citizen/organization attitudes and on the impact of CCAM) and adopted a “Roadmap for automated public transport services in Helmond” in 2023. A stepwise approach has been chosen to develop and test automated public transport services in order to be able to implement and upscale them in the city. Starting with automated public transport service operations in an easy environment and then later in more complex environments. In 2024, we will start with the first step; an automated public transport service without the need of a (remote) safety driver in “Bedrijventerrein Zuid Oost Brabant” (BZOB) – an industrial area with an easy Operational Design Domain (ODD). © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Adaptive Centralized State Prediction for Multi-Agent Systems via Sliding-Window Dynamic Mode Decomposition
authors: Merzi, Alp
venue: 12th 2026 International Conference on Control, Decision and Information Technologies, CoDIT 2026
abstract: Predicting the evolution of a Multi-Agent System (MAS) is a notoriously complex task due to the non-linear coupling and local interaction protocols governing the agents. This work explores a purely data-driven adaptive predictive framework based on Dynamic Mode Decomposition with Control (DMDc) applied at the macroscopic swarm level. Rather than modeling individual agents and their localized interaction rules in a static manner, the proposed approach aggregates the entire swarm into a single global state and continuously identifies a local linear surrogate model over a sliding historical window. By doing so, the sliding-window DMDc algorithm implicitly extracts a time-varying linear surrogate model that captures the dominant cross-couplings and emergent spatiotemporal patterns of the collective motion. This paper outlines how such a linear adaptive predictive engine can be naturally embedded within a centralized Model Predictive Control (MPC) architecture, tightly coupling the evaluation horizon to the MPC prediction horizon. Finally, experimental results involving a swarm of wheeled robots successfully validate the open-loop predictive capabilities of the identified sliding-window model, showing a drastic performance increase over isolated agent identification. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Analysis of Coal Mine Safety Accident Risk Intervention Propagation Based on Agent Heterogeneity: Considering Intervention Time and Risk Preference
authors: Li, Shuang; Zhang, Yi
venue: Quality and Reliability Engineering International
abstract: Complex nonlinear relationships exist among coal mine accident risks, which provide favorable conditions for risk propagation. Insufficient identification and prevention of these risks can easily trigger chain reactions among risk factors and eventually lead to accidents. To accurately locate risk intervention nodes, this study took coal mine accident cases that occurred in China from 2020 to 2024 as the research object. By integrating association rule mining and complex network methods, a risk interaction network for coal mine accidents was constructed, and the interaction strengths among risks were quantified. Furthermore, factors such as risk concealment, personnel risk preference, risk propagation intensity, and risk intervention timing were introduced to improve the traditional SEIR risk propagation model. The entire process of coal mine accident risk propagation was then simulated. The main findings are as follows: (1) For every 5 s that risk intervention is advanced, the spread of risk propagation can be reduced by 23.7%, and the risk network can return to a stable state earlier. (2) Personnel risk preference significantly affects the peak value of risk propagation and the time required to return to a stable state, with risk-averse preferences showing a more significant effect on suppressing risk propagation. (3) The risk intervention effect of regulatory and supervision departments and coal mining enterprises is significantly better than that of ordinary operational personnel. (4) Multi-agent collaborative intervention can achieve an optimal level of risk recovery; however, collaborative intervention is not always superior to single-agent intervention. Based on these findings, it is recommended to improve the risk awareness and assessment ability of coal mine workers, optimize the allocation of risk intervention resources, and formulate differentiated and dynamic risk intervention measures. Moreover, when implementing collaborative risk intervention, key nodes and appropriate intervention intensity should be selected to avoid weakening the intervention effect due to resource dispersion. The coal mine accident risk propagation and intervention model constructed in this study deepens the understanding of risk propagation mechanisms and helps move the accident risk threshold forward. © 2026 John Wiley & Sons Ltd.

title: Recent Trends in the Public Acceptance of Autonomous Vehicles: A Review
authors: Alqahtani, Thaar
venue: Vehicles
abstract: The rapid evolution of autonomous vehicles (AVs) has ignited widespread interest in their potential to transform mobility and transportation ecosystems. However, despite significant technological advances, the acceptance of AVs by the public remains a complex and multifaceted challenge. This state-of-the-art review explores the key factors influencing AV acceptance, focusing on the intersection of artificial intelligence (AI) services, user experience, social dynamics, and regulatory landscapes across diverse global regions. By analyzing trust, perceived safety (PS), cybersecurity, and user interface design, this paper delves into the psychological and behavioral drivers that shape public perception of AVs. It also highlights the role of demographic segmentation and media influence in accelerating or hindering adoption. A comparative analysis of AV acceptance across North America, Europe, Asia, and emerging markets reveals significant regional variations, influenced by regulatory frameworks, economic conditions, and social trends. Also, this review reveals critical insights into the perceived safety associated with AV technology, including legal uncertainties and cybersecurity concerns, while emphasizing the future potential of AVs in urban environments, public transit, and autonomous logistics fleets. This review concludes by proposing strategic roadmaps and policy implications to accelerate AV adoption, offering a forward-looking perspective on how advances in technology, coupled with targeted industry and government initiatives, can shape the future of autonomous mobility. Through a comprehensive examination of current trends and challenges, this paper provides a foundation for future research and innovation aimed at enhancing public acceptance and trust in AVs. © 2025 by the author.

title: Joint Optimization of 3-D UAV Trajectory and Task Scheduling With Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Chai, Jiahui; Meng, Yun; Wang, Wei
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking
abstract: Uncrewed Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-assisted Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) has emerged as a promising paradigm for supporting computation-intensive applications of ground User Equipments (UEs). However, with the growing computational demands for UEs, it becomes crucial and extremely challenging to jointly optimize the Three-Dimensional (3D) UAV trajectory and task scheduling decision, given UAVs' limited coverage and scarce resources. To address these challenges, we develop a Multi-UAV Trajectory Optimization and Task Scheduling (MUTOTS) algorithm based on Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (MADRL). The proposed MUTOTS framework jointly optimizes multi-UAV 3D trajectories and task scheduling decisions, with the objective of maximizing total system throughput under strict flight-safety constraints. To further improve training stability and convergence, MUTOTS integrates prioritized experience replay and L2 regularization technologies. Moreover, MUTOTS can adapt to different take-off locations, and effectively guide UAVs approach near-optimal deployment locations during the execution stage. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the effectiveness, convergence and stability of the MUTOTS algorithm, and it significantly improves the system throughput compared with the other existing benchmark schemes. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning for robotic systems: A review
authors: Low, Derrick; Zhou, Ye
venue: Multiagent and Grid Systems
abstract: This review provides a comprehensive analysis of cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) approaches for robotic systems, with particular emphasis on methodological foundations, practical implementations, and emerging challenges. We first examine the evolution of distributed intelligence in robotics, tracing its development from early architectures to modern learning-based frameworks.
