title: Transformer-based human-motion forecasting coupled with safe reinforcement learning for telepresence robot co-navigation
authors: Mohamed, Heba G.; Khan, Muhammad Nasir; Naseer, Fawad; Tahir, Muhammad; Jamil, Mohsin
venue: Frontiers in Neurorobotics
abstract: Introduction: Telepresence robots (TPRs) must co-navigate with humans in constrained hospital environments, where safety depends on anticipating rather than merely reacting to human motion. Existing approaches rarely integrate short-horizon human-motion forecasting with safety-constrained control, which reduces robustness in dense corridors and ward bays. This study addresses this gap by evaluating an anticipatory, safety-aware co-navigation framework for TPRs. Methods: We developed a modular framework that couples a lightweight transformer-based forecaster that predicts multi-agent trajectories under occlusion with a safe reinforcement learning (RL) controller. The forecaster produces short-term distributions over pedestrian states that are embedded into the RL policy state and cost as risk-aware occupancy features. Safety is enforced via constrained policy optimization augmented by a run-time control barrier function (CBF) shield that filters unsafe actions. We benchmarked the approach against a social-force or dynamic window approach (DWA), an attention-based crowd-RL policy, and model predictive control (MPC) with CBF. Experiments were conducted across two hospital-like benchmarks (a crowded corridor and a four-bed ward), totaling 2,400 episodes. Outcomes included task success, collision count, minimum human–robot clearance, near-miss events (≤ 0.3 m), time-to-goal, CBF violations, and ablations removing forecasting and the CBF shield. Results: Relative to the best-performing baseline, the proposed method improved task success by 21.6% and reduced collisions by 47.3%. Median minimum human–robot clearance increased by 0.19 m, and near-miss events decreased by 38.5%. Time-to-goal was maintained within +2.7% of MPC+CBF while incurring zero CBF violations under the shield. Ablation studies showed that removing forecasting degraded success by 14.2%, whereas removing the CBF shield increased constraint breaches from 0% to 6.1% of steps. Discussion: Anticipatory perception combined with Safe-RL yields substantially safer and more reliable telepresence co-navigation in human-dense clinical layouts without sacrificing efficiency. The framework is modular, enabling alternative forecasters and safety shields. Limitations include sensitivity to forecast drift during abrupt changes in crowd flow. Future work will explore on-device adaptation, shared-autonomy overlays to incorporate operator intent, and prospective evaluations in live hospital workflows. Copyright © 2026 Mohamed, Khan, Naseer, Tahir and Jamil.

title: Multi Agent Reinforcement Learning Based Swarm Navigation
authors: Yigit, Omer; Ceylan, Suleyman Efe; Palas, Sevval Selin; Isik, Arda; Bekar, Emir; Vatansever, Berkay; Oniz, Yesim
venue: ICHORA 2026 - 8th International Congress on Human-Computer Interaction, Optimization and Robotic Applications, Proceedings
abstract: Swarm navigation in dynamic and complex environments represents a critical challenge for both decentralized control systems and dynamic obstacle avoidance. Therefore, this study presents a robust, decentralized Multi Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) model which uses a distributed-proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithm and enables the navigation of swarms collectively in a decentralized manner, using a shared policy without explicit communication among agents. In order to train each agent to learn how to transform an 8 dimensional vector into a specific action from their perspective in a two dimensional arena (thus enabling them to take action in the arena), we represent the system as a decentralized Multi Agent Markov Decision Process (MAMDP) and use a multi component reward function that provides penalty against collisions, rewards agents for successful progress toward the goals, and dampens velocity to promote stability. Our simulation results show quick convergence during training, and our agents achieve high success rates in all randomized configurations of the environment. Furthermore, our agents are able to generalize well across new, unseen obstacles; therefore, they are able to maintain their ability to navigate efficiently and safely in previously unseen obstacle configurations. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Adaptive Replay Strategies Stabilize Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Differential-Drive Robot Coordination
authors: Kyzyrkanov, Abzal; Otarbay, Zhenis; Yedilkhan, Didar; Amirgaliyev, Beibut
venue: Journal of Robotics and Control (JRC)
abstract: —Background: Coordinating differential-drive mobile robots for landmark coverage is challenging due to non-holonomic dynamics, clutter, and sparse rewards. Standard multi-agent RL pipelines often show unstable learning and inconsistent completion in this setting. Methodology: We adopt a centralized-training, decentralized-execution actor-critic without inter-agent communication. Our replay-centric design combines a tagged buffer that up-samples goal-reaching transitions and an offline replay initialization that seeds early learning with curated trajectories. Dynamic task assignment uses the Hungarian algorithm during training and evaluation, and we benchmark against uniform replay and established variants. Results: In a cluttered six-robot arena, the approach improves training stability relative to uniform replay. Convergence is faster and requires fewer updates to reach consistent success. Coverage efficiency increases as landmarks are reached earlier across runs. Collisions per episode decrease without adding communication or architectural changes. Multiseed evaluations show gains that persist with narrow confidence intervals. Train-evaluation gaps shrink on unseen maps, indicating improved generalization. Ablations attribute complementary benefits to the tagged and offline components. Performance remains competitive with prioritized and hindsight replay baselines under matched budgets. Computational overhead is small because sampling logic changes while network sizes do not. Conclusions: Focusing on replay design substantially stabilizes multi-agent learning for differential-drive coordination. The pipeline integrates cleanly with standard CTDE implementations and supports practical deployment in coverage tasks. © 2025, Department of Agribusiness, Universitas Muhammadiyah Yogyakarta. title: Multi-Agent Pickup and Delivery with external agents
authors: Bonalumi, Luca; Flammini, Benedetta; Azzalini, Davide; Amigoni, Francesco
venue: Robotics and Autonomous Systems
abstract: In a Multi-Agent Pickup and Delivery (MAPD) problem, a team of agents moving in an environment must complete pickup and delivery tasks while avoiding collisions. These tasks appear and are assigned dynamically at runtime, assuming that the environment is static, except for the movements of the agents. This paper introduces a novel MAPD formulation, where team agents must solve their MAPD problem in an environment populated by moving external agents. Team agents do not communicate nor collaborate with external agents and cannot interfere with external agents’ goals and paths, which are unknown. Thus, team agents are in charge of preventing collisions with external agents while fulfilling their pickup and delivery tasks. To address this challenge, we propose an approach where team agents build behavioral models of external agents, and then use these models to anticipate potential conflicts with external agents and plan paths accordingly. We employ two modeling approaches: (1) a probabilistic occupancy model that estimates the likelihood of each location in the environment being occupied by external agents and (2) a Markovian model that captures how external agents transition between locations in the environment. The proposed approach is evaluated under different observational assumptions for team agents, demonstrating that leveraging knowledge of external agents’ behavior reduces collision events and task completion times for team agents. © 2025 The Authors

title: Toward 6G ISAC-Enabled Low-Altitude Economy Networking: A Multi-Agent DRL Perspective
authors: Quy, Vu Khanh; Nam, Vi Hoai; Chehri, Abdellah; Nguyen, Tan N.; Tran, Duc-Tan; Le, Long Bao
venue: IEEE Network
abstract: Thanks to Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles’ (UAVs) breakthrough capabilities, the low-altitude economy concept is rapidly emerging as a new frontier for intelligent transportation, logistics, public safety, and urban aerial services. To support these applications, future networks must provide not only reliable wireless connectivity but also real-time sensing and adaptive intelligence. In this context, 6G integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) offers a promising foundation for low-altitude economy networking by enabling communication and environmental awareness within a unified framework. However, the high mobility of aerial nodes, dynamic network topology, and tightly coupled sensing-communication tasks make efficient coordination highly challenging. This article presents a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (DRL) perspective for 6G ISAC-enabled low-altitude economy networking. We discuss key challenges, outline a cooperative intelligent framework, and highlight representative application scenarios and open research issues. The goal is to show how multi-agent DRL can help enable adaptive, efficient, and safe networking for future low-altitude ecosystems. © 1986-2012 IEEE.

title: The People Behind the Robots: How Wizards Wrangle Robots in Public Deployments
authors: Pelikan, Hannah R.M.; Bu, Fanjun; Ju, Wendy
venue: Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems - Proceedings
abstract: In the Wizard-of-Oz study paradigm, human "wizards"perform not-yet-implemented system behavior, simulating, among others, how autonomous robots could interact in public to see how unwitting bystanders respond. This paper analyzes a 60-minute video recording of two wizards in a public plaza who are operating two trash-collecting robots within their line of sight. We take an ethnomethodology and conversation analysis perspective to scrutinize interactions between the wizards and the people in the plaza, focusing on critical instances where one robot gets stuck and requires collaborative intervention by the wizards. Our analysis unpacks how the wizards deal with emergent problems by pushing one robot into the other, how they manage front and backstage interactions, and how they monitor the location of each other's robots. We discuss how scrutinizing the work of wizards can inform explorative Wizard-of-Oz paradigms, the design of multi-agent robot systems, and the operation of urban robots from a distance. © 2025 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: Recent breakthroughs in AI-driven robotics: advancements, challenges, and future directions: a systematic literature review
authors: Hasnain, Muhammad; Rehman, Fazal Ur; Hu, Yu-Chen; Wu, Chang-Ming; Shakoor, Saira
venue: International Journal of Intelligent Robotics and Applications
abstract: With their revolutionary applications and potential for innovation across a wide range of industries, artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics are expected to continue influencing society and business. This study aimed to review recent literature published between 2018 and 2026 in the areas of AI and Robotics. The “Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses” (PRISMA) guidelines are used to conduct the research in the area of AI and robotics. The search strategy resulted in the selection of 119 studies based on the exclusion and inclusion criteria. The literature review revealed that robotics and AI are widely used across manufacturing, logistics, agriculture, e-commerce, finance, and entertainment to automate tedious tasks, increase production, and improve efficiency. While autonomous drones are utilized for tasks such as transportation, inspection, and surveillance, collaborative robots operate alongside humans in production contexts. Despite significant improvements, issues with robots and AI include data security and privacy, resilience against hostile attacks, the interpretability of AI models, and public acceptance of automation. Stakeholder participation, teamwork, and interdisciplinary research are necessary to address these issues. Some future research directions in AI and robotics include explanatory AI, ethical AI, human-centered design, multi-agent systems, bioinspired robotics, sustainable and resilient AI, and multi-agent systems. Future advancements in these areas could improve the capabilities, safety, and societal effects of intelligent systems. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.

title: An Accelerated Algorithm for Minimum-Time Multi-Agent Motion Planning
authors: Nadi, Elahe; Babazadeh, Maryam
venue: Iranian Conference on Electrical Engineering, ICEE
abstract: This paper presents a distributed computational framework for minimum-time multi-agent motion planning in complex environments with static obstacles. Traditional motion planning methods face significant computational challenges in multi-agent scenarios, requiring initial guesses close to optimal solutions and suffering from inefficiency at scale. The proposed approach integrates the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) with the Convex Feasible Set (CFS) algorithm to address these limitations. The framework decomposes the overall problem into independent subproblems for agent dynamics and collision avoidance, facilitating parallel computation and efficient coordination among agents. The CFS algorithm approximates non-convex obstacle constraints as convex sets, transforming computationally challenging problems into tractable quadratic subproblems. Extensive simulations in complex obstacle environments demonstrate that our ADMM-CFS framework achieves remarkable improvements, including 93% reduction in computation time, superior path quality, and enhanced convergence compared to Interior Point Method (IPM). The method maintains safety constraints while producing smooth, coordinated paths for multiple agents, making it suitable for real-time applications in autonomous systems and multi-robot coordination. © 2026 IEEE.

title: A Push-Pull Elastic Flow Framework for UAS Corridor Generation in Urban Low-Altitude Airspace
authors: Yuan, Yutong; Yan, Hui; Wang, Lizhen; He, Ping; Fu, Yanghui
venue: International Conference on Big Data and Information Analytics, BigDIA
abstract: Air corridors serve as the core spatial infrastructure enabling Uncrewed Aircraft System (UAS)-based Internet of Things (IoT) networks for continuous urban sensing and logistics. Planning these corridors requires processing massive high-resolution topographic data to guarantee collision-free transit. While fluid flow via Laplace Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) provides a parallel, physics-driven routing approach over such spatial big data, existing PDE-based methods suffer from severe flow stagnation in dense urban canyons. This fundamentally bottlenecks the spatial traffic capacity and the topological connectivity of aerial IoT fleets. To address this limitation, we propose a Push-Pull Moat-Driven Elastic Flow Framework. In the Push phase, a virtual moat mechanism relaxes obstacle boundaries, guiding the PDE solver to generate high-density flow within narrow urban gaps. In the Pull phase, an S3 (Snap-Smooth-Snap) kinematic repair matrix combined with an adaptive topological veto mechanism elastically refines trajectories. Ablation experiments on high-resolution urban datasets verify that our framework efficiently processes complex spatial structures, greatly eliminating topological violations and significantly improving the yield of valid corridors. Our method provides a highly parallel, robust, and collision-free physical routing foundation for massive UAS-IoT operations in metropolitan environments. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Real-time cooperative target tracking in cluttered environments using multiple drone swarms with adaptive fuzzy emotional learning
authors: Page, Lucas William; Tran, Vu Phi; Nguyen, Duy Luan
venue: Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: This paper presents a real-time adaptive trajectory prediction framework for cooperative unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms engaged in dynamic target tracking within cluttered environments. The proposed system introduces a novel artificial intelligence (AI)-based control architecture combining fuzzy inference, neuro-emotional learning, and distributed multi-agent coordination. At the core of the approach is a Bidirectional Fuzzy Brain Emotional Learning Prediction (BFBEL-P) model, which integrates fuzzy logic and an online adaptive neural structure to enable trajectory forecasting without pre-training or prior knowledge of the environment. From an engineering perspective, this AI model is deployed in UAV swarm navigation, where robust decision-making, predictive coordination, and obstacle avoidance are essential for target interception missions. In contrast to conventional prediction methods, such as curve fitting, nonlinear model predictive control (MPC), and deep learning-based Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, the BFBEL-P framework offers fast convergence, low computational cost, and high adaptability. The system incorporates multi-threaded data fusion across the swarm to achieve consensus-driven predictions and maintain situational awareness, even under sensor failures or occlusions. Simulation results show that BFBEL-P improves short-term prediction accuracy by 82.2%, reduces prediction time by 15%, and achieves a 100% tracking success rate across benchmark scenarios. These results establish BFBEL-P as a reliable AI technique for distributed control in real-world UAV swarm applications, offering a promising tool for search-and-rescue, surveillance, and defense operations. © 2025 The Authors

title: Comparative Evaluation of IoT-Based Telematics Platforms for Smart Fleet Management
authors: Zgambo, Irwin K.; Staroverova, Natalia
venue: Proceedings - 2026 International Russian Smart Industry Conference, SmartIndustryCon 2026
abstract: The rapid digitalization of the transportation sector has accelerated the integration of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies in fleet monitoring, safety management, and operational optimization. This paper presents a comprehensive comparative evaluation of IoT-based telematics platforms used in transportation systems management, focusing on international solutions (e.g., Samsara) and Russian platforms (Omnicomm, SCOUT, GLONASSsoft, Wialon, and Monitoring Avto). A multi-criteria assessment methodology is applied, encompassing functional decomposition, performance indicators, API integration capabilities, cybersecurity considerations, and total cost of ownership (TCO). A practical case study involving the deployment of Omnicomm Online in a large retail fleet ("Verny") validates the analytical framework. Furthermore, the paper details the development and implementation of a proactive, data-driven maintenance system leveraging API integration, demonstrating a practical pathway to enhance operational resilience. Results indicate that while international platforms excel in AI-driven analytics and ecosystem integration, Russian platforms offer competitive advantages in fuel monitoring accuracy, regulatory compliance, and cost efficiency. The study identifies key technological gaps and proposes actionable directions for enhancing domestic telematics platforms within smart transportation systems. These findings are relevant for engineers, system integrators, logistics operators, and policymakers involved in intelligent transport solutions. © 2026 IEEE.

title: A Learning-Based Estimation and Fault-Tolerant Control Scheme for Uncertain Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Liu, Jialu; Dong, Jiuxiang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: The learning-based cooperative control problem is investigated for the heterogeneous multi-agent system affected by unknown system uncertainties, actuator faults, and external disturbances. A learning-based estimation scheme is proposed to simultaneously identify unknown uncertainties, actuator faults, and disturbances. Exponential convergence of estimation errors is guaranteed by the designed learning laws without requiring persistent excitation. Based on the time-varying system matrix estimation, a constrained matrix observer is developed to satisfy specified matrix inequalities, thereby guaranteeing the stability of the closed-loop system. Furthermore, a distributed cooperative controller is designed for virtual agents to achieve synchronization with the leader while preventing fault propagation. Subsequently, a fault-tolerant controller is constructed for the actual heterogeneous agents, ensuring convergence between the faulty agents and the leader. Theoretical results are validated through simulations of connected vehicle platoons incorporating realistic vehicle dynamics and fault scenarios. Finally, the superiority of the proposed method regarding transient performance and control efficiency is highlighted through comparisons with existing adaptive learning techniques. Note to Practitioners - This study is motivated by the practical challenge of maintaining reliable and precise cooperative control in multi-agent systems, such as autonomous vehicle platoons or robotic teams, when agents experience real-world unknown internal dynamics, partial actuator failures, and external disturbances. To address this, this paper proposes a learning-based scheme that can simultaneously identify and compensate for these combined uncertainties in real time. A key advantage is that the method ensures rapid and stable estimation without relying on hard-to-maintain persistent excitation signals. Based on these estimates, a fault-tolerant cooperative controller is designed to synchronize all agents with a leader while actively containing potential faults and preventing them from spreading through the network. The framework has been validated in simulations of connected vehicle platoons using high-fidelity vehicle models and realistic fault scenarios. Results show improved transient response and control efficiency compared to existing adaptive methods, making it suitable for applications where safety and robustness are critical. Future work could focus on further reducing computational load and testing the strategy in hardware-in-the-loop environments. © 2004-2012 IEEE.

title: Teleoperating Mobile Robots Via Vda 5050 - A First Middleware Evaluation Within Open Industrial Networks
authors: Wagner, Niklas A.; Toenning, Lars; Lunsch, Dennis; Jost, Jana; Wietfeld, Christian; Detzner, Peter
venue: IEEE International Workshop on Factory Communication Systems - Proceedings, WFCS
abstract: Teleoperation is a practical fallback for mobile robots in intralogistics when rare but safety- and throughputcritical edge cases exceed autonomous capabilities. While Fleet Management Systems (FMSs) increasingly rely on vendor-neutral interfaces such as VDA 5050 to coordinate heterogeneous robots, teleoperation is not natively represented in the standard and is typically implemented as an ad hoc, robot-specific add-on. This paper closes this gap by proposing a VDA 5050 teleoperation extension that enables human-in-the-loop control as part of the same interface used for autonomous task and route coordination. To facilitate reproducible evaluation, we further contribute a configurable VDA 5050 traffic generator that reproduces realistic message patterns for middleware-based FMS communication. Employing the Open Radio Access Network (Open RAN) concept, cellular 5G and future 6G networks can be flexibly deployed in industrial environments to provide reliable, low-latency wireless connectivity for mobile robot teleoperation. Using an end-to-end stack consisting of VDA 5050 messaging, middleware transport, and Open RAN wireless link, we evaluate latency and communication overhead to characterize the performance implications of standardized teleoperation integration. © 2026 IEEE.

title: VissimRL: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Traffic Signal Control Based on Vissim
authors: Chang, Hsiao-Chuan; Huang, Sheng-You; Chen, Yen-Chi; Wu, I-Chen
venue: IEEE Intelligent Vehicles Symposium, Proceedings
abstract: Traffic congestion remains a major challenge for urban transportation, leading to significant economic and environmental impacts. Traffic Signal Control (TSC) is one of the key measures to mitigate congestion, and recent studies have increasingly applied Reinforcement Learning (RL) for its adaptive capabilities. With respect to SUMO and CityFlow, the simulator Vissim offers high-fidelity driver behavior modeling and wide industrial adoption but remains underutilized in RL research due to its complex interface and lack of standardized frameworks. To address this gap, this paper proposes VissimRL, a modular RL framework for TSC that encapsulates Vissim's COM interface through a high-level Python API, offering standardized environments for both single- and multi-agent training. Experiments show that VissimRL significantly reduces development effort while maintaining runtime efficiency, and supports consistent improvements in traffic performance during training, as well as emergent coordination in multi-agent control. Overall, VissimRL demonstrates the feasibility of applying RL in high-fidelity simulations and serves as a bridge between academic research and practical applications in intelligent traffic signal control. The implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/CGI-LAB/VissimRL. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Navigation safety optimization of mobile autonomous robots using deep reinforcement learning, long short-term memory, and artificial immune system
authors: de Jesús Plasencia-Salgueiro, Armando
venue: Modeling, Dynamics and Control approaches for Modern Robotics
abstract: Current mobile robots face challenges in executing certain tasks that affect the safety of path navigation. To address issues such as autonomous learning, slow path planning convergence, and the lack of smoothness in planned routes, deep reinforcement learning can be employed. This approach enables robots to understand their surroundings and extract features, allowing them to adapt to the environment through state-action functions. One of the solutions reflected by the specialized literature is the complementation of different algorithms in the form of fusion or hybridity in one hierarchical structure for a safety framework. Still, it is not clear which solution is the best from the energy-safety trade-off point of view. For the solution of this problem in the chapter, studying different existing frameworks, taking the reference of the immunological system, conclude that like this system, our framework should be structured in three levels, a low level corresponding to the immunological innate system or primary immune stage, a middle level corresponding to immunological adapting system or secondary immune response, and a high level corresponding to immunological collective cell migration. For each level, taking the reference of cyber-physical system conception, and after the demonstration of the feasibility of modeling each stage using deep reinforcement learning algorithms, the corresponding technical solution model was associated with each level. For the primary stage, the soft actor-critic algorithm was selected, for the secondary stage, the soft actor-critic-long short-term memory hybrid algorithm, and for the high level, the multiagent deep reinforcement learning. This framework conception outperforms the rest of the exposed safety frameworks because the soft actor-critic algorithm has a lower computational load than the hybrid, so can be used in the static obstacle environment during the majority time of trajectory and use the hybrid long short-term memory in dynamics environment in short time of trajectory and deep reinforcement learning in a hierarchy safety framework incorporate the multi-agent deep reinforcement learning. Combining the response results of each level, the path planning performance of autonomous robots is improved. All these conceptions are probed in the rest of the chapter. Finally, using the MetaDrive, “an Open-source Driving Simulator for AI and Autonomy Research simulation platform,” the simulation environment is established, and the performance indices of traditional path planning and the suggested techniques may be compared. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

title: LNS2+RL: Combining Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Large Neighborhood Search in Multi-Agent Path Finding
authors: Wang, Yutong; Duhan, Tanishq; Li, Jiaoyang; Sartoretti, Guillaume
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) is a critical component of logistics and warehouse management, which focuses on planning collision-free paths for a team of robots in a known environment. Recent work introduced a novel MAPF approach, LNS2, which proposed to repair a quickly obtained set of infeasible paths via iterative replanning, by relying on a fast, yet lower-quality, prioritized planning (PP) algorithm. At the same time, there has been a recent push for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) based MAPF algorithms, which exhibit improved cooperation over such PP algorithms, although inevitably remaining slower. In this paper, we introduce a new MAPF algorithm, LNS2+RL, which combines the distinct yet complementary characteristics of LNS2 and MARL to effectively balance their individual limitations and get the best from both worlds. During early iterations, LNS2+RL relies on MARL for low-level replanning, which we show eliminates collisions much more than a PP algorithm. There, our MARL-based planner allows agents to reason about past and future information to gradually learn cooperative decision-making through a finely designed curriculum learning. At later stages of planning, LNS2+RL adaptively switches to PP algorithm to quickly resolve the remaining collisions, naturally trading off solution quality (number of collisions in the solution) and computational efficiency. Our comprehensive experiments on high-agent-density tasks across various team sizes, world sizes, and map structures consistently demonstrate the superior performance of LNS2+RL compared to many MAPF algorithms, including LNS2, LaCAM, EECBS, and SCRIMP. In maps with complex structures, the advantages of LNS2+RL are particularly pronounced, with LNS2+RL achieving a success rate of over 50% in nearly half of the tested tasks, while that of LaCAM, EECBS and SCRIMP falls to 0%. Copyright © 2025, Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (www.aaai.org). All rights reserved.

title: A Hierarchical Framework and Marginal Return Optimization for Dynamic Task Allocation in Heterogeneous UAV Networks
authors: Guo, Anxin; Zhang, Zhenxing; Wu, Ao; Li, Qi; Li, Leyan; Yang, Rennong
venue: Sensors
abstract: The coordination of heterogeneous Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) for complex, multi-stage tasks presents a significant challenge in robotics and autonomous systems. Traditional linear models often fail to capture the emergent synergistic effects and dynamic nature of multi-agent collaboration. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel hierarchical framework based on a Mission Chain (MC) concept. We systematically define and model key elements of multi-agent collaboration, including Mission Chains (MCs), Execution Paths (EPs), Task Networks (TNs), and Solution Spaces (SSs), creating an integrated theoretical structure. Based on this framework, we formulate the problem as a Sensor–Effector–Target Assignment challenge and propose a Marginal Return-Based Heuristic Algorithm (MRBHA) for efficient dynamic task allocation. Simulations demonstrate that our proposed MRBHA achieves a substantially higher total expected mission value—outperforming standard greedy and random assignment strategies by 14% and 77%, respectively. This validates the framework’s ability to effectively capitalize on synergistic opportunities within the UAV network. The proposed system provides a robust and scalable solution for managing complex missions in dynamic environments, with potential applications in search-and-rescue, environmental monitoring, and intelligent logistics. © 2025 by the authors.

title: Event-Driven Self-Organized Fencing Control for Second-Order Multi-Agent Systems With an Unknown Time-Varying Target
authors: Zhang, Enhua; Wang, Jian; Liu, Xinran; Liang, Xiaofeng
venue: IEEE Control Systems Letters
abstract: This letter investigates the event-triggered self-organized fencing control problem for second-order multi-agent systems subject to external disturbances and an unknown time-varying target. Unlike prescribed fencing configurations, a self-organized formation is generated through potential-field regulation rather than prescribed relative positions. Based on the velocity compensation function, a regulation potential function is constructed to drive the agents towards the target while the collision and obstacle avoidance potentials are further incorporated to guarantee the local safety. A dynamic controller is then developed where a smooth reinforcement learning echo state network (RL-ESN) compensation function is introduced to attenuate bounded disturbances. Furthermore, an event-driven mechanism with a safety-regulation function is designed to guarantee the system safety and reduce the unnecessary data transmission between the controller and actuators. The rigorous theoretical analysis illustrates that the regulation and tracking error signals are uniformly ultimately bounded. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. © 2017 IEEE.

title: Dynamic Multi-Agent Drone Path Planning Using Conflict-Based Search with YOLOv12
authors: Tiwari, Smriti; Chakraborty, Nilotpal; Khatua, Manas
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence, ICETCI 2026
abstract: The growing deployment of autonomous unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in applications such as surveillance, logistics, and disaster response necessitates robust multi-agent navigation in dynamic environments. A critical challenge in such systems is ensuring collision-free path planning while adapting to unforeseen obstacles. This paper proposes a vision-integrated multi-agent path planning framework that combines Conflict-Based Search (CBS) with real-time object detection using YOLOv12, an attention-enhanced deep learning model. Initially, optimal paths are computed using A∗ and refined through CBS to resolve inter-agent conflicts. During execution, onboard vision systems detect dynamic obstacles using YOLOv12, which are incorporated into the environment model, triggering real-time replanning. The proposed approach is validated in a 3D simulation environment. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework achieves zero collision instances, maintains near-optimal path lengths (19, 19, 14 steps for three drones), and introduces only 0.005 seconds of additional computation time compared to standard CBS, while successfully adapting to dynamically appearing obstacles. © 2026 IEEE.

title: An Agent-Based Framework for Performance Evaluation and Tradeoff Analysis of Highway Work Zone Policies
authors: Tao, Qiugang; Gong, Jinrui; Zhang, Xujie; Mei, Zhenyu; Xu, Xiaoyong; Zhang, Zhihua
venue: IEEE Open Journal of Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: Amidst global efforts to mitigate climate change, managing the disruptive impact of highway work zones requires intelligent solutions. Traditional assessment methods often lack the capability to model the complex, dynamic interactions between traffic flow and temporary control policies, while struggling to balance computational efficiency with system-level dynamic assessment in large-scale networks. To address this gap, this paper designs, implements, and validates a Multiagent System based decision support framework. In this framework, individual vehicles and infrastructure elements are modeled as autonomous agents that interact to simulate emergent, system-level traffic dynamics. By modeling the system from the bottom up, this mesoscopic simulation approach enables a system-level quantification of the relative effectiveness of various control policies in reducing CO 2 emissions across different work zone scenarios. Using the Hangzhou Ring Expressway as a case study, the study demonstrates the utility of the framework as a virtual testbed. The results of the framework not only reveal the non-linear sensitivity of emissions to policy parameters but, more critically, the multi-objective tradeoff analysis uncovers non-intuitive, Pareto-optimal strategies. For instance, the analysis identifies scenarios where a well-configured two-lane closure can outperform a suboptimal one-lane closure in both traffic efficiency and environmental impact. The findings confirm that the proposed framework is a powerful and extensible tool for transportation authorities to design, test, and deploy more efficient and sustainable work zone management strategies in the era of Intelligent Transportation Systems. © 2020 IEEE.

title: Development of a UAV-based Disaster Evacuation Support System
authors: Taga, Shohei; Sekiguchi, Yuta; Kato, Toshiyasu; Takimoto, Munehiro; Kambayashi, Yasushi
venue: Proceedings of the 18th ACM International Conference on PErvasive Technologies Related to Assistive Environments, PETRA 2025
abstract: We have developed a system that supports evacuation before and after disasters using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). We focus on addressing evacuations in mountainous areas. Mountainous areas are prone to landslides caused by heavy rain. It is crucial for people there to evacuate before such disasters occur. It is also important to make them evacuate after earthquakes occur. In order to address these problems, we have proposed an evacuation support system that uses two types of UAVs. One type of UAVs, which we call monitoring UAVs, conducts road condition checks and collects information about affected individuals, while another type of UAVs, which we call guiding UAVs, guides the evacuees. The guided route is not simply the shortest path. The UAV selects the most suitable route based on factors such as route safety and congestion levels. The monitoring UAV that grasps the situation informs the guiding UAVs of the route status as needed, allowing the guiding UAVs to dynamically adjust the evacuation route. Both UAVs share information by exchanging messages by way of a control server through ad hoc communication through an opportunistic network. We have developed a series of simulators to demonstrate the effectiveness of our system. In the previous work, the simulator setting was not realistic enough. We have improved our simulator, and the current one reflects the reality well, and gives us many insights. © 2025 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: Congestion-Aware Multi-Agent Path Planning for Pick-Up and Delivery Tasks
authors: Asadi, Mehrdad; Nowé, Ann; Ghofrani, Javad
venue: GECCO 2025 - Proceedings of the 2025 Genetic and Evolutionary Computation Conference
abstract: Mobile robotic systems play a pivotal role in logistics, particularly in warehouse operations, where efficient and collision-free navigation is essential for completing tasks. However, managing a large number of robots often leads to congestion, causing delays and adversely affecting system scalability. This paper proposes a novel online algorithm for solving the Multi-Agent Pickup and Delivery (MAPD) problem. The algorithm addresses local collision detection and global congestion avoidance by integrating a congestion prediction model to enhance process efficiency. A deep neural network is employed to approximate congestion predictions independently of the number of agents, reducing computational complexity. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly improves system throughput and scalability, with a notable average doubling of throughput in specific scenarios. The findings provide a foundation for advanced congestion management strategies in multi-agent systems, paving the way for efficient and scalable deployment in logistics and beyond. © 2025 Copyright is held by the owner/author(s). Publication rights licensed to ACM.

title: Guarded Swarms: Building Trusted Autonomy Through Digital Intelligence and Physical Safeguards †
authors: Borghoff, Uwe M.; Bottoni, Paolo; Pareschi, Remo
venue: Future Internet
abstract: Autonomous UAV/UGV swarms increasingly operate in contested environments where purely digital control architectures are vulnerable to cyber compromise, communication denial, and timing faults. This paper presents Guarded Swarms, a hybrid framework that combines digital coordination with hardware-level analog safety enforcement. The architecture builds on Topic-Based Communication Space Petri Nets (TB-CSPN) for structured multi-agent coordination, extending this digital foundation with independent analog guard channels—thrust clamps, attitude limiters, proximity sensors, and emergency stops—that operate in parallel at the actuator interface. Each channel can unilaterally veto unsafe commands within microseconds, independently of software state. The digital–analog interface is formalized via timing contracts that specify sensor-consistency windows and actuation latency bounds. A two-robot case study demonstrates token-based arbitration at the digital level and OR-style inhibition at the analog level. The framework ensures local safety deterministically while maintaining global coordination as a best-effort property. This paper presents an architectural contribution establishing design principles and interface contracts. Empirical validation remains future work. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Safe Fuzzy-CBF: A Monitoring Approach for Deep Reinforcement Learning Navigation Agents
authors: Yang, Min; Liu, Guanjun; Zhou, Ziyuan; Liu, Gaiyun
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: In safety-critical reinforcement learning tasks such as robot navigation, autonomous driving, and industrial control, real-time monitoring of agent behavior is paramount to prevent unsafe actions from compromising system reliability. We introduce Safe Fuzzy Control Barrier Functions (Safe Fuzzy-CBF), a monitoring framework that continuously evaluates agent risk using a smooth control barrier function learned from data via Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy rules, rather than relying on a predefined model-based barrier. In the offline phase, we extract fuzzy rules from trajectory data and construct a continuously differentiable barrier that unifies state, action, and cost into a single risk metric. During online execution, we estimate the barrier's time derivative using finite differences, apply Lipschitz-based corrections, and when the barrier condition is violated, we solve a small quadratic program in the normalized control space to compute a safe corrective action. Evaluated on three Safety-Gymnasium navigation tasks and the MetaDrive autonomous driving environment, our framework detects emerging safety violations in real time and enforces runtime safety without degrading the underlying RL policy's performance, achieving up to an 86.8% reduction in accumulated cost. Note to Practitioners - Real-world deployment of reinforcement learning controllers is challenged by model inaccuracies and high human monitoring costs, especially in safety-sensitive scenarios such as robotic navigation and autonomous driving. To this end, we propose an end-to-end, online differentiable safety fuzzy-CBF monitoring module that can be embedded in any reinforcement learning system. The module extracts a small number of trajectories offline before training, automatically generates differentiable fuzzy control barrier functions, evaluates barriers in real time during training or inference, and solves a quadratic program to generate safe corrective actions on potentially dangerous actions to generate safe actions to replace the original decisions. Experimental results show that the safety fuzzy-CBF monitoring module can reduce the cumulative cost of navigation tasks without degrading the performance of the original policy of the original policy, providing engineers with a real-time safety assurance method. Although our method has demonstrated strong safety monitoring performance in single-agent scenarios with unknown dynamics, to extend it to multi-agent applications it is necessary to combine decentralized barrier function design with graph neural networks to cope with complex interactions between agents and real-time scalability. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Dynamic Communication and Global Guidance for Multi-Agent Path Finding
authors: Ma, Yinghao; Lu, Xiguang; Ning, Nianwen; Zhu, Panpan; Shi, Lei; Li, Wei; Trung, Nguyen Huu; Zhou, Yi
venue: Proceedings - 2026 International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Intelligent Transportation Systems, RAITS 2026
abstract: Autonomous mobile robots are deployed in transport and logistics for large-scale handling and distribution tasks. However, real-time collaboration in such dynamic settings faces two primary challenges: effective collision avoidance and efficient communication. To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework, Dynamic Communication with Global Guidance for Multi-Agent Path Finding (DCGGM), which integrates a Latent Representation Dynamic Communication (LRDC) module reducing redundant messaging and a early waiting policy to anticipate conflicts. It significantly enhances multi-agent cooperation without compromising real-time performance. Experimental results show that DCGGM matches the performance of coupled centralized expert algorithms. Ablation studies and comparisons across various agent densities confirm the effectiveness of our communication mechanism. The framework generalizes to potential problem instances and surpasses state-of-the-art learningbased approaches in success rate, path efficiency, and collision minimization. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Enterprise Fire Safety System Risk Assessment Based on Multi-Agent Modeling within a Complex Adaptive Systems Framework
authors: Song, Zhenjun; Shan, Wei; Huang, Xintao; Zhang, Yichi
venue: IEEE International Conference on Control and Automation, ICCA
abstract: Enterprise fire safety is shaped by nonlinear interactions among leadership, management, workers, facilities, and the environment, which cannot be adequately captured by traditional static assessment methods. Existing practices mainly rely on qualitative inspections and static scoring models, providing only snapshot evaluations and overlooking the microlevel mechanisms through which multiple factors accumulate into systemic fire risk. This paper develops a fire complex adaptive system agent-based model (FCAS-ABM), in which the five subsystems are represented as heterogeneous agents characterized by stochastic evolution, nonlinear feedback, and veto thresholds. Based on the model, a composite system safety index incorporating dynamic smoothing, grading, and trendoriented early warning is constructed. The model is calibrated using expert knowledge and engineering data and implemented in a five-year discrete-time simulation to examine baseline dynamics and alternative governance strategies. Baseline simulations and scenario analyses reveal that the FCAS-ABM provides a quantitative and interpretable tool for dynamic enterprise fire-risk assessment, proactive early warning, and governance strategy optimization. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Agentic AI, AI Agents, and Quantum AI Agents
authors: Islam, Sardar M. N.; Saini, Hemant Kumar; Gupta, Meenu; Jain, Rachna
venue: Agentic AI, AI Agents, and Quantum AI Agents
abstract: Agentic AI, AI Agents, and Quantum AI Agents examines the evolution of intelligent systems from rule-based systems to self-reliant systems with adaptive capabilities to make decisions in complicated environments. This book first introduces agent architectures, learning, planning, and multi-agent systems. It then introduces practical information, modern technologies, and deployment mechanisms of AI agents and stresses the importance of safety, ethics, and explainability. Readers will become acquainted with the structure, training, implementation, and control of smart agents in today’s artificial intelligence environments and with the application of quantum computing to improve agent intelligence and the ability to make decisions. This book is intended for researchers, postgraduate students, AI practitioners, software engineers, and technology specialists interested in obtaining a detailed overview of autonomous AI systems and their integration with future quantum technologies. This book is also relevant for educators, innovators, and policymakers interested in the development of responsible AI, its governance, and the profound impact of smart and quantum-enhanced agents throughout the industry and society. KEY FEATURES An in-depth coverage of agentic AI, AI agents, multi.agent systems, and quantum AI agents Balanced theory, implementation, best practices, and real-world examples Specific attention given to secure, ethical, explainable, and responsible autonomous AI systems Extensive discussion on quantum machine learning, quantum decision systems, and quantum.enabled systems with applications in health, smart city, logistics, finance, and security. © 2027 selection and editorial matter, Sardar M. N. Islam, Hemant Kumar Saini, Meenu Gupta, and Rachna Jain; individual chapters, the contributors.

title: Demystifying the Real-World Applications of Agentic AI
authors: Nagarajan, S.; Natarajan, Gnanasankaran; Elango, Elakkiya; Sundaravadivazhagan, B.
venue: Agentic Artificial Intelligence: Engineering AI Agents for Autonomous AI Systems
abstract: The term Agentic AI describes an AI system that is capable of functioning autonomously to achieve specific objectives, often with minimal help from humans. These systems display initiatives, flexibility, and decision-making skills that enable them to act in complex, dynamic real-world conditions. Accelerated development of Agentic AI is transforming many fields, such as financial advice systems, smart manufacturing, autonomous mobility, and personal healthcare. Such intelligent agents emphasize methods of evolving from theoretical concepts to practical applications; this chapter explores many real-world uses of agentic AI. Agentic AI is used to adapt treatment protocols in healthcare, follow patient health in real time, and assist in initial diagnoses. Such systems automatically handle route adaptation in fleet synchronization, barrier navigation and logistics, and autonomous vehicles. Algorithmic trading, fraud detection, and personal financial planning are all made possible by agents in the financial industry. AI-driven assistants also provide dynamic, context-aware participation in customer support and education, adapting to user preferences and behavior. Enabling technologies such as large language models, sensor-based integration, and reinforcement learning, which this chapter also includes, propel agentic behavior. The moral and safety effects of implementing autonomous agents in society are also investigated, including issues of control, accountability, and transparency. This chapter provides a deep understanding of how Agentic AI is not only changing specific industries but also the broader area of human-AI cooperation. © 2026 Walter de Gruyter GmbH, Genthiner Straße 13, 10785 Berlin, Germany.

title: Advancing Mine Detection Through Multi-Agent Systems: Collaborative Robotics for Enhanced Efficiency and Safety
authors: Alsalem, Hesham I.; Khazalah, Fayez S.; Mansour, Ayman M.
venue: WSEAS Transactions on Systems
abstract: This study investigates how to apply a multi-agent system (MAS)-based process on robotic platforms to mine detection, especially improving collaboration/communication between agents. Agents can communicate and collaborate by sharing sensor data relevant to the task, sharing requests for tasks to be acted on by agents, applying standard protocols, wireless communications, message passing, etc. Using a publish-subscribe architecture will enable the agents not to force all agents to receive all information and use decentralized decision-making to promote adaptable behavior. In addition, through adaptive communications protocols, a better means of data sharing, adaptations of behavior, and higher-order activities will be simpler. Finally, a shared state of relevant communication will allow collaborative robotic agents in an MAS to have higher accuracy and efficiency to clear minefields while improving safety and effectiveness.
